# Engine C3: varying conditions and the live-edit layer, with XC-288's change log — Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

>
> Execution: subagent-driven, a fresh implementer and reviewer per task, then a whole-branch review on the most capable model, as C2b was; the full mutation sweep dispatched on the branch before the merge (Task 20, Step 5). **Every commit** ends with the session's attribution lines (Global Constraints).

**Goal:** A task may draw settings at random each trial: from a default the task declares, which a block type may
replace, or from a condition's own range. Each draw comes from distributions the PI chose: uniform, weighted, truncated
normal, a prepared list, and the non-aging wait, whose tail is drawn again. Draws come from a generator keyed by run
seed, trial and setting; each drawn setting declares what a repeat takes, `same` or `fresh`, and a drummed repeat
follows it too. `wlx run` draws a fresh seed when given none. A block may make its conditions from factors, and may
play a designed order: sequence-balanced de Bruijn cycles, or priming by chance or by runs, with no repeat or "again at
once". A person's value now replaces a draw too. A person may hand a setting back, change a drawn range live, and
revert to an earlier moment. Each setting's card says where its value comes from and which conditions set or draw it,
and a staged change names the conditions it will override. Trials a live change eased are kept out of moving up and
still count toward moving back. Settings no animal can get right are refused in the file, at a run's start and live,
a live change judged also against the values the trials waiting to come back keep. The record says what was drawn and
from where, what a person held, what eased a trial, each designed trial's planned place, and what varied in each
block. `parameter_changes.jsonl` grows into one change log of every kind, which resume reads, the clears and switches
written to it as well as to `controls.jsonl`. wl-preproc is told first.

**Architecture:** `wl_xcon/task.py` gains the vocabulary: the five distributions, `Factorial`, the two designed
orders, `Task.draws`, `Block.draws`, `Block.factorial`; all fields have defaults, so no hash moves and `FORMAT` stays 1.
A new pure module, `wl_xcon/variation.py`, holds the arithmetic every consumer shares, entered in
`tools/mutation_gate.RETURNS`:
- keyed draws and their bounds, and a draw's extremes;
- the non-aging hazard and realized mean;
- where a block's draws come from;
- factorial expansion and condition names;
- de Bruijn sequences;
- live numbers, the record's form of a draw, its words, which settings are directions, and whether a value is easier.

`check.py` refuses what cannot be drawn, factorial and designed-order faults, and the three impossible combinations;
`check.impossible` is shared by load, a run's start and a live change. `scheduler.py` plays the designed orders,
records `designed` shortfalls, names the trials a waiting repeat holds, and leaves eased trials out of a block's rule
window. `taskd.py` changes in these places:
- the trial loop draws between trials in §17.1's order, keeps `same` values, and computes `eased`;
- one generic applier (`_apply_staged`) writes every kind of change row, with change ids per act;
- three new off-list acts: hand back, range, revert;
- the live refusal, one line in `_command`, judging the run's blocks and the trials waiting to come back;
- the record's new fields;
- telemetry schema 19's sources, staged kinds and moments.

`record.py` writes the change log's rows (`SessionRecord.change`) and the trial line's four fields. `resume.py` reads
every kind. `link.py` adds three commands and schema 19, and `serve.py` their page bodies. `preflight.py` counts a drawn
setting as given, widens draws past their range and refuses an impossible start; `cli.py` draws a fresh seed. `web.py`
shows sources, hand back, ranges and revert. `review.py` shows draws, generated conditions, designed orders and the
wait's hazard.

**Tech Stack:** Python 3.11-3.13; dataclasses; the standard library's `hashlib`, `statistics.NormalDist`, `random`
and `math`; pytest; Playwright for the page's browser tests (as `tests/test_page_browser.py` runs today). **No new
dependency.**

**Spec:** `../specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md` (approved by the PI 2026-10-30, section by section; every answer
quoted in `.superpowers/c3-prep/answers.md`); the engine spec `../specs/2026-10-07-engine-design.md` §6.11, §13, §14,
§16.4-16.5, §17, §20 item 3; XC-288 §3.4 (`../specs/2026-10-10-xc288-training-records-design.md`);
`docs/references/decisions.md` TSK-06, TSK-15, TSK-19, TSK-21 to TSK-24, TSK-31, TSK-43, TSK-51, TSK-59, TRN-03,
TRN-06, STE-29; backlog XC-343, XC-344, XC-361, XC-362, XC-363, XC-418 (closed), XC-383 (C3's part), XC-365, XC-404,
XC-371, XC-372, XC-387 (amended). Scope: `.superpowers/c3-prep/scope.md` §4 (calls 1-26), `code-map.md` (16

## Calls

Engineering rulings the plan makes, each with its cost if wrong. The spec's **Engineering** labels and scope §4's
calls are adopted unless the code contradicts them; where it does, that is said. Each names its owning task.

1. **The vocabulary lives in `task.py`** (scope call 1). The format pins read only `wl_xcon.task`'s dataclasses
   (`tests/test_declarations._vocabulary`, by module), so the classes cannot live in `variation.py`. The designed orders
   are block `Order`s, beside `Shuffled`; `task.Balanced` and `task.Random` already name *plan* orders, so the names
   are `SequenceBalanced` and `Priming`. The fields:
   - `repeat`, last field of every distribution, `None` by default and refused at load;
   - `Factorial.targets` (a number per generated name);
   - `Factorial.structure`.

   These fields are beyond the spec's three-argument signature, at defaults. Cost if wrong: a rename moves the hash of
   any task using them (none yet). Task 1.
2. **Distributions are not refused as built.** `check` refuses them at load (`bad-draw`), so a bad draw is a finding
   with a sentence, never an import failure. `Task.__post_init__` refuses only a `draws` that is not a dict of text to
   `Distribution`s, as it does `meanings` and `plans`. **A draw, a condition's own range or a factor naming any
   `declarations.BOUNDED` name is refused explicitly**, whether or not the task also declares a `Param` of that name
   (review M-24).
   - **Only the five distributions are drawn** (the controller's ruling on Task 5's draft): anything else where a
     distribution can stand (a bare `Distribution()`, an author's subclass) is refused, `bad-draw`. A `list` given for
     `values` or `weights` is refused at load (tuples only): it hashes like a tuple but compares unequal and cannot be
     hashed. Nothing in the build uses a `Factorial`, or a distribution with list fields, as a dict key, a set member
     or a cache key (Tasks 4 and 10).

   Cost: one class of error moves. Tasks 1, 5.
3. **"Never both" is a refusal, judged per block** (scope call 3; spec §2). `bad-draw` refuses two cases:
   - a block whose own draw names a setting one of its conditions gives (a value or its own range);
   - a block whose conditions give a setting the task draws, unless the block lists that setting as `BY_CONDITIONS`
     (the text `"by conditions"`) in `Block.draws`.

   `BY_CONDITIONS` for a setting the task does not draw is refused too. Cost: one class change. Task 5.
4. **The generator: a keyed hash, not a seeded stream** (scope call 5; TSK-06's counter-based approach
   [@salmon2011parallel]). `variation.unit(*key)` is the first 53 bits of `sha256` over the key's parts joined by
   `"\x1f"`, as a fraction in [0, 1).
   - **The key for a trial's draw** is `(seed, Draw.number, setting, counter)`. `Draw.number` is the trial's index in
     the run, from 0, never the record's session-wide `trial_number` (review M-2). The counter is 0 (the ruling on
     Task 4's draft).
   - **Properties:** the key is stable across processes and Python versions, holds no generator state, and is computed
     between trials, never in a frame.
   - **Isolation:** it never touches the scheduler's `_rng` (which serves `_refill` and `_repeat`) or `_order_rng`.

   **Not adopted from call 5: "A 'same values' repeat re-derives from the original trial's number."** After a live
   range change, re-deriving gives another value; Call 13 keeps the value instead. Cost if wrong: every seeded run's
   draws differ (none recorded yet). Tasks 4, 10.
5. **Closed forms, bounded work, and nothing that raises between trials.**
   - **A truncated normal** draws by inverse CDF (`statistics.NormalDist`) between its cut's CDF values. `p` is clamped
     into the open interval (0, 1) with `math.nextafter`, since `inv_cdf` raises `StatisticsError` at 0 and 1.
     A cut holding no probability in floating point is refused at load and live (`check.undrawable`, Task 5; review
     I-2).
   - **The non-aging wait's "draw again"** draws by the truncated exponential's inverse CDF. That is exactly the
     distribution redrawing until in range gives, in bounded work.

   - **Nothing a draw can raise on reaches a run** (the ruling on Task 4's draft): Task 5 refuses at load what
     `variation.draw` would raise on: an empty list; all-zero weights, or more weights than values; an `sd` at or below
     0; a wait whose mean is at or below its shortest; a normal missing an end of its cut where its setting declares no
     range to cut to; and a factorial `variation.expanded` reads as giving or excluding nothing (no factors, an empty
     or non-dict exclusion, levels or targets of the wrong type). `check.undrawable` returns a clause beginning "it" or
     "its", which Task 13 writes as "<where> cannot be drawn: <clause>"; it never raises (the ruling on Task 5's
     draft).
   - **A weighted set whose weights sum past a float, or hold a positive weight below the smallest normal float**, is
     refused too, and `variation.draw` clamps its index to the last value of positive weight as a backstop (the plan's
     engineering review, M-2: such weights loaded and then faulted the session at its first draw). **Every flag of
     the new vocabulary** (`Listed.in_order`, `again_at_once`) refuses a value that is not a bool (its M-4).

   Neither has a loop. Cost: none; the distribution is identical. Tasks 4, 5.
6. **The non-aging mean is `minimum + τ`**, the constant-hazard wait's own mean before redrawing (call 20). Spec §3's
   numbers come out exactly: 750-1250 ms with mean 1000 has hazard 1.16, 1.58, 3.03 and 10.51 times flat, and realizes
   922 ms. The spec's "10" rounds 10.51 down (review M-20). It is refused unless `minimum < mean <= maximum` and
   `minimum < maximum`; a mean equal to the minimum is "a spread of zero". The realized mean is written
   `L·e^(-L/τ) / -expm1(-L/τ)`, so a wait whose longest is far past its mean (`NonAging(0, 0.001, 1.0)`) is computed,
   never an `OverflowError` (found drafting Task 8; fixed in Task 4, its test there). Cost: an author's average off by
   the truncation, said in the report. Tasks 4, 5, 8.
7. **Draw keys, and a prepared list in shuffled passes** (call 19; review M-3). Every draw is named by a key tuple:
   - the task's draw: `("task", name)`;
   - a block type's draw: `("block", block_name, name)`;
   - a condition's own range: `("condition", condition_name, name)`.

   `variation.in_force` and `own_ranges` return these keys, and `Session._ranges`, `Session._listed`, `Pending.key` and
   `check.impossible`'s `ranges` are keyed by them. A trial line's `drawn` writes `key[0]` (or a change id).

   For a list, pass `p`'s order sorts the items by `unit(seed, "pass", *key, p, i)`. `Session._listed[key]` counts that
   draw's fresh draws in the run and gives a fresh draw's place; a `same` repeat does not advance it. `in_order=True`
   cycles. Task 10 passes `ordinal=Session._listed[key]` for a list's fresh draws, and `declared=` so a normal is cut
   to its setting's range (the ruling on Task 4's draft). `variation.numbers()` leaves out a normal's cut ends that are
   `None`. Cost: one counter per key. Tasks 4, 10.
8. **A uniform draws real numbers, so a whole-number setting is drawn from a set** (review M-12). A setting an `Array`
   reads as its `n` or its `target` is read through `int()` by the trial (`task.py:869-875`, `946-947`). `check` finds
   those settings and refuses a `Uniform`, `TruncatedNormal` or `NonAging` on one (`bad-draw`, unreadable record: 4.7
   recorded while 4 objects show). They are drawn by `Weighted` or `Listed`. Cost: none found. Tasks 1, 5.
9. **A position is drawn two ways** ("by eccentricity and direction", spec §2):
   - a whole position from a `Weighted` or `Listed` of positions;
   - continuously, through an eccentricity setting and a direction setting, each drawn as a number.

   A `Polar` of distributions is not built; Task 3 files it (XC-D). Cost: a later field. Task 1.
10. **Draws are taken where the trial's values are built** (call 6), between trials, in §17.1's order:
    1. the task's start, then the run's value, then a person's value (the live layer is merged in `spec.values`, call
       8);
    2. a condition's value, or a draw, over them: the block's own or the task's by `variation.in_force`, or the
       condition's own range;
    3. a person's held value over both.

    A held setting is not drawn and not in `drawn`. It is in `live`, and in `overridden` where its condition gave it,
    a value or its own range. Cost: none on the frame path. Task 10.
11. **Directions** (controller ruling 1; the PI's rule, and his later answer of 2026-10-30, "Warn at load
    (Recommended)": a setting's number is shown and recorded as the number it holds, and a load warning,
    `direction-outside-0-360`, tells the author to write 0 to 360; review I-6 rejected on it).
    - **The rig's spelling and the author's.** A value the rig produces for a direction setting, a draw, is normalized
      when written: the rig chooses its spelling. A value a person or the task gives (a condition's, a start, a live
      value) is written as given, and the load warning covers the task's.
    - **Declaration.** A task declares a drawn direction in its own terms, e.g. `Uniform(-45, 45)`. "Lowest above
      highest" stays refused. For a direction setting the span must be at most 360°.
    - **Which settings are directions:** `variation.directions(task)`, the settings a `Polar` reads as its direction.
    - **Drawn values.** The value is drawn in declared terms, and the trial uses it; the position is the same either
      way. A drawn direction setting's value is written through `geometry.shown_direction` in the trial line's
      `params`.
    - **Change rows: written as given** (the controller's ruling on Task 3's draft, over this call's first wording,
      which normalized them through `shown_direction`): a value a person or the task gives is written as given
      everywhere, change rows included. A person's -90 is -90 in `params` and in its row's `was` and `now`.
    - **Ranges.** A written range of directions is normalized end by end (`variation.recorded`, `variation.words`), so
      its lowest may exceed its highest: the range crosses rightward (315 to 45).
    - **Not normalized by C3:** a condition's own value, a start, a person's live value, a change row's value. A drawn
      whole `Polar` is written by `record._written`, whose direction is the `direction-360` branch's.
    - **The load warning:** Call 39.

    Cost if wrong: one record key re-shaped, or one normalization added later. Tasks 3, 4, 5, 7, 10.
12. **Draws are recorded with every field, defaults included** (controller ruling 2), as an appearance is (REC-27).
    **This revises spec §10's "in the hash's form" for the start row's `draws`** (review M-18): a drafter reading the
    spec writes the every-field form there, not the hash's.
    - `variation.recorded(distribution, declared, direction=)` writes a draw that way, and fills a `TruncatedNormal`'s
      missing cut from its setting's declared range.
    - `record._written` writes any `Distribution` it meets as `declarations.canonical(value, every_field=True)`.
    - Where it applies: the start row's `draws`, `generated`'s ranges, `range` and `revert` rows' draws, and `varied`'s
      `distribution`.
    - **The task hash and `plan_form` keep the hash's form**, so no content hash moves.

    Cost: larger rows. Tasks 4, 10, 13, 16.
13. **`same` values are kept, not re-derived** (review M-1).
    `Session._kept: dict[int, dict[str, tuple[object, object, int]]]` maps a trial's `Draw.number` to each setting it
    drew as `(value, source, original)`:
    - `source` is what the trial line's `drawn` wrote: `key[0]` or a change id;
    - `original` is the `Draw.number` whose key drew it.

    An entry is kept while a waiting repeat, a drum or an "again at once" names that trial (`Scheduler.waiting`), and
    is pruned between trials. A `same` setting on a repeat, ordinary or drummed, takes the kept value and source, and
    passes on `original`. `_eased` reads `original` for the seed's value from the range as written. A `fresh` setting
    draws on the repeat's own number. Where the original drew nothing for that setting (a person held it), the repeat
    draws fresh. Cost: memory for waiting repeats only. Tasks 6, 10, 15.
14. **A factorial expands at load into ordinary conditions** (call 13). `variation.expanded(block)` puts the hand-listed
    conditions first, then the generated ones, with `factorial=None`.
    - **Each factor is a setting the task declares** (review M-13), never a bounded name. **Each level is a value that
      setting can hold** (one of its choices, or a finite number) **or its own range** (a `Distribution`). Anything
      else is refused at load (`bad-plan`).
    - **Who uses it:** `Session._plan`, `check`, `preflight` and `review`. `plan_form` stays the declared plan; the
      start row's `generated` lists what expanded.
    - **Names:** `", ".join(f"{factor}={variation.level_name(level)}")` in the factors' declared order. `level_name`
      writes:
      - numbers by `repr` (shortest exact; a `bool` is refused);
      - text as written;
      - a `Polar` as `f"{e!r}° at {shown_direction(d)!r}°"`, its direction normalized, and one at eccentricity 0 as
        `"0°"`, with no direction (the ruling on Task 4's draft);
      - a pair as `f"({x!r}, {y!r})"`;
      - a range by `variation.words`, in the task's own terms (`"-45 to 45"`);
      - anything else by its `repr`, refused at load when that holds an address (`" at 0x"`).
    - **Targets:** `target` for every cell, `targets` by generated name over it.

    Cost: names are what wl-preproc groups by. Tasks 4, 5, 10.
15. **Sequence-balanced** (spec §5; call 14). `SequenceBalanced(depth=2, cycles=1, again_at_once=False)` plays the
    same de Bruijn cycle `cycles` times: one random Euler circuit through the de Bruijn graph of its conditions
    [@aguirre2011de; @brooks2012counterbalancing].
    - **Randomness:** the circuit is drawn from `random.Random(f"design:{seed}:{occurrence}")`, where `occurrence` is
      `len(Scheduler.ended)` as the block opens. Each opening of a block, a person's *back one* included, is a new
      block with its own sequence.
    - **Length** (the PI, 2026-10-31, Appendix B item 1, "Add one closing trial (Recommended)"; Call 45): each cycle
      is the linear de Bruijn sequence, `n**depth + depth - 1` trials (4 conditions: 17 at pairs, 66 at triples), so
      every tuple shows once in each cycle; its first `depth - 1` places are a lead-in that only precedes what
      follows, marked on each trial's `planned` (`lead_in`). The block plays `cycles` of them,
      `(n**depth + depth - 1) * cycles` trials. (The spec's n² cycle missed its closing pair in the last cycle, review
      M-19; the PI chose the closing trial.)
    - **Targets:** each condition's target must be exactly `cycles * n**(depth-1)`, the places it plays past the
      lead-ins; anything else is refused, saying the number to write.
    - **Ending** (review I-3): the block ends at whichever comes first, its plan played out or its `trials` run. It owes
      nothing then: no shortfall, every target treated as met. The places it did not play stay on `block_ends`'
      `planned`, and that cut is the `cut-sequence` warned at load. `trials` above the planned length is refused
      (§11 row 7, a target contradicting the sequence). A time limit cuts the same way.
    - **Refused:**
      - fewer than 2 conditions;
      - a depth under 2, or cycles under 1;
      - a criterion;
      - being a training progression's top stage, which "keeps working" past its rule while a played-out sequence has
        nothing to draw (review M-8).

    Cost: one trial, one refusal. Tasks 4, 5, 6.
16. **Priming** (Q6). `Priming(feature, chance=None, runs=None, again_at_once=False)` takes exactly one of `chance` (in
    [0, 1]) and `runs`: `(low, high)`, whole numbers, `1 <= low <= high`, or a distribution of run lengths, any of the
    five, each draw rounded down, at least 1, a prepared list played in passes (the plan's science review, I-8: lengths
    drawn evenly make a switch ever more expected along a run, confounding run position, which a non-aging draw
    avoids; `variation.run_length`, `Scheduler._run_length`). The review report shows a runs block's chance of a switch
    after each trial of a run (`variation.switch_chances`).
    - **Grouping:** every condition sets `feature` to a value, not a range, and there are at least two values. Values
      are counted and grouped by `repr(canonical(value))`, as the load does (the ruling on Task 5's draft). Task 5's
      refusal of neither or both of `chance` and `runs` is load-bearing: the scheduler assumes exactly one.
    - **The record:** Task 16 writes a priming block's `block_ends` `planned` as `{value, length}` pairs.
    - **A switch** picks another value uniformly. Within a value, conditions play in shuffled passes.
    - **"Last"** is the last trial whose stimulus appeared. A run's length counts only trials whose stimulus appeared.
    - **Targets** are 0 (refused otherwise). The block needs `trials` or `time_limit_s` and ends on them; it takes no
      criterion. As a training progression's top stage it keeps working until its time or a stop, as any top stage does.
    - **Load warnings it no longer meets** (review M-8): designed blocks are exempt from `empty-block` and
      `late-condition`.

    Cost: one counting rule. Appendix B item 6. Tasks 1, 5, 6.
17. **A break in a designed block** (Q5b; engineering in spec §5).
    - **Sequence-balanced, by default:** no repeat. `Scheduler.record` forgives that one trial,
      `Shortfall(..., trials=1, because=DESIGNED, after_trial=<the trial that broke>)`; `possible_avoidance` stays
      false. The sequence goes on.
    - **Priming, by default:** no repeat, and **no shortfall** (review M-9). Runs count shown trials, so a break before
      the stimulus loses no place, and one after it is a shown trial of its run.
    - **With `again_at_once=True`** (either order): the broken trial comes straight back, with `repeat_of`, `at_once`
      and the same `planned`. Its draws follow `same`/`fresh`.
    - **The repeat limit applies to it** (review I-4): `_cap` and the failed tries in a row count as for any repeat.
      Past the limit the trial is forgiven `CAP` or `RIG`, flagged as possible avoidance as §16.6 does, and the
      sequence goes on. Appendix B item 9.
    - **A trainer's drumming** still repeats a trial until right without moving the plan. Task 10 never mutates
      `Draw.planned`, which a trial and its retries share.
    - **What the outline left open, built one way** (Task 6's engineering calls, Appendix B items 11 to 14): a
      sequence-balanced block owes its unplayed places, and nothing once its trials or a time limit cut it; in a
      designed block *clear* moves past only a trial waiting to come back, refusing anything else; a time limit does
      not wait for a trial due "again at once" (only a drum holds it); a priming run's recorded length under a chance
      is the trials it showed.

    Cost: none found; each of the four is a line to change. Task 6.
18. **Eased trials** (Q8; spec §7's engineering). `Scheduler.record(..., eased=False)`.
    - **What an eased trial skips:** it is left out of `_window` (the block's criterion and a stage's own rule), and
      still feeds `_back` (the fall-back) and its condition's counts.
    - **In a training progression** (`ByCriterion`; review I-7): an eased trial also counts toward neither a stage's
      number of trials nor its targets when the stage's end is judged. `Counts.eased` counts it, and in such a plan
      `owed` and `block_trials` leave it out, so the condition is drawn on. The end row's `conditions` still count it
      toward its condition. `Counts.eased_paid` sits beside `Counts.eased`: a stage's trial count leaves out eased
      trials, its targets only the eased tries that paid (the ruling on Task 6's draft). A trial counts as eased for a
      stage's trial count where its **paying** try was eased: a drummed trial whose paying retry followed an easing
      change was made easier (the ruling on Task 15's draft). A sequence-balanced stage below the top ends when its
      plan is played out, eased trials included, never replayed. Appendix B item 10.
    - **Who judges:** `taskd`, from declared meanings (`declarations.resolved`) through `variation.easier`.
    - **What it compares:** for a person's value, the trial's actual value against what it would otherwise have had:
      the condition's value, the run's own (`Session._run_values`), or for a drawn setting the seed's value from the
      range as written. That value is drawn on the original's key (`_kept`'s `original`, Call 13). **For a range
      changed live, the range as a whole against the range as written** (the PI, 2026-10-31, Appendix B item 18,
      "Judge the range as a whole (Recommended)"; Call 45): every trial drawn from it is kept out while it reaches
      anything easier, or which way cannot be read, until it is put back; never trial by trial.
    - **When it cannot tell:** a choice setting's meaning reads "on changing it" (TRN-11), so a changed choice is read
      by its `raising` (`variation.easier(..., choices=bool(param.choices))`, the ruling on Task 4's draft; Task 7's
      `went` for a choice setting comes from its declared `raising`), and **a changed appearance is read the same way**
      (the ruling on Task 15's draft, correcting this call's first wording). Only a reading relative to the
      background, relative to a setting holding no number, or against no value cannot be read; there a live change
      keeps the trial out. The animal is never moved up on doubt (review M-19).

    - **Said to the trainer** (the plan's engineering review, I-2; its science review, I-4: a trainer who widens a
      window sees a perfect streak and a block that will not end): the changes feed warns, once a block for each
      setting, where the block's criterion or a training stage moves the animal on (`Scheduler.moves_up`), naming the
      trial, the setting and the way back (`taskd._kept_out`); telemetry's `eased` and the page's standing line say
      it while it lasts (Tasks 15, 17, 18).

    Cost: fewer trials toward moving up (Appendix B items 2 and 10). Tasks 4, 6, 15, 17, 18.
19. **The live layer stays merged in `spec.values`, its names kept apart and recorded beside it** (call 8). Change ids
    are assigned in `_apply_staged` (call 9), the one applier of every kind of change. It is built in three steps, each
    with its consumer (review M-23):
    - **Task 7:** `_staged` rows, kind `set`, one change id each.
    - **Task 13:** `Pending` rows (hand-backs and ranges), applied with `_staged` in the order offered.
    - **Task 14:** acts: one change id for every row of a revert, kind `revert`, and a `Moment` per act.

    Tasks 13 and 14's branches in `_apply_staged` pass `sequence` and raise `_sequence` and `_change` as Task 7's does.
    A ceiling's change row writes `meaning` null, as the ask promised (the ruling on Task 7's draft).

    **A hand-back and a range never pass through `Session.set`.** A hand-back carries no new value: it restores the
    run's own. A range is not a `SetParameter`. A revert's values do pass through `Session.set`; its hand-backs and
    ranges do not. Cost: if the PI wants hand-backs through `set`, one call changes (Appendix A, item 5, for
    approval). Tasks 7, 13, 14.
20. **Each new console act is its own command and branch** (call 10): `HandBack`, `SetRange`, `Revert`, with wire kinds
    `hand_back`, `range` and `revert`. `SetRange.numbers` are decoded by `link._setting`, called unchanged; a word among
    them is refused by the decoder.
    - **The three acts run outside the listed `try`, so each refuses its own failures** (review I-1).
      `_hand_back`, `_range` and `_revert` never raise. Each catches its own `Exceeded`, `ValueError` and any other
      `Exception`, and refuses with `_refuse` and a sentence, as `_beyond_range` does. Anything leaving `_command`
      reaches the run loop's `except Exception` and ends the session as a fault (`taskd.py:3052`).
    - **Order inside `_range`:** `_possible` runs before `_beyond_range`, which writes accepted warnings, so a range
      refused for §9 leaves no warning written.

    Cost: Appendix A items 1-2 (approved). Tasks 2, 13, 14.
21. **The change log's row** (XC-288 §3.4; call 11; controller rulings 3 and 4, adopting the ask's names).
    `parameter_changes.jsonl` keeps its name.
    - **Keys:** the "Record shapes" contract below. Every row has a non-empty `name`.
    - **`sequence`** appears only on the four kinds that strobe `PARAM_CHANGED`.
    - **Resume** learns every kind in Task 7, the commit that first writes a row without `sequence` (`_clear`'s). It
      stays fail-closed (review M-6): `_read` raises `Unresumable` for:
      - a row of unknown `kind`;
      - a row of a strobed kind, or with no kind, that has no integer `sequence`;
      - a `change` that is not an integer.
    - **Clears and the two switches are written twice** (ruling 3): `controls.jsonl` exactly as today, and the change
      log, until wl-preproc reads and times the log's rows (XC-B).
    - **Fixed by the ask** (the ruling on Task 3's draft): change ids start at 1, never 0; a change row's
      `trial_number` equals the trial line's. `SessionRecord.change` keeps its four checks: a code defect that would
      write a row the log cannot hold fails loudly, and an unreadable record is a refusal case (the ruling on Task 7's
      draft).

    Cost: a session made unresumable, failing closed; dual writes to remove later. Tasks 3, 7.
22. **A live range** (Q7b; spec §6's engineering).
    - **Which draw it changes:** the one the open block uses, its own `Block.draws` entry (key `("block", block, name)`)
      or else the task's (`("task", name)`). It holds for the rest of the run wherever that draw applies.
    - **Live numbers:** `Uniform` `low`, `high`; `TruncatedNormal` `mean`, `sd`, `low`, `high`; `NonAging` `minimum`,
      `mean`, `maximum` (`variation.LIVE_NUMBERS`). The kind never changes.
    - **Refused:**
      - a condition's own range (the PI);
      - a setting declared `live=False`, as `Session.set` refuses it (review M-4);
      - a direction setting's range, which is not live in C3, since a shown range would need mapping back to declared
        terms (review M-15; XC-E);
      - `Weighted` and `Listed`, whose numbers are not live in C3 (XC-C).
    - **Checks:** `undrawable` (an empty cut included), then `_possible`, then each extreme past the declared range
      re-checked widened (`_beyond_range`).
    - **Undoing it:** *hand back* does not undo a range. It is set back by sending its numbers or by revert.
    - **Said before and after it applies** (the plan's science review, M-2 and I-4): a person's staged range names the
      blocks of the run's plan it reaches (`Session._reaches`, carried in its `Staged.overrides`), and the card of a
      draw whose range a person changed says so (`ParamRow.source` `"range"`, "drawn each trial, from a range a person
      changed live").
    - **Built one way where the outline was silent** (Task 13's engineering calls): a second range on one draw builds
      on the first, its row's `was` the first's `now`; a range row's `meaning` says which way the new range went,
      judged as a whole against the range written (`went`; the PI, 2026-10-31; Call 45); both acts refuse a
      ceiling's name first, by name; refusals are filed under the setting's name; a range's extremes are checked as a
      typed value is, over every block, so a block's own draw can be refused for another block.

    Cost: one more branch (Appendix B items 3-4). Tasks 4, 13.
23. **A hand-back** (Q7a). It is refused for a setting no person holds.
    - **What it does:** it always puts `spec.values[name]` back to the run's own value (`Session._run_values`, the
      task's start under the run's; absent if neither).
    - **What its row says:** `to` names what takes the setting back **in the open block** (review M-16): `"conditions"`,
      `"draw"`, or `"run"`. `now` is the run's value only where `to` is `"run"`, else null. Both are read **as it
      applies** (`_apply_pending`), never as it is offered, since the plan may move to another block between (the
      plan's engineering review, M-1: a row claimed a value no trial held).
    - **Checked as a typed value is** (the plan's engineering review, I-3): beside `_possible`, the run's own value it
      restores, where it lies outside its declared range, is re-checked widened with the ranges in force now
      (`_beyond_range`), and the hand-back refused at once if that refuses it; a range widened since the run started
      could otherwise meet a run value no check had judged with it.

    Typing the old value back still does not hand back. Cost: none. Task 13.
24. **Revert** (spec §8). It goes to a change id of the run in progress, or 0 (the run's start); a change id of another
    run, or none, is refused with a sentence.
    - **A clear's, drum switch's or training switch's id** restores the moment in force then: the latest snapshot at or
      before it (review M-15).
    - **Rebuilt from:** `Session._moments`, a snapshot after each act (held values and live ranges, task settings only).
    - **Values held then:** re-staged through `Session.set`, unchanged.
    - **Settings held now and not then:** handed back.
    - **Ranges:** restored, or removed back to the declaration.
    - **Refused whole** (review M-16): on any refusal, by `set` or by `_possible`, `_staged`, `_pending` and `_acts`
      are cut back to their lengths before the revert. No change row is written and nothing is applied. A warning
      `_beyond_range` accepted for an earlier value stays accepted, by that function's documented rule.
    - **Rows:** one act, rows of kind `revert`, each with `moment`.
    - **Never touched:** counts and training aids are not reverted; a bounded setting never appears in a moment.
    - **Built one way where the outline was silent** (Task 14's engineering calls, accepted): a revert offers its
      hand-backs and ranges ahead of its values, and sets its values in the order of their names; a revert row's `was`
      is what the setting held just before that row; a reward size's change keeps no moment; a revert that changes
      nothing is refused; restored ranges are not re-checked widened (each was checked when offered; a probe showed
      such a re-check could not fail). Its one residual, two values each outside its range judged in name order, can
      only refuse a revert needlessly (XC-F). The page asks no confirmation (Appendix B item 15).
    - **A preview before one tap** (the plan's science review, M-1): each moment the frame lists says what a revert to
      it would change, from what the run will hold once all offered applies (`MomentRow.changes`, `Session._preview`
      over `Session._undone`, which `_revert` reads too, so the two cannot disagree).
    - **No widened re-check of a revert's hand-backs** (the engineering review's I-3 is a hand-back's): a revert puts
      back a moment's whole layer, its held values through `set` and its ranges as they were, a state the run held;
      each act that made it was checked over the whole plan as it applied (a start by the pre-flight, a value and a
      range widened, a hand-back now too), so the layer it restores was judged as a whole, and `_possible` judges the
      revert again at once.

    Cost: one key (`moment`) the ask gains. Task 14.
25. **§9's three combinations judge concrete values** (call 17), in one function, `check.impossible`. It runs at load
    (Task 9), at a run's start (Task 11's pre-flight, Task 12's backstop in `Session.run`) and live (Task 12).
    - **No time to answer:** a `Hold` beaten by a plain `After` on the same state to an `Outcome` **not in `task.RIGHT`**
      (review M-10). A no-go design whose timeout is the right answer is not refused. Ties go by exit order, as
      `_holds_cut_short` reads them: `t <= h` where the `After` is listed first, `t < h` otherwise. **Judged by
      bounds**, so no enumeration cuts it short.
    - **A target that looks like its distractors:** an `Array` whose `looks` and `among` are equal once references are
      resolved. **Judged by value sets:** the set of each resolved appearance, over its references' possible values,
      never a cross product of all settings.
    - **Looks that swap:** set size 2 in a block where the same pair of looks is target and distractor on one trial
      and distractor and target on another, **a full swap only**, judged by the same value sets (the controller's
      ruling on Task 9's draft: the spec's reason, "one display can call for either answer"; a chain whose displays
      differ has an answer on each and loads; warnings over refusals).
    - **Only an array found by its look** (the PI, 2026-10-31, Appendix B item 17, "Refuse only odd-one-out tasks
      (Recommended)"; Call 45): the two look checks refuse only an array whose `found_by` is `"look"`, the default,
      and a swap where any array in it is; in one a cue names the target of (`"cue"`) they warn, `cued-target`, at
      load and at a run's start (`impossible(..., cued=True)`), and live they are accepted. No time to answer is
      refused whatever names the target.
    - **At load:** judged at the task's starting values. A setting nothing gives is not judged; the pre-flight refuses
      it.
    - **The reference tasks** hold their target hold in its own `verify` state with `After(3.0)`, so none is refused.

    - **Keyed as the session keys them:** `Session._ranges` holds `{key: (Distribution, change)}`;
      `check.impossible` takes `{key: Distribution | None}`, so a caller strips the change ids, and is called once per
      change (it dedupes; the ruling on Tasks 9 and 10's drafts).
    - **Live, judged against the trials waiting to come back too:** Call 42.

    `hold-cut-short` keeps warning over ranges. Cost: a refusal where a warning was wanted, one class change. Tasks 9,
    11, 12, 13.
26. **The live refusal fails closed.** `Session._impossible` runs inside the listed `try`; nothing but `Exceeded`
    leaves it (as `_beyond_range`). A fault in the check refuses the edit, never the session; a ceiling's name is never
    judged. Cost: a broken check refuses live edits of task settings until fixed (Appendix A, item 2's text). Task 12.
27. **`_beyond_range` learns conditions and draws** (spec §11). A value outside its range is re-checked with the run's
    plan's conditions and the draws' bounds in force. `check.beyond_range`'s result depends only on the values outside
    their ranges (`check.py:264-355`), so it runs **once per distinct set of outside values**, never once per condition
    (review M-11). Its signature `(name, value, by)` stays, since welfare-listed `set` calls it. **One rule for a draw's
    extremes:** `variation.extremes(distribution, declared=None) -> tuple` (Task 11's) widens a draw one extreme at a
    time with its condition's values, leaving out a value of weight 0, which is never drawn, as `check._drawable`
    does; Task 12 calls it, and the pre-flight does (the ruling on Tasks 11 and 12's drafts). Cost: more work between
    trials, unmeasured (XC-372). Tasks 11, 12.
28. **A run's start: draws widened, and the impossible refused.**
    - **Widening:** a draw past its declared range is the pre-flight's to widen (spec §11; scope call 4; C2b's
      precedent for conditions' values), in `preflight.beyond`, never in `check_task`: `beyond_range` calls
      `check_task`, so that would recurse. A drawn setting counts as given in `preflight.values` (call 24).
    - **§9 at the start** (review I-5): `preflight.beyond` also runs `check.impossible` over the plan's expanded blocks
      at the merged starting values. A finding blocks, failing the starting-values item. `Session.run` runs the same
      check as its backstop, beside `_unwritable`, refusing as its blocking-findings backstop does; that covers
      `wlx run --set`.
    - **`wlx run` and `wlx check`** take no pre-flight (XC-159), so they do not widen a draw; XC-371 is extended to
      draws.
    - `preflight` may import `check._outside`: the memo's key is what `beyond_range` filters by.

    Cost: `wlx run` does not widen a draw. Tasks 11, 12.
29. **`wlx run` draws a fresh seed when given none** (call 23): `--seed` defaults to `None`, then
    `service._fresh_seed()`. The seed is recorded on the start row as today and said at the terminal. `cli.main`'s
    listed line is untouched. Cost: tests that leaned on seed 1 pass one. Task 11.
30. **Telemetry schema 19** (spec §6; call 22). It adds:
    - `ParamRow.source`, `conditions`, `draw`, `numbers`;
    - `Staged.kind`, `overrides`;
    - `MomentRow` and `Telemetry.moments`;
    - from the plan's reviews (revision round 1): `Telemetry.eased` (engineering I-2, science I-4); `ParamRow.source`
      `"range"` (science I-4); a person's staged range's `overrides` naming the blocks it reaches (science M-2);
      `ParamRow.more`, a card naming at most `link.CONDITIONS_SHOWN` (20, an engineering default, a display bound)
      conditions and counting the rest (engineering M-5: a factorial of 1296 conditions doubled every frame); and
      `MomentRow.changes`, what a revert to it would change (science M-1).

    The staged row names the conditions it will override before it applies. `taskd._overriding` is retired, replaced
    by `Session._overrides(name)`, which the card, the staged row and the applied feed line all read. The feed line
    keeps naming them, as the revision drafted for TSK-19 says ("stays").

    Details (review M-15):
    - a staged range's `was` and `now` are the rig's words (`variation.words`);
    - a staged hand-back's `now` is `None` or the run's value;
    - `moments` keeps the run's start when the list is capped: `Session.moments` is built from `_moments`, newest
      first, `_moments[0]` the run's start kept last;
    - `numbers` is `None` for a setting declared `live=False` (M-4) or a direction setting;
    - `Staged.kind` reads `_acts` and `Pending.act`, so a revert's staged changes show as `revert`;

## Global Constraints

- **Language:** US English in code, comments and docs.
- **The PI's decisions** above are binding and quoted where built; none is re-asked.
- **Welfare** (Appendix A): the welfare-critical list (`docs/design/architecture.md`, "Welfare-critical modules") is
  not widened. **The only listed function whose text changes is `Session._command`.** It changes by exactly these
  four insertions and nothing else, its `held` pass-through and its `except (Exceeded, TypeError) as refused:` line
  untouched:
  - Tasks 13 and 14 insert, immediately after the `BackBlock` branch (before
    `if not isinstance(command, _link.SetParameter):`), in this order:

    ```python
            if isinstance(command, _link.HandBack):
                self._hand_back(command, index)
                return
            if isinstance(command, _link.SetRange):
                self._range(command, index)
                return
            if isinstance(command, _link.Revert):
                self._revert(command, index)
                return
    ```

    (Task 13 the first two branches, Task 14 the third.) These branches sit outside the listed `try`, so the three
    functions they call never raise (Call 20).
  - Task 12 inserts, as the first line inside the `try:` of the setting path, before `self.set(command.name,
    command.value, by=command.by)`:

    ```python
                self._impossible(command.name, command.value)
    ```

  **Byte-identical with `d3a1070`:** `Session.set`, `_ends`, `_hold`, `_manual_reward`, `_schedule`, `OUTSIDE_A_RUN`,
  `link._setting`, `Service._start` and the other listed `Service` functions, `preflight.gate` and `out_of_cage`,
  `cli._settle_departure`, `_settle_return`, `main`'s `_marks.depart(session, departure)` line, and `bounds.py`,
  `welfare.py`, `marks.py` and `stranded.py` whole. Task 20 compares them.
- **Hot path: nothing new per frame.** Every draw, designed sequence, eased judgement, check, change row and snapshot
  is taken between trials. `run_trial`'s per-frame hook is unchanged. Nothing allocates per frame.
- **Nothing new raises between trials.** A draw, an act or a check that can fail refuses or clamps; it never ends a
  session (Calls 5, 20, 26).
- **No timing claim** (CLAUDE.md). The wait's hazard and averages are arithmetic of the declared distribution. A change

  place: `tests/test_references.py` reads its prose, so it cites no library key the base lacks (a key a task adds is
  named in a code span). Then each task's Step "the whole suite" states the count the plan's re-proof after revision
  round 2 printed at that task (the header).

  in the dry runs (the build worktree's own in the build), always `cd <worktree> && $PY ...`, never `-I`.

## Review Focus

Five inputs the spec implies that no task's own tests would exercise unless pinned, most likely first. Each is pinned
by a test in its owning task.

1. **A `same` setting's repeat after the range it came from changed, inside a long drum** (Q3, Q7b, "Follow
   same/fresh"). A drummed chain of 12 failed tries holds a waiting repeat past its window, while a live range change
   lands between tries. Expected:
   - every drummed try and the late ordinary repeat carry the original trial's `same` value, its `drawn` naming the
     original's source (`_kept`'s source);
   - `fresh` settings are drawn inside the new range, `drawn` naming its change id;
   - `_kept` never drops an entry a waiting repeat names.

   Owner: Task 13, `test_a_same_value_survives_a_long_drum_and_a_range_changed_meanwhile` (moved from Task 10 with
   `Pending`, review M-23).
2. **A designed block a trainer disturbs** (Q5b, C2b's moves). Within one session:
   - a trainer switches drumming on mid-sequence;
   - presses *back one* into a sequence-balanced block;
   - lets its time limit cut the second cycle.

   Expected: drummed tries never advance `planned`; the reopened block plays a new sequence from its own occurrence;
   the cut leaves the unplayed positions on `block_ends`' `planned` with no `designed` shortfall for trials never
   reached (only broken ones); `cut-sequence` was warned at load. Owner: Task 6,
   `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_survives_a_drum_a_move_back_and_its_time`; Task 16 its record,
   `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_a_trainer_disturbs_records_each_plan_its_drum_and_its_cut`.
3. **A revert in the same drain as another console's change, sent while paused** (spec §8; `_hold` drains through
   `_command`). Expected:
   - another person's `set` staged before the revert in the same drain applies first and keeps its own change id;
   - the revert applies as one act after it;
   - a revert refused whole (one value outside its range breaking the run) leaves that earlier `set` staged and writes
     nothing.

   Owner: Task 14, `test_a_revert_refused_whole_leaves_another_persons_staged_change_alone`.
4. **Resume over the grown log** (spec §8; `stranded.find` is welfare-listed and reads through `resume._read`). A
   session's log holds a clear, a drum switch, a hand-back, a range change and a two-row revert, written through
   `record.change` before it crashed. Expected:
   - `stranded.find` lists it resumable;
   - the resumed session's next `sequence` and next `change` exceed every one in the log;
   - the reward size is restored from the last `set` row of it only;
   - with one damaged row added (an unknown `kind`; a `set` without `sequence`; a `change` that is text), it is
     listed not resumable, failing closed (review M-6).

   Owner: Task 7, `test_a_session_whose_log_holds_every_kind_is_found_resumable_and_goes_on_numbering`.
5. **The new code in `_command`'s path fed what `set` alone used to refuse, and checks that raise** (review I-1).
   - **The line:** a word for a numeric setting, a ceiling's name (`reward_correct`), an undeclared name, `nan`, and a
     setting no structure uses are each refused exactly as before, by `set`'s own sentence. A ceiling's value is
     staged as before. Nothing raises past the `except` line. A `check.impossible` that raises refuses the change,
     saying the check could not run, and the session runs on.
   - **The three acts:** a check that raises inside a hand-back, a range or a revert refuses it, and the session runs
     on.

   Owners: Task 12, `test_the_live_refusal_line_lets_set_refuse_what_it_always_refused_and_never_raises`; Tasks 13
   and 14, `test_a_check_that_raises_inside_a_hand_back_or_a_range_refuses_it_and_the_session_runs_on` and
   `test_a_check_that_raises_inside_a_revert_refuses_it_and_the_session_runs_on`.

## Record shapes (the contract Tasks 3, 7, 10, 13, 14, 16, 17 write and Task 19 reads)

Field names are the ask's (`preproc-ask.md`), with the additions marked **+** (Call 31; Task 3 puts them in the ask
before committing it), updated by the controller's rulings on the drafts (Calls 11, 31, 41).

**A `trials.jsonl` line** gains:
- `drawn`: `{name: source}`, `{}` when nothing was drawn.
  - **The source** is the draw key's first part (Call 7): `"task"` or `"block"` (that draw as declared), or
    `"condition"` (a condition's own range).
  - **Or it is an integer:** the `change` id of the act whose range is in force, a `range` row or a `revert` that
    restored a changed range.
  - **On a repeat,** a `same` setting is listed with its original's source (`_kept`).
- `live`: sorted list of the names a person holds this trial (`Session._edited`). A live range is not here.
- `overridden`: as C2b, the subset of `live` the trial's condition gave, now including a condition's own range.
- `eased`: sorted list of names whose live change kept the trial out of moving up.
- `planned`: one of these, or null:
  - `{"cycle": c, "position": p, "lead_in": l}` (sequence-balanced, `cycle` and `position` each from 0; `lead_in`
    true on the first `depth - 1` places of each cycle, a lead-in that only precedes what follows: the PI, 2026-10-31,
    Appendix B item 1);
  - `{"run": r, "switch": s, "value": v}` (priming): `run` counts from 0, `switch` is true on the first trial of its
    run, and `v` is the planned feature value, written as a setting's value is.

  A trial played again at once has the same `planned` as the one that broke.
- `params`: unchanged in shape. A drawn direction setting's value goes through `shown_direction`; a value a person or
  the task gives is written as given (Call 11).

**The `runs.jsonl` start row** gains:
- `draws`: `{name: variation.recorded(...)}` for the task's draws, every field (Call 12), or null when the task draws
  nothing.
- `generated`: `[{"block": name, "conditions": [{"name", "values", "target"}], "excluded": [exclusion, ...]}]` for each
  block type whose factorial expanded, its range values written by `variation.recorded`; `[]` when none. A plain run
  has `[]`.
- `plan_form` stays `declarations.canonical(task.plans[run.plan])`, the declared plan, not the expanded one.
- **+** `directions`: the names of the run's direction settings, sorted, so a reader applies circular statistics to
  values written from 0 to 360; `[]` where none (the plan's science review, M-4).

**Each `block_ends` entry** gains:
- `varied`: `{name: [way, ...]}`, each way one of:
  - `{"by": "condition"}`;
  - `{"by": "draw", "from": source, "distribution": variation.recorded(...)}`, with `from` as `drawn` writes it: one
    entry for each draw the block's trials were drawn from, that is, each distinct pair of source and draw, a
    condition's own range a draw of its own (Call 31);
  - `{"by": "person"}`.
- `planned`: a sequence-balanced block's planned condition names in order, played or not; a priming block's
  `[{"value": v, "length": n}, ...]` as far as it played; else null.
- **+** `counts`: `{condition: {"trials": n, "overridden": k, "eased": e}}` for each condition that ran a trial in the
  block, its lines, those whose `overridden` is not empty and those whose `eased` is not empty; `{}` for a block that
  ran no trial (the plan's science review, M-4).

`varied` entries are made at a block's first trial; a block that ran no trial has `varied` `{}`.

**Shortfalls** (sequence-balanced only, Call 17): `because` `"designed"`, `trials` 1, the broken trial's condition,
`after_trial` the trial that broke, `by` null.

**A `parameter_changes.jsonl` row** (`SessionRecord.change`; one per setting an act moves):

```
{"change": int, "kind": str, "name": str, "was": ..., "now": ..., "by": actor map or null,
 "at": float, "at_local": str, "trial_number": int, "run": int|null,
 "meaning": {"kind", "role", "raising", "relative_to", "went", "step"} | null,
 "offered": [], "odds": null, "event_code": int|null,
 ["sequence": int]  (kinds set, hand_back, range, revert only), **detail}
```

- **`kind`** is one of `record.KINDS` = `("set", "hand_back", "range", "revert", "clear", "drum", "training")`.
  `record.STROBED` = the first four.
- **`change`** starts at 1, never 0, one id per act.
- **`trial_number`** is `Session._levels.trials + 1`, the first trial it applies to, numbered as that trial's line.
- **`was` and `now`** are written as given, a direction's included (Call 11). **`was` is null** where a person's value,
  or a revert's, lands on a setting drawn or given by its conditions at that moment, no person holding it (Call 41).
- **`meaning`** is the setting's resolved `Meaning` with `relative_to` as written (`"background"` for `BACKGROUND`).
  Its last two keys:
  - `went`: `"easier"`, `"harder"` or null, from `variation.easier`; on a `range` row, and a `revert` row putting a
    range back, from `variation.easier_range`, the new range judged as a whole against the range written (the PI,
    2026-10-31, Appendix B item 18), null where it is the written range again or which way cannot be read; and null
    where `was` is null;
  - `step`: `now - was` in the setting's unit, or null when either is not a number.

  `meaning` is null on a row naming no task setting: a ceiling's, `clear`, `drum` and `training` rows.
- **Per kind:**

| kind | name | was / now | detail |
|---|---|---|---|
| `set` | the setting | its value before, after, as given; `was` null under a draw or conditions (Call 41) | |
| `hand_back` | the setting | the person's value; the run's value where `to` is `"run"`, else null | **+** `to`: `"run"`, `"conditions"` or `"draw"` (the open block's) |
| `range` | the setting | the draw before and after, `variation.recorded` (every field) | **+** `from`: `"task"` or `"block"` (the key's first part); **+** `block`: the block type's name or null |
| `revert` | the setting | what it held before; what it holds again: a value, null where handed back, or a recorded draw | **+** `moment`: the change id restored (0, the run's start); `from`/`block` on a range row |
| `clear` | `"owed"` | what the condition owed before, after | the control row's `condition`, `block`, `rest`, `cleared` |
| `drum` | `"drumming"` | what drumming read before, after | the control row's `scope`, `block` |
| `training` | the setting, `"clear"` or `"first_answers"` | off or on, before and after (booleans) | the control row's `setting` |

A row written before C3 has no `kind`, and resume reads it as `set`.

## The drafting waves

The tasks were drafted and dry-run in waves, in parallel within a wave; a task's text says "wave N" for its own. In
this plan's numbers the waves run in order: wave 1, Tasks 1 to 3; wave 2, Task 4; wave 3, Tasks 5 to 8; wave 4, Tasks
9 and 10; wave 5, Tasks 11 and 12; wave 6, Task 13; wave 7, Tasks 14 and 15; wave 8, Tasks 16 and 17; wave 9, Tasks 18
and 19; wave 10, Task 20. The build runs them one after another, in this order, as the sequential dry run did.

---

### Task 1: The variation vocabulary in the task object

A task may draw settings at random each trial, and a block may make its conditions from factors and play them in a designed order (spec §2-§5). **The vocabulary lives in `task.py`** (Call 1), beside the condition orders, where the format pins read it (`tests/test_declarations.py`'s `_vocabulary`, by module) and a task file can name it; `variation.py` (Task 4) holds the arithmetic, which `task.py` cannot import. It gains:
- **the five distributions the PI chose** (TSK-24): `Uniform`, `Weighted`, `TruncatedNormal`, `Listed` and `NonAging`, under `Distribution`, each closing with `repeat`, `SAME` or `FRESH`, which the load will require (Q3, "Per drawn setting, required");
- **where draws are written** (Q1a, "Task default, block may replace"): `Task.draws`, which a block type's own `Block.draws` replaces or, for a setting its conditions give, marks `BY_CONDITIONS` (Call 3); and a condition's value that is a `Distribution`, its own range (Q1b), said in `Condition`'s docstring;
- **`Factorial`** (TSK-22, Q4): a block's conditions from factors minus exclusions, each cell owed the same, with `targets` and `structure` beyond the spec's three arguments, at defaults (Call 1);
- **the two designed orders**, `SequenceBalanced` (TSK-23, Q5a) and `Priming` (Q6), each a block's `Order` beside `Shuffled`, never a plan's: the names `Balanced` and `Random` are the plan orders' (Call 1);
- **what names an array's target** (the PI, 2026-10-31, on this plan's Appendix B item 17, "Refuse only odd-one-out tasks (Recommended)"): `Array.found_by`, one of `FOUND_BY`, `"look"` by default (the target is the odd one out, found by its look) or `"cue"` (something else the trial shows names it: a cue, a remembered sample, a place). The load's two look checks refuse only an array found by its look and warn for a cued one (Task 9); a word in the task language's own style, a text value from a tuple of them, as `Stimulus.combine` is from `COMBINE`, documented where the array's other words are, on its fields.

**Distributions are not refused as built** (Call 2): a draw that cannot be drawn is a load finding with a sentence (`bad-draw`, Task 5), never a task file that will not import. Only a task's `draws` is refused as built when it is not a dict of non-empty text to `Distribution`s, as its `meanings` and `plans` are. Every new field is at a default, so `canonical` leaves it out, **no task's content hash moves and `FORMAT` stays 1**; `DEFAULTS` gains each class and field. Nothing here is played yet: Task 4 draws, Task 5 checks, Tasks 6 and 10 play.

**Files:**
- Modify: `wl_xcon/task.py` (a new "Drawn values" section before "Plans and blocks": `SAME`, `FRESH`, `REPEATS`, `BY_CONDITIONS`, `Distribution`, `Uniform`, `Weighted`, `TruncatedNormal`, `Listed`, `NonAging`; `SequenceBalanced` and `Priming` after `Constrained`; `Factorial` after `Condition`; `Condition`'s and `Block`'s docstrings; `Block.draws`, `Block.factorial`; `Task`'s docstring, `Task.draws`, `Task.__post_init__`; `FOUND_BY` before `Array`, and `Array.found_by`, its last field)
- Modify (docs): `docs/design/architecture.md` (the task object's paragraph names its draws)
- Modify (test): `tests/test_declarations.py` (`DEFAULTS` only)
- Create (test): `tests/test_draw_vocabulary.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: `task.Order`, `BlockOrder`, `Condition`, `Block`, `Plan`, `Task` and `Task.__post_init__` (unchanged in shape); `declarations.canonical`, `content_hash` (unchanged).
- Produces (in `wl_xcon/task.py`; every class `@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)`, fields in this order, none with a `__post_init__` but `Task`'s):
  - **Constants:** `SAME = "same"`, `FRESH = "fresh"`, `REPEATS = (SAME, FRESH)`, `BY_CONDITIONS = "by conditions"`.
  - **Distributions:** `Distribution` (no fields), and under it:
    - `Uniform(low: float, high: float, repeat: str | None = None)`;
    - `Weighted(values: tuple, weights: tuple, repeat: str | None = None)`;
    - `TruncatedNormal(mean: float, sd: float, low: float | None = None, high: float | None = None, repeat: str | None = None)`;
    - `Listed(values: tuple, in_order: bool = False, repeat: str | None = None)`;
    - `NonAging(minimum: float, mean: float, maximum: float, repeat: str | None = None)`.
  - **`Factorial(factors: dict[str, tuple], exclude: tuple = (), target: int = 1, targets: dict[str, int] = field(default_factory=dict), structure: str | None = None)`**. Each factor names a setting the task declares; each level is a value that setting can hold or its own range, a `Distribution` (Call 14). `exclude` is a tuple of `{factor: level}` dicts, **each excluding every combination that holds all the levels it names** (the docstring's rule; Task 4's `generated` implements it). `structure` is what each generated condition plays (`None`, the task's default).
  - **Designed orders:** `SequenceBalanced(Order)` with `depth: int = 2`, `cycles: int = 1`, `again_at_once: bool = False`; `Priming(Order)` with `feature: str`, `chance: float | None = None`, `runs: tuple[int, int] | Distribution | None = None` (a distribution of run lengths, each rounded down: the science review's I-8), `again_at_once: bool = False`. Neither is a `BlockOrder`, so `Plan.__post_init__` refuses either as a plan's order, as built.
  - **What names an array's target:** `FOUND_BY = ("look", "cue")`, immediately before `Array`; `Array.found_by: str = "look"`, its last field, after `phase`. At its default `canonical` leaves it out, so no task that shows an array moves its hash.
  - **New fields:** `Block.draws: dict[str, Distribution | str] = field(default_factory=dict)` and `Block.factorial: Factorial | None = None`, the last two fields, after `time_limit_s`; `Task.draws: dict[str, Distribution] = field(default_factory=dict)`, the last field, after `plans`.
  - **Shape check:** `Task.__post_init__` raises `ValueError` for a `draws` that is not a dict ("a task's draws are a dict of setting names to Distributions"), a key that is not non-empty text ("a draw names its setting by text, not ''"), or a value that is not a `Distribution` ("draw 'wait' is a Distribution (Uniform, Weighted, TruncatedNormal, Listed or NonAging), not str"; `BY_CONDITIONS` included).
  - **Docstrings:** `Condition`'s says a value may be a `Distribution`, its own range (Q1b); `Uniform`'s carries Call 8 (a whole-number setting is drawn from a set; `check` refuses a uniform, a normal or a wait on an `Array`'s `n` or `target`); `Distribution`'s says a direction is drawn in the task's own terms, span at most 360, and written from 0 to 360 (Call 11).

```python
"""The variation vocabulary in the task object (engine build C3; its spec §2-§5): the five
distributions a setting is drawn from, each saying what a repeat of its trial takes; where a task
and a block type declare their draws; the conditions a block makes from factors; and the two
designed orders of a block's conditions. Declarations only: what they declare is judged at load
(`check.check_task`) and played between trials, never here."""

from __future__ import annotations

import dataclasses
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from wl_xcon.cli import _load_task
from wl_xcon.declarations import canonical, content_hash
from wl_xcon.task import (
    BY_CONDITIONS,
    FOUND_BY,
    FRESH,
    OWED,
    REPEATS,
    SAME,
    After,
    Array,
    Block,
    BlockOrder,
    Condition,
    Counting,
    Distribution,
    Factorial,
    Listed,
    NonAging,
    On,
    Order,
    Outcome,
    P,
    Param,
    Plan,
    Priming,
    SequenceBalanced,
    Shuffled,
    State,
    Task,
    Trial,
    TruncatedNormal,
    Uniform,
    Weighted,
)

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
HOLD = Param("fix_hold", unit="s", low=0.05, high=2.0, start=0.3)
WAIT = Param("wait", unit="s", low=0.5, high=1.5, start=1.0)
CONTRAST = Param("contrast", unit="fraction", low=0.02, high=1.0, start=0.5)


def _task(**fields) -> Task:
    """One structure declaring a hold, a wait and a contrast; its draws and plans as given."""
    trial = Trial(
        start="wait",
        params=[HOLD, WAIT, CONTRAST],
        states=[State("wait", go=[On(After(P("wait")), Outcome.CORRECT)])],
        counting=Counting(after_stimulus=OWED, appears="wait"),
    )
    return Task({"wait": trial}, default="wait", **fields)


def test_the_five_distributions_carry_their_numbers_and_what_a_repeat_takes():
    """The PI's five (TSK-24), frozen, each closing with `repeat`: `SAME` or `FRESH` on a repeat of
    its trial (the PI, 2026-10-30, Q3, "Per drawn setting, required"), `None` until the author
    says, which the load refuses. **Not refused as built** (call 2): a draw that cannot be drawn
    is a finding at load with a sentence, never a task file that will not import."""
    drawn = {
        Uniform: (Uniform(0.2, 0.4), ("low", "high", "repeat")),
        Weighted: (Weighted((0.1, 0.5), (3, 1)), ("values", "weights", "repeat")),
        TruncatedNormal: (TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1), ("mean", "sd", "low", "high", "repeat")),
        Listed: (Listed((2, 4, 6)), ("values", "in_order", "repeat")),
        NonAging: (NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25), ("minimum", "mean", "maximum", "repeat")),
    }

    assert dataclasses.fields(Distribution) == ()
    for kind, (distribution, names) in drawn.items():
        assert type(distribution) is kind and isinstance(distribution, Distribution)
        assert tuple(spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(kind)) == names
        assert distribution.repeat is None
        with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
            distribution.repeat = SAME
    assert (SAME, FRESH, REPEATS) == ("same", "fresh", ("same", "fresh"))
    assert (TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1).low, TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1).high) == (None, None)
    assert Listed((2, 4, 6)).in_order is False
    assert Uniform(0.2, 0.4, repeat=FRESH).repeat == FRESH
    assert NonAging(minimum=0.75, mean=1.0, maximum=1.25, repeat=SAME) == NonAging(
        0.75, 1.0, 1.25, SAME)
    assert Uniform(0.4, 0.2).low == 0.4 and Weighted((0.1,), (0, 0)).weights == (0, 0)


def test_a_task_and_a_block_declare_draws_and_a_block_a_factorial():
    """Where a draw is written (the PI, 2026-10-30, Q1a, "Task default, block may replace"): the
    task's `draws`, the plain run included, which a block type's own `draws` replaces or, for a
    setting its conditions give, marks `BY_CONDITIONS`; a condition may draw its own setting from
    its own range (Q1b). A block may make conditions from factors (TSK-22), a level a value of its
    setting or its own range. Every new field closes its class, at a default."""
    wait = NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25, repeat=FRESH)
    own = Condition("wide", {"fix_hold": Uniform(0.5, 0.9, repeat=SAME)}, target=5)
    factorial = Factorial(
        {"contrast": (0.1, 0.5), "fix_hold": (0.3, TruncatedNormal(0.6, 0.1, repeat=SAME))},
        exclude=({"contrast": 0.1, "fix_hold": 0.3},),
        target=4,
        targets={"contrast=0.5, fix_hold=0.3": 8},
        structure="wait",
    )
    block = Block("mixed", [own], draws={"wait": wait, "fix_hold": BY_CONDITIONS},
                  factorial=factorial)
    task = _task(draws={"wait": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH)}, plans={"one": Plan([block])})

    assert task.draws == {"wait": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH)}
    assert task.plans["one"].blocks[0].draws == {"wait": wait, "fix_hold": BY_CONDITIONS}
    assert task.plans["one"].blocks[0].factorial is factorial
    assert own.values["fix_hold"] == Uniform(0.5, 0.9, repeat=SAME)
    assert BY_CONDITIONS == "by conditions"
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(Factorial)] == [
        "factors", "exclude", "target", "targets", "structure"]
    assert Factorial({"contrast": (0.1, 0.5)}) == Factorial(
        {"contrast": (0.1, 0.5)}, (), 1, {}, None)
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(Block)][-4:] == [
        "trials", "time_limit_s", "draws", "factorial"]
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(Task)][-2:] == ["plans", "draws"]
    plain = Block("plain", [own])
    assert (plain.draws, plain.factorial, _task().draws) == ({}, None, {})
    assert plain.draws is not Block("other", []).draws


def test_the_designed_orders_are_a_blocks_condition_orders():
    """Sequence-balanced (TSK-23; the PI, 2026-10-30, Q5a, "Block picks; pairs default") and
    priming (Q6, "Both of the last two") order a block's conditions, beside `Shuffled`, so a plan
    cannot take either as its order of blocks; named apart from the plan orders `Balanced` and
    `Random`. No repeat on a break by default (TSK-31); "again at once" is the block's to choose
    (Q5b)."""
    balanced = SequenceBalanced()
    priming = Priming("contrast", chance=0.7)

    assert isinstance(balanced, Order) and isinstance(priming, Order)
    assert not isinstance(balanced, BlockOrder) and not isinstance(priming, BlockOrder)
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(SequenceBalanced)] == [
        "depth", "cycles", "again_at_once"]
    assert (balanced.depth, balanced.cycles, balanced.again_at_once) == (2, 1, False)
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(Priming)] == [
        "feature", "chance", "runs", "again_at_once"]
    assert (priming.feature, priming.chance, priming.runs, priming.again_at_once) == (
        "contrast", 0.7, None, False)
    block = Block("primed", [Condition("dim", {"contrast": 0.1}, target=0)],
                  order=Priming("contrast", runs=(3, 7), again_at_once=True), trials=200)
    assert block.order == Priming("contrast", None, (3, 7), True)
    assert Block("pairs", [], order=SequenceBalanced(depth=3, cycles=2)).order.cycles == 2
    assert Block("plain", []).order == Shuffled()
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="a plan's order is a BlockOrder"):
        Plan([], order=SequenceBalanced())


def test_an_array_says_what_names_its_target_its_look_by_default():
    """The PI, 2026-10-31, on the engine C3 plan's Appendix B, item 17, "Refuse only odd-one-out
    tasks (Recommended)": an array says what tells the animal which of its objects is the target
    (`found_by`, one of `FOUND_BY`). **Its look, by default** (`"look"`): the target is the odd
    one out, as in a pop-out search, which the load's two look checks hold it to. **A cue**
    (`"cue"`): something else the trial shows names it -- a cue, a remembered sample, a place --
    as in a cued two-choice design, whose target may look like its distractors. At its default it
    is left out of what the hash reads, so every task that shows an array hashes as before; a cued
    array's hash moves."""
    assert FOUND_BY == ("look", "cue")
    assert [spec.name for spec in dataclasses.fields(Array)][-1] == "found_by"
    assert Array().found_by == "look"
    cued = Array(n=2, found_by="cue")
    assert (cued.n, cued.found_by) == (2, "cue")
    with pytest.raises(dataclasses.FrozenInstanceError):
        cued.found_by = "look"
    assert "found_by" not in canonical(Array(n=2))["fields"]
    assert canonical(cued)["fields"]["found_by"] == "cue"
    assert canonical(cued) != canonical(Array(n=2))
    for name in ("visual_search", "visual_search_training"):
        assert "found_by" not in str(canonical(_load_task(ROOT / "tasks" / f"{name}.py")))


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    ("draws", "said"),
    [
        ([("wait", Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH))], "a dict of setting names to Distributions"),
        ({"": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH)}, "names its setting by text, not ''"),
        ({3: Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH)}, "names its setting by text, not 3"),
        ({"wait": (0.8, 1.2)}, r"draw 'wait' is a Distribution \(.*\), not tuple"),
        ({"wait": BY_CONDITIONS}, r"draw 'wait' is a Distribution \(.*\), not str"),
        ({"wait": Shuffled()}, r"draw 'wait' is a Distribution \(.*\), not Shuffled"),
    ],
)
def test_a_tasks_draws_are_refused_as_built_unless_settings_to_distributions(draws, said):
    """Call 2: a task's draws are a dict of settings, by name, to `Distribution`s, refused as built
    otherwise, as its meanings and plans are. `BY_CONDITIONS` is a block's word, never the task's.
    What a draw declares is the load's to judge (`check.check_task`)."""
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=said):
        _task(draws=draws)


def test_a_task_that_draws_hashes_apart_and_one_that_does_not_keeps_its_hash():
    """Each new declaration changes what a run of the task is, so each moves the content hash. At
    its default each is left out (`declarations.canonical`), so a task that draws nothing and a
    block declaring neither draws nor factors hash as before the fields existed -- every reference
    task among them -- and `declarations.FORMAT` stays 1."""
    near = Condition("near", {"contrast": 0.5}, target=4)

    def of(**fields) -> str:
        return content_hash(_task(**fields))

    def block(**fields) -> str:
        return of(plans={"one": Plan([Block("b", [near], **fields)])})

    two = {"fix_hold": (0.3, 0.6)}
    variants = [
        of(),
        of(draws={"wait": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=FRESH)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Uniform(0.8, 1.3, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"fix_hold": Uniform(0.8, 1.2, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Weighted((0.8, 1.2), (1, 1), repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Weighted((0.8, 1.2), (1, 3), repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1, low=0.9, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": TruncatedNormal(1.0, 0.1, high=1.1, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Listed((0.8, 1.2), repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": Listed((0.8, 1.2), in_order=True, repeat=SAME)}),
        of(draws={"wait": NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25, repeat=SAME)}),
        block(),
        block(draws={"wait": NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25, repeat=FRESH)}),
        block(draws={"contrast": BY_CONDITIONS}),
        block(factorial=Factorial(two)),
        block(factorial=Factorial(two, exclude=({"fix_hold": 0.3},))),
        block(factorial=Factorial(two, target=2)),
        block(factorial=Factorial(two, targets={"fix_hold=0.6": 3})),
        block(factorial=Factorial(two, structure="wait")),
        block(factorial=Factorial({"fix_hold": (0.3, Uniform(0.5, 0.7, repeat=SAME))})),
        block(order=SequenceBalanced()),
        block(order=SequenceBalanced(depth=3)),
        block(order=SequenceBalanced(cycles=2)),
        block(order=SequenceBalanced(again_at_once=True)),
        block(order=Priming("contrast", chance=0.7)),
        block(order=Priming("contrast", chance=0.6)),
        block(order=Priming("contrast", runs=(3, 7))),
        block(order=Priming("contrast", runs=(3, 7), again_at_once=True)),
        of(plans={"one": Plan([Block("b", [dataclasses.replace(
            near, values={"contrast": Uniform(0.1, 0.9, repeat=SAME)})])])}),
    ]

    assert len(set(variants)) == len(variants) == 31
    assert of(draws={}) == of() == content_hash(_task())
    assert block(draws={}, factorial=None) == block()
    written = canonical(_task(plans={"one": Plan([Block("b", [near])])}))
    assert "draws" not in written["fields"]
    assert set(written["fields"]["plans"]["one"]["fields"]["blocks"][0]["fields"]) == {
        "name", "conditions"}
    for name in ("fixation_detection", "adaptive_detection", "visual_search",
                 "visual_search_training", "calibration"):
        assert "draws" not in canonical(_load_task(ROOT / "tasks" / f"{name}.py"))["fields"]
```
