`docs/references/decisions.md`: insert

```markdown
### TSK-65 — A sequence-balanced block plays a de Bruijn cycle of its conditions to a depth the block picks, pairs by default; the block ends when its cycles are played out or its number of trials is run, owing nothing then
- **Decided:** 2026-10-30, the PI, in engine build C3's brainstorm: Q5a, "Block picks; pairs default (Recommended)" -- pairs, each condition following each, itself included, once per cycle (n squared trials; four conditions, 16), or triples (n cubed; 64). And 2026-10-31, on the engine C3 plan's Appendix B, item 1, "Add one closing trial (Recommended)" -- each cycle is played as the linear de Bruijn sequence, n to the depth plus depth minus 1 trials (17 for four conditions at pairs, 66 at triples), so every pair (every triple) is shown once per cycle; its first depth minus 1 trials are a lead-in that only precedes what follows, and each such trial's line marks it (`planned`'s `lead_in`) so an analysis can drop it. Q5b, "'Again at once' as an option (Recommended)" -- a break in the sequence repeats nothing by default (TSK-31), and a block may choose that the broken trial come straight back. That the cycle is picked from the run's seed as a random Euler circuit through the conditions, drawn again each time the block opens by a generator apart from the one ordinary draws and repeats share; that the block ends when its cycles are played out or its number of trials is run, whichever comes first, owing nothing more; that a trial count or time limit may cut a cycle short and the record says so; that the lost transition is recorded as a shortfall `because` `"designed"`; and that a trial brought back at once is moved past after the task's repeat limit, as any repeat is, are engineering (the C3 spec §5, call 14; the engine C3 plan's review, I-3 and I-4, and its Appendix B, items 7 and 9, which the PI confirmed as built on 2026-10-31).
- **Where:** [the C3 spec §5](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#5-designed-orders); [`wl_xcon/task.py`](../../wl_xcon/task.py) (`Balanced` is a block order's name; the designed order is `SequenceBalanced(depth=2, cycles=1)`); [`wl_xcon/variation.py`](../../wl_xcon/variation.py) (`balanced_sequence`); [`wl_xcon/scheduler.py`](../../wl_xcon/scheduler.py) (`Scheduler.next_trial`, `record`, `planned`, `DESIGNED`); TSK-23, TSK-31.
- **Basis:** PI decision, on published methods. [@aguirre2011de] -- de Bruijn cycles as pseudo-random stimulus sequences with arbitrary levels of counterbalance (abstract); [@brooks2012counterbalancing] -- counterbalanced sequences come from Euler circuits through a graph of conditions (abstract). That a depth-k de Bruijn cycle of n conditions has n to the k trials, and its linear sequence n to the k plus k minus 1, is arithmetic. The cost of "again at once" is the one the PI turned down for ordinary blocks (TSK-30): breaking brings the display straight back [@nimhmonkeylogic2026task] ("On error"). A serially balanced sequence has each condition precede and follow every other [@aguirre2007continuous] (abstract), as the linear sequence does within each cycle, where a cycle of n squared trials falls one transition short in its last; that its type 1 index 1 sequences are n squared plus one trials long is UNVERIFIED here (full text not reached).

### TSK-66 — A priming block repeats a named setting's value with a set chance, interleaved, or in runs of drawn length, then switches; block swaps stay plan block types
- **Decided:** 2026-10-30, the PI, in engine build C3's brainstorm: Q6, "Both of the last two" -- within one block, on a setting it names (its `feature`, such as the target's color), either a set chance that the next trial repeats the last one's value, interleaved, or runs of one value whose lengths are drawn (for example 3 to 7), then a switch. His own block-swap design (2020) stays a plan block type, as built in C2b. That a switch picks another value at random, that within a value the conditions are shuffled, that "last" is the last trial whose stimulus appeared and a run counts only those, that a break therefore loses no place and writes no shortfall, and that the block ends on its trial count or time, are engineering (the C3 spec §5; the engine C3 plan's call 16, its review, M-9, and its Appendix B, item 6, for the PI to confirm).
- **Where:** [the C3 spec §5](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#5-designed-orders); [`wl_xcon/task.py`](../../wl_xcon/task.py) (`Priming`); [`wl_xcon/scheduler.py`](../../wl_xcon/scheduler.py) (`Scheduler._planned_next`, `_move_on`, `_new_run`, `_run_length`); TSK-23, TSK-31, TSK-25.
- **Basis:** PI decision, on published findings. In priming of pop-out the previous trial's features and target position change performance [@bichot2002priming] (abstract); the PI's own 2020 design held the target color constant in blocks, then swapped it [@westerberg2020priming] (Materials and Methods). No paper in the library describes building interleaved or run-length priming sequences. Priming of pop-out builds over the trials after a repeat, laid down with each trial [@maljkovic1994priming] (abstract), so a run counts each trial whose display appeared, and run lengths drawn evenly make a switch ever more expected along a run, which a non-aging draw of lengths avoids (the engine C3 plan's science review, I-8).

```

- [ ] **Step 6: Prove they can fail**

Nothing is committed until Step 7, so copy the module aside first (`cp wl_xcon/scheduler.py <scratch>/scheduler.py`), **never `git checkout -- <file>`**, which would put back the base and lose the work. Apply each break alone, clear `__pycache__`, run `cd <worktree> && PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 $PY -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_designed_orders.py`, then restore byte for byte (`cp <scratch>/scheduler.py wl_xcon/scheduler.py && cmp <scratch>/scheduler.py wl_xcon/scheduler.py`) and clear `__pycache__` again. Each must read `N failed`, never an error. Every break is in `wl_xcon/scheduler.py`; the fuzz is ten cases, each counted on its own, so a break it catches adds up to ten to the count.

- **B-I8a**, a run's length drawn from its distribution (revision round 1, the plan's science review's I-8): `        return run_length(runs, self._design.random())` → `        return run_length(runs, 0.0)` -- `test_priming_runs_drawn_from_a_distribution_play_their_drawn_lengths` fails (every non-aging length 2): `1 failed`.
- **B-I8b**, a distribution's length used: `        return group, self._run_length(order.runs)` → `        return group, 3` -- the same test: `1 failed`.
- **B-I8c**, a list's pass shuffled: `                if not runs.in_order:` → `                if False:` -- the same test (passes in listed order): `1 failed`.
- **B-I8d**, a list's whole pass: `                self._lengths.extend(items)` → `                self._lengths.extend(items[:1])` -- the same test: `1 failed`.
- **B1**, the designed generator apart from the ordinary one: `        self._design = random.Random(f"design:{self.seed}:{len(self.ended)}")` → `        self._design = self._rng` -- `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_plays_each_cycle_as_the_linear_sequence_every_pair_once`, `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_survives_a_drum_a_move_back_and_its_time`, `test_an_ordinary_blocks_draws_are_as_the_seed_gave_them` (an ordinary block after a designed one draws other conditions) and `test_priming_by_chance_repeats_at_its_rate_and_every_switch_changes_the_value` fail: `4 failed`.
- **B2**, each opening its own plan: `f"design:{self.seed}:{len(self.ended)}"` → `f"design:{self.seed}:0"` -- `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_survives_a_drum_a_move_back_and_its_time` fails (the reopened block replays its first plan): `1 failed`.
- **B3**, a cycle's places: `            position = place % self._cycle` → `            position = place` -- `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_plays_each_cycle_as_the_linear_sequence_every_pair_once`, `test_a_sequence_balanced_block_survives_a_drum_a_move_back_and_its_time` and the fuzz fail: `12 failed`.

### Task 7: The change log and resume (closes XC-363)

XC-288 §3.4 (approved 2026-10-10; told to the PI 2026-10-30, E11): **`parameter_changes.jsonl` grows into one log of every change to what the animal experiences**, one row for each setting an act moves, of one of seven kinds (`record.KINDS`). This task builds the log, its first kind and the three kinds C2a writes as control rows; Tasks 13 and 14 add the rest through the same writer.
- **The writer.** `SessionRecord.change` replaces `parameter_change` (its one caller and its one test move). Each row carries `change` (from 1, never 0: the controller's ruling from Task 3's draft), `kind`, `name` (never empty: ruling 3), `was`, `now`, `by`, `at` and `at_local`, `trial_number` (the first trial it applies to, equal to that trial's line's: the same ruling), `run`, `meaning`, `offered` (empty), `odds` (null), `event_code`, a kind's own fields, and **`sequence` on the four kinds that strobe `PARAM_CHANGED` alone** (`record.STROBED`; Call 21). It refuses, with `ValueError` and before the file is opened, a row its readers would refuse: a kind outside `KINDS`, a `sequence` on a kind outside `STROBED` or none on one inside it, an empty `name`, a change id that is not a whole number from 1. No input reaches those: every caller passes its own literal kind and the session's own counters.
- **A person's value** (`_apply_staged`, Call 19's first step): each `_staged` row takes its own change id, assigned where it applies and never in `Session.set` (spec §14 item 4), strobes `PARAM_CHANGED` once with its `sequence`, and is written kind `set`, with the setting's meaning (`Session._meaning`: the resolved meaning, `went` and `step`), then its line on the feed at the same instant. A bounded row still goes through `bounds.set` in the same pass. **Values are written as given** (the controller's ruling from Task 3's draft, on the PI's "Warn at load", 2026-10-30, overriding Call 11's and Record shapes' normalized change rows): a person's -90 for a direction setting is -90 in `was`/`now`, as in `params`.
- **The clears and the two switches** (XC-363; controller ruling 3): `_clear`, `_drum` and `_train` write their control row to `controls.jsonl` exactly as C2a does, and a change row beside it (`Session._logged`) at the control row's instant, named `"owed"`, `"drumming"` or the training setting, with no meaning and no `sequence`. Both until wl-preproc reads and times the log's rows (XC-B, Task 3's). **The path, not the piece:** wl-preproc's own reader (`wl_preproc/events/rigrecords.read_rig_records`, through the worktree's `wl-preproc` link) takes every row a session writes with no problem, `sequence` on the strobed one alone.
- **Resume** (Call 21; review M-6): `resume._read` reads every kind through a new `_changes`, which fails closed (`Unresumable`, naming the row) on a row of an unknown kind, a row of a strobed kind or with no kind that has no whole-number `sequence`, and a `change` that is not a whole number from 1. It sorts and maxes `sequence` over strobed and kindless rows only, reads bounded values from `set` and kindless rows only, and fills **`Restoration.change`** with the largest change id, which `Session.resume` restores into `Session._change`. A row written before C3 has no `kind` and is a `set`: `tests/test_resume.py` writes only such rows and passes unedited, which pins that.
- **The ledger the later tasks read:** `Session._run_values` (the task's starts under the run's given, per run) and `Session._ranges` (empty per run until Task 13 fills it). **No `Session._directions`** (the controller's ruling on this task's draft): once change rows are written as given, nothing reads it, and Task 10, which normalizes drawn directions, builds what it needs itself.

**Files:**
- Modify: `wl_xcon/record.py` (`WELFARE_NOTES`' and `CONTROLS`' comments; `KINDS` and `STROBED` after `CONTROLS`; `SessionRecord.change` replaces `parameter_change`; `refusal`'s docstring)
- Modify: `wl_xcon/resume.py` (its `record` import; `Restoration.change`; `_whole` and `_changes` before `_accepted`; `_read`: `_changes`, `strobed`, bounded values from `set` rows, `sequence`, `change`)
- Modify: `wl_xcon/taskd.py` (imports; `Session._change`; `resume`; `_clear`, `_drum`, `_train`; `_apply_staged`; new `_meaning` and `_logged` after it; `_run_values` and `_ranges` after `_declared`; `run`'s per-run resets)
- Modify (docs): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-10-xc288-training-records-design.md` (§3.4, a dated note); `docs/backlog.md` (XC-363 removed)

**Interfaces:**

The outline's `variation.directions` is not consumed here (no `Session._directions`, above), nor its `variation.recorded`: the rows this task writes hold a person's values and the controls' values, as given; Tasks 13 and 14 write `range` and `revert` rows through it.

Its row's keys: `change`, `kind`, `name`, `was`, `now`, `by`, `at`, `at_local`, `trial_number`, `run`, `meaning`, `offered` (`[]`), `odds` (`null`), `event_code`, `sequence` where given, and `detail` as given (written with sorted keys). A range row's `from` is passed as `**{"from": ...}`.

Task 13 adds its `_pending` branch here.

```python
        "meaning", "offered", "odds", "event_code", "sequence"}


def _spec(tmp_path, **over) -> SessionSpec:
    spec = SessionSpec(
        task=TASK, allocation="tasks/allocation.py", root=tmp_path, session_id="2027-01-14_01",
        subject="A", trials=3, frame_period=1 / 240, seed=1, values=dict(VALUES),
        bounds=Bounds(
            subject="A",
            ceilings={"reward_correct": Ceiling(value=0.15, maximum=0.40, unit="mL"),
                      "out_of_cage": Ceiling(value=800.0, maximum=100_000.0, unit="s")},
            minima={"daily_fluid": Floor(value=250.0, unit="mL")},
        ),
        already_delivered_today=0.0, deployment=Deployment.RIG_FIXED, geometry=DIRECT,
        session_kind="training", calibration=SRGB,
    )
    for name, value in over.items():
        setattr(spec, name, value)
    return spec


def _session(spec, link=None, *, service=False) -> Session:
    """On the simulators, its wall following its frames from `WALL_NOW`, the animal out of its
    cage and its head fixed then, as `tests/test_taskd.py`'s sessions are; a `wlx taskd` one
    opened."""
    session = Session(spec, card=Card(), pump=Pump(),
                      link=link if link is not None else Simulated(), service=service)
    session.wall_clock = lambda: WALL_NOW + session.now()
    session.left_cage(at=WALL_NOW)
    session.head_fixed(at=session.wall_now())
    if service:
        session.open(how="wlx taskd")
    return session


class _Drained(Simulated):
    """A link that queues `script[n]` as the `n`th drain begins: the commands reach the loop at
    the boundary before trial `n`."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        super().__init__()
        self.script, self.drains = dict(script), 0

    def drain(self) -> list:
        self.drains += 1
        for command in self.script.get(self.drains, ()):
            self.queue(command)
        return super().drain()


def _rows(session: Session, name: str) -> list[dict]:
    return [json.loads(line) for line in (session.directory / name).read_text().splitlines()]


def _without_instants(row: dict) -> dict:
    return {key: value for key, value in row.items() if key not in ("at", "at_local")}


def test_a_persons_value_writes_a_set_row_with_every_key_and_its_first_trial(tmp_path):
    """XC-288 §3.4: the row's `change` id, from 1; when it applied, at the instant its line on
    the changes feed names; the first trial it applies to, numbered as that trial's line; the
    setting's meaning, with the way it went and its step; `offered` empty and `odds` null; and
    the `sequence` its strobe joins it by."""
    link = _Drained({1: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=Box("jake"))]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path), link)

    session.run()

    (row,) = _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")
    assert set(row) == KEYS
    assert _without_instants(row) == {
        "change": 1, "kind": "set", "name": "fix_hold", "was": 0.3, "now": 0.5, "by": JAKE,
        "trial_number": 2, "run": 0,
        "meaning": {"kind": "clear-cut", "role": "criterion", "raising": "harder",
                    "relative_to": None, "went": "harder", "step": pytest.approx(0.2)},
        "offered": [], "odds": None, "event_code": 4130, "sequence": 1,
    }
    lines = _rows(session, "trials.jsonl")
    assert [(line["trial_number"], line["params"]["fix_hold"]) for line in lines] == [
        (1, 0.3), (2, 0.5), (3, 0.5)], "its first trial is the line its trial_number names"
    (fed,) = [at for kind, _, at, _ in session.controls if kind == "set"]
    assert (row["at"], row["at_local"]) == (fed, _local(fed))


def _near_far() -> Block:
    return Block(name="b", conditions=[Condition("near", {"target_x": 5.0}, target=4),
                                       Condition("far", {"target_x": 12.0}, target=4)])


def _switched(tmp_path) -> Session:
    """A run in which, before its first trial, a trainer switches the training aid *clear* on,
    clears one trial of `near` and switches drumming on for the run; and in which a person sets
    `fix_hold` before its second, applied from its third."""
    link = _Drained({1: [Training(setting="clear", on=True, by=Box("jake")),
                         ClearOwed(condition="near", by=Box("jake")),
                         Drum(scope="run", by=Box("jake"))],
                     2: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=Box("jake"))]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, trials=400, blocks=[_near_far()]), link)
    session.run()
    return session


def test_a_clear_a_drum_switch_and_a_training_switch_are_written_to_both_files(tmp_path):
    """XC-363, and the C3 ask (`docs/pending-wl-preproc-amendments.md`): each is a control row in
    `controls.jsonl` exactly as engine build C2a writes it, and a change row of its own kind
    beside it, at the same instant, its `name` what it moved, no meaning and no `sequence`: it
    strobes nothing. A person's value after them takes the next change id, and the first
    `sequence`."""
    session = _switched(tmp_path)

    controls = [row for row in _rows(session, "controls.jsonl")
                if row["kind"] in ("training", "clear", "drum")]
    first = {"by": JAKE, "trial_index": 0, "event_code": None, "run": 0}
    assert [_without_instants(row) for row in controls] == [
        {**first, "kind": "training", "setting": "clear", "was": False, "now": True},
        {**first, "kind": "clear", "condition": "near", "block": "b", "rest": False,
         "cleared": 1, "owed": 3},
        {**first, "kind": "drum", "scope": "run", "block": "b", "was": None, "now": "run"},
    ], "the control rows exactly as engine build C2a writes them"
    changes = _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")
    common = {"by": JAKE, "trial_number": 1, "run": 0, "meaning": None, "offered": [],
              "odds": None, "event_code": None}
    assert [_without_instants(row) for row in changes[:3]] == [
        {**common, "change": 1, "kind": "training", "name": "clear", "was": False, "now": True,
         "setting": "clear"},
        {**common, "change": 2, "kind": "clear", "name": "owed", "was": 4, "now": 3,
         "condition": "near", "block": "b", "rest": False, "cleared": 1},
        {**common, "change": 3, "kind": "drum", "name": "drumming", "was": None, "now": "run",
         "scope": "run", "block": "b"},
    ]
    assert [(row["at"], row["at_local"]) for row in changes[:3]] == [
        (row["at"], row["at_local"]) for row in controls]
    (person,) = changes[3:]
    first_at = next(line["trial_number"] for line in _rows(session, "trials.jsonl")
                    if line["params"]["fix_hold"] == 0.5)
    assert (person["kind"], person["change"], person["sequence"], person["trial_number"]) == (
        "set", 4, 1, first_at)


def _their_reader():
    """wl-preproc's reader of these rows (`wl_preproc/events/rigrecords.py`), or a skip where its
    checkout is absent -- a failure under `WLX_REQUIRE_PREPROC=1`, which CI sets, as
    `tests/test_taskd.py` guards its assembler."""
    try:
        from wl_preproc.events.rigrecords import read_rig_records
    except ImportError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - exercised by the CI job
        if os.environ.get("WLX_REQUIRE_PREPROC") == "1":
            raise AssertionError(
                f"WLX_REQUIRE_PREPROC=1 but wl-preproc is not importable ({exc})") from exc
        pytest.skip("wl-preproc checkout not beside this repo")
    return read_rig_records


def test_wl_preprocs_reader_takes_every_change_row_and_its_strobed_ones_sequence(tmp_path):
    """The path, not the piece (the C3 ask: "Every row names something in `name`", since
    wl-preproc's reader leaves out a row that does not): its reader takes the clear's, the
    switches' and the person's rows with no problem, `sequence` on the one that strobed alone."""
    read_rig_records = _their_reader()
    session = _switched(tmp_path)

    records = read_rig_records(session.directory.parent)

    assert records.problems == ()
    assert [(change.name, change.sequence) for change in records.changes] == [
        ("clear", None), ("owed", None), ("drumming", None), ("fix_hold", 1)]


def test_two_changes_in_one_drain_each_take_an_id_and_strobe_once_in_order(tmp_path):
    """Engine build C3's spec §8 ("a `change` id ... one per revert"; a person's value is an act
    of its own): two values drained in one pass apply at one boundary, each its own change id and
    `sequence` in the order offered, each strobing `PARAM_CHANGED` once, back to back; a
    ceiling's row names no task setting, so it writes no meaning."""
    link = _Drained({1: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=Box("jake")),
                         SetParameter(name="reward_correct", value=0.2, by=Box("sam"))]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path), link)

    session.run()

    changes = _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")
    assert [(row["change"], row["sequence"], row["name"], row["trial_number"], row["by"]["name"])
            for row in changes] == [(1, 1, "fix_hold", 2, "jake"),
                                    (2, 2, "reward_correct", 2, "sam")]
    assert changes[1]["meaning"] is None
    codes = session.card.codes
    first = codes.index(4130)
    assert codes.count(4130) == 2 and codes[first + 1] == 4130


def test_a_rows_meaning_says_which_way_it_went_and_its_step(tmp_path):
    """XC-288 §3.4 and §4.1 (TRN-03): the setting's declared meaning, `relative_to` as written,
    the way the change went by it and its step. A choice has no order (TRN-11), so a change goes
    the way its `raising` says, whichever way it moved; a meaning relative to another setting
    reads that setting's value; the background cannot be read here, nor anything for a setting
    that is not a difficulty setting; a ceiling's name is no task setting."""
    task = _load_task(Path(TASK))
    detection = task.structures["detection"]
    extra = [Param("cue_size", unit="deg", choices=(1.0, 2.0)),
             Param("guide_x", unit="deg", low=-16.0, high=16.0, start=0.0)]
    task = dataclasses.replace(
        task,
        structures={"detection": dataclasses.replace(detection,
                                                     params=[*detection.params, *extra])},
        meanings={"cue_size": Meaning(CLEAR_CUT, STIMULUS, raising=EASIER),
                  "guide_x": Meaning(CLEAR_CUT, STIMULUS, raising=EASIER, relative_to="target_x")},
    )
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path))
    session._take(task)
    meaning = session._meaning
    disc, square = next(p for p in task.params if p.name == "target_appearance").choices

    assert meaning("fix_hold", 0.3, 0.5) == {
        "kind": "clear-cut", "role": "criterion", "raising": "harder", "relative_to": None,
        "went": "harder", "step": pytest.approx(0.2)}
    assert [meaning("fix_hold", 0.5, 0.3)["went"], meaning("fix_window", 2.0, 3.0)["went"],
            meaning("fix_window", 2.0, 2.0)["went"]] == ["easier", "easier", None]
    assert (meaning("fix_hold", None, 0.5)["went"], meaning("fix_hold", None, 0.5)["step"]) == (
        None, None)
    luminance = meaning("target_luminance", 40.0, 60.0)
    assert (luminance["kind"], luminance["relative_to"], luminance["went"], luminance["step"]) == (
        "expected", "background", None, 20.0)
    assert meaning("target_x", 10.0, -10.0) == {
        "kind": "not a difficulty setting", "role": "stimulus", "raising": None,
        "relative_to": None, "went": None, "step": -20.0}
    assert (meaning("target_appearance", disc, square)["went"],
            meaning("target_appearance", disc, square)["step"]) == (None, None)
    assert [meaning("cue_size", 2.0, 1.0)["went"], meaning("cue_size", 1.0, 2.0)["went"]] == [
        "easier", "easier"]
    assert meaning("guide_x", 8.0, 4.0)["relative_to"] == "target_x"
    assert [meaning("guide_x", 8.0, 4.0)["went"], meaning("guide_x", 4.0, 8.0)["went"],
            meaning("guide_x", 8.0, 12.0)["went"]] == ["easier", "harder", None]
    assert meaning("reward_correct", 0.15, 0.2) is None


def _direction_task(folder: Path) -> Path:
    """The reference detection task with its target 8° out at a direction, `target_dir`, declared
    from -180 to 180 (`task.Polar`), written into `folder` as `direction.py`. Engine test material,
    run only in the simulator: no reference task places a target by a direction setting."""
    text = Path(TASK).read_text()
    for old, new in (
        ('"target", at=(P("target_x"), P("target_y")), looks=P("target_appearance")',
         '"target", at=Polar(8.0, P("target_dir")), looks=P("target_appearance")'),
        ('            at=(P("target_x"), P("target_y")),\n            radius=P("target_window"),',
         '            at=Polar(8.0, P("target_dir")),\n            radius=P("target_window"),'),
        ('        Param("target_x", unit="deg", low=-16.0, high=16.0, start=10.0),',
         '        Param("target_dir", unit="deg", low=-180.0, high=180.0, start=90.0),\n'
         '        Param("target_x", unit="deg", low=-16.0, high=16.0, start=10.0),'),
        ("from wl_xcon.task import (", "from wl_xcon.task import (\n    Polar,"),
    ):
        assert text.count(old) == 1, old
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    text += (
        "\n\nimport dataclasses as _direction_dataclasses\n"
        "from wl_xcon.task import NOT_DIFFICULTY, STIMULUS, Meaning\n"
        "TASK = _direction_dataclasses.replace(TASK, meanings={\n"
        "    'target_dir': Meaning(NOT_DIFFICULTY, STIMULUS, note='where the target is'),\n"
        "})\n"
    )
    path = Path(folder) / "direction.py"
    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path.write_text(text)
    return path


def test_a_persons_direction_is_written_as_given_in_its_change_row(tmp_path):
    """The PI, 2026-10-30, "Warn at load": a setting's number is shown and recorded as the number
    it holds, and only a value the rig draws is normalized when written (the C3 ask). A person's
    -90 for a direction setting is -90 in its change row's `now`, as in the trials' `params`."""
    task = _direction_task(tmp_path / "tasks")
    link = _Drained({1: [SetParameter(name="target_dir", value=-90.0, by=Box("jake"))]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, task=str(task), values={**VALUES, "target_dir": 90.0}),
                       link)

    session.run()

    (row,) = _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")
    assert (row["was"], row["now"], row["meaning"]["step"]) == (90.0, -90.0, -180.0)
    assert [line["params"]["target_dir"] for line in _rows(session, "trials.jsonl")] == [
        90.0, -90.0, -90.0]


def test_a_change_row_its_readers_would_refuse_is_never_written(tmp_path):
    """The record's side of resume's refusal: a kind the rig does not write, a `sequence` where
    the kind strobes nothing or none where it strobes `PARAM_CHANGED`, a row naming nothing
    (wl-preproc leaves one out), and a change id that is not a whole number from 1 are each
    refused before the file is opened."""
    assert record.KINDS == ("set", "hand_back", "range", "revert", "clear", "drum", "training")
    assert record.STROBED == ("set", "hand_back", "range", "revert")
    log = SessionRecord.open(tmp_path, "2027-01-14_01", "A")
    good = dict(change=1, kind="set", name="fix_hold", was=0.3, now=0.5, by=Box("jake"),
                at=WALL_NOW, trial_number=1, run=0, meaning=None, event_code=4130, sequence=1)
    for over, said in (({"kind": "preset"}, "kind is one of"),
                       ({"sequence": None}, "carries a sequence exactly when"),
                       ({"kind": "clear", "event_code": None}, "carries a sequence exactly when"),
                       ({"name": ""}, "names nothing"),
                       ({"change": 0}, "whole number from 1"),
                       ({"change": True}, "whole number from 1")):
        with pytest.raises(ValueError, match=said):
            log.change(**{**good, **over})
    assert not (log.directory / "parameter_changes.jsonl").exists()
    log.change(**good)
    log.change(**{**good, "change": 2, "kind": "drum", "name": "drumming", "was": None,
                  "now": "run", "by": None, "event_code": None, "sequence": None,
                  "scope": "run", "block": "b"})
    rows = [json.loads(line) for line in
            (log.directory / "parameter_changes.jsonl").read_text().splitlines()]
    assert set(rows[0]) == KEYS
    assert set(rows[1]) == KEYS - {"sequence"} | {"scope", "block"}
    assert (rows[1]["by"], rows[1]["at_local"]) == (None, _local(WALL_NOW))


def test_each_run_keeps_its_own_values_and_starts_with_no_live_range(tmp_path):
    """The run's own values are the task's starts under what the run was given, before any live
    edit; a draw changed live is the run's alone (engine build C3's spec §6); the change ids go on
    across runs, as `sequence` does."""
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, task="", trials=0, values={}), service=True)
    session.link.queue(SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=Box("jake")))

    session.run(RunSpec(task=TASK, trials=3, seed=2, values={"fix_window": 3.0}))

    assert session._run_values == {**STARTS, "fix_window": 3.0}
    assert session.spec.values["fix_hold"] == 0.5
    # As a live range would leave it (`Session._range`, the C3 plan's Task 13).
    session._ranges[("task", "fix_hold")] = (Uniform(0.2, 0.4, repeat=FRESH), 1)
    session.link.queue(SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.6, by=Box("jake")))
    session.run(RunSpec(task=TASK, trials=3, seed=2, values={}))

    assert (session._run_values, session._ranges) == (STARTS, {})
    assert [(row["change"], row["sequence"], row["run"])
            for row in _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")] == [(1, 1, 0), (2, 2, 1)]


#: A change row as the rig writes one, whole: what each damage below starts from.
_WHOLE = {"change": 10, "kind": "set", "name": "fix_hold", "was": 0.4, "now": 0.5, "by": JAKE,
          "at": WALL_NOW + 600.0, "at_local": "", "trial_number": 12, "run": 0, "meaning": None,
          "offered": [], "odds": None, "event_code": 4130, "sequence": 8}
_UNSEQUENCED = {k: v for k, v in _WHOLE.items() if k != "sequence"}
_NO_SEQUENCE = "strobed PARAM_CHANGED and holds no whole-number sequence"
#: One damaged row each, and what `stranded.find` says of it.
_DAMAGED = {
    "unknown kind": ({**_WHOLE, "kind": "preset"}, "is of the kind 'preset'"),
    "set without sequence": (_UNSEQUENCED, _NO_SEQUENCE),
    "range without sequence": ({**_UNSEQUENCED, "kind": "range"}, _NO_SEQUENCE),
    "no kind, no sequence": ({k: v for k, v in _UNSEQUENCED.items() if k != "kind"},
                             _NO_SEQUENCE),
    "change as text": ({**_WHOLE, "change": "10"}, "holds no change id"),
    "change 0": ({**_WHOLE, "change": 0}, "holds no change id"),
}


def test_a_session_whose_log_holds_every_kind_is_found_resumable_and_goes_on_numbering(tmp_path):
    """Review Focus 4 (engine build C3's spec §8; `stranded.find` is welfare-listed and reads
    every stranded folder through `resume.read`). A session's log holds a clear, a drum switch and
    a training switch, a person's values, a hand-back, a range change and a two-row revert,
    written through `record.change` before its process stopped: it is found resumable, its next
    `sequence` and its next `change` exceed every one in the log, and its reward size is restored
    from the last `set` row of it alone, never from another kind's row naming it (which the rig
    never writes). With one damaged row added -- an unknown kind, a strobed or kindless row without
    a whole-number `sequence`, a `change` that is text or 0 -- it is found not resumable, saying
    which row, failing closed."""
    root = tmp_path / "first"
    link = _Drained({1: [Training(setting="clear", on=True, by=Box("jake")),
                         ClearOwed(condition="x", by=Box("jake")),
                         Drum(scope="block", by=Box("jake")),
                         SetParameter(name="reward_correct", value=0.2, by=Box("jake"))]})
    first = _session(_spec(root, task="", trials=0, values={}), link, service=True)
    block = Block(name="X", conditions=[Condition("x", {}, target=3)], counting=EVERY_TRIAL)
    first.run(RunSpec(task=TASK, trials=50, seed=2, values=dict(VALUES), blocks=[block]))
    log = SessionRecord.open(root, "2027-01-14_01", "A")
    later = {"by": Box("jake"), "at": WALL_NOW + 500.0, "trial_number": 9, "run": 0,
             "meaning": None, "event_code": 4130}
    uniform = {"class": "Uniform", "fields": {"low": 0.2, "high": 0.4, "repeat": "fresh"}}
    log.change(change=5, kind="hand_back", name="fix_hold", was=0.5, now=0.3, sequence=2,
               to="run", **later)
    log.change(change=6, kind="range", name="fix_hold", was=uniform,
               now={**uniform, "fields": {**uniform["fields"], "high": 0.5}}, sequence=3,
               block=None, **{"from": "task"}, **later)
    log.change(change=7, kind="revert", name="fix_hold", was=0.3, now=0.4, sequence=4,
               moment=4, **later)
    log.change(change=7, kind="revert", name="fix_window", was=2.0, now=2.5, sequence=5,
               moment=4, **later)
    log.change(change=8, kind="set", name="reward_correct", was=0.2, now=0.25, sequence=6,
               **later)
    log.change(change=9, kind="revert", name="reward_correct", was=0.25, now=0.35,
               sequence=7, moment=4, **later)
    kinds = [row["kind"] for row in _rows(first, "parameter_changes.jsonl")]
    assert kinds == ["training", "clear", "drum", "set", "hand_back", "range", "revert",
                     "revert", "set", "revert"]
    for label, (row, _) in _DAMAGED.items():
        copy = tmp_path / label.replace(" ", "_")
        shutil.copytree(root, copy)
        with (copy / "2027-01-14_01" / "xcon" / "parameter_changes.jsonl").open("a") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(row) + "\n")

    (found,) = stranded.find(root)
    assert (found.resumable, found.why) == (True, "")
    restoration = resume.read(first.directory, first.welfare.left_cage_wall_at)
    assert (restoration.sequence, restoration.change) == (7, 9)
    assert restoration.bounded["reward_correct"] == 0.25
    again = Session(_spec(root, task="", trials=0, values={}), card=Card(), pump=Pump(),
                    link=Simulated(), service=True)
    later_still = first.now() + 60.0
    again.wall_clock = lambda: WALL_NOW + later_still + again.now()
    again.resume(restoration, by=Box("jake"), how="test")
    assert (again._sequence, again._change) == (7, 9)
    assert again.spec.bounds.value("reward_correct") == 0.25
    again.link.queue(SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.4, by=Box("jake")))
    again.run(RunSpec(task=TASK, trials=50, seed=2, values=dict(VALUES), blocks=[block]))
    last = _rows(again, "parameter_changes.jsonl")[-1]
    assert (last["kind"], last["change"], last["sequence"], last["run"]) == ("set", 10, 8, 1)

    for label, (_, said) in _DAMAGED.items():
        (found,) = stranded.find(tmp_path / label.replace(" ", "_"))
        assert not found.resumable, label
        assert found.why.startswith(f"its parameter_changes.jsonl row 11 {said}"), found.why
```

with

```python
#: **A clear, a drumming switch and a training switch are written to the change log too**
#: (engine build C3's spec §8; XC-363): each a row of its own kind there (`KINDS`), without a
#: `sequence`, since it strobes nothing, and each still written here exactly as engine build C2a
#: writes it, until wl-preproc reads and times the change log's rows (XC-B; the C3 ask in
#: `docs/pending-wl-preproc-amendments.md`).
CONTROLS = "controls.jsonl"

#: **The change log's kinds** (`parameter_changes.jsonl`; XC-288 §3.4, engine build C3's spec
#: §8), one row for each setting an act moves (`SessionRecord.change`): a person's value (`set`),
#: a setting handed back (`hand_back`), a draw's numbers changed live (`range`), each setting a
#: revert restores (`revert`), and a clear, a drumming switch and a training switch (`clear`,
#: `drum`, `training`), which `CONTROLS` keeps as well. A row written before engine build C3 has
#: no `kind`, and is a `set`, the only kind there was (`resume._read`).
KINDS = ("set", "hand_back", "range", "revert", "clear", "drum", "training")

#: **The kinds that strobe `PARAM_CHANGED`**, once for each row, and so carry its `sequence`, which
#: joins the n-th such row to the n-th such code (XC-288 §3.4): the first four `KINDS`. A clear and
#: a switch strobe nothing.
STROBED = KINDS[:4]
```

```python
    def parameter_change(
        self,
        sequence: int,
        name: str,
        was: object,
        now: object,
        by: Actor,
        run: int | None = None,
        *,
        event_code: int | None,
    ) -> None:
        """One live parameter change, joined to the recording by `sequence`.

        The `PARAM_CHANGE` escape is to carry that number and nothing else: the values
        live here (S2 §5.2). **Not yet**: until XC-008, `Session` strobes the
        payload-less `PARAM_CHANGED` word, so a row joins its code by count, the n-th
        row to the n-th code -- and since XC-321 ask 1 by `event_code` besides, the number
        that row strobed (`PARAM_CHANGED`'s), `null` when it strobed nothing and absent on
        a row written before that. If the two ever disagree the change cannot be placed on
        the recording clock at all, so the join is the entire point of both halves.

        `by` records the origin -- console, control API, or the task -- because one
        validated write path with an unrecorded actor is only half the guarantee.

        `run` is the run it happened in: `taskd` always passes it, since a session holds
        several and each numbers its own changes from the session's one sequence.
        """
        with (self.directory / "parameter_changes.jsonl").open(
            "a", encoding="utf-8"
        ) as handle:
            handle.write(
                json.dumps(
                    {
                        "sequence": sequence,
                        "name": name,
                        "was": was,
                        "now": now,
                        "by": actors.to_map(by),
                        "run": run,
                        "event_code": event_code,
                    },
                    sort_keys=True,
                    default=_written,
                )
                + "\n"
            )
```

with

```python
    def change(
        self,
        *,
        change: int,
        kind: str,
        name: str,
        was: object,
        now: object,
        by: Actor | None,
        at: float,
        trial_number: int,
        run: int | None,
        meaning: dict | None,
        event_code: int | None,
        sequence: int | None = None,
        **detail: object,
    ) -> None:
        """**One row of the change log** (`parameter_changes.jsonl`; XC-288 §3.4, engine build C3's
        spec §8): one setting one act moved, of one of `KINDS`, from `was` to `now`.

        - `change` is the act's id, from 1, shared by the rows of one act (a revert's); 0 names
          no act, and a revert's `moment` reads it as a run's start.
        - `at` is the instant it applied, on the session's anchored clock, written as the number
          and as local clock time with its zone, as a control row's is: the rig's bookkeeping, of
          no stated accuracy (XC-383), never a time on the recording's clock.
        - `trial_number` is the first trial it applies to, as that trial's line and its
          `TRIAL_NUMBER` escape number it; `run` the run it happened in.
        - `meaning` is the setting's declared meaning with the way this change went and its step
          (`taskd.Session._meaning`), or `None` on a row naming no task setting: a ceiling's, and
          every clear and switch.
        - `by` is who made it, an `Actor`, written as `actor.to_map`'s map, or `None`, null.
        - `offered` is written empty and `odds` null, until a later build and build D fill them
          (XC-288 §3.4, §4.5).
        - `event_code` is the number the act strobed, `null` when it strobed nothing (XC-321 ask
          1). **`sequence` is on a row of the kinds that strobe `PARAM_CHANGED` alone**
          (`STROBED`): it joins the n-th such row to the n-th such code. The `PARAM_CHANGE`
          escape is to carry that number and nothing else, the values living here (S2 §5.2);
          until XC-008 the payload-less word goes out, so the join is by count.
        - `detail` is the kind's own fields, written as given: a hand-back's `to`, a range's
          `from` and `block`, a revert's `moment`, and a clear's and a switch's control-row
          fields (`CONTROLS`).

        A value is written as given, a person's -90 as -90 (the PI, 2026-10-30, "Warn at load");
        `_written` writes what `json` cannot. **A row its readers would refuse is never written**:
        a kind not in `KINDS`, a `sequence` on a kind outside `STROBED` or none on one inside it,
        an empty `name` (wl-preproc leaves out a row naming nothing), and a `change` that is not a
        whole number from 1 each raise `ValueError` here, before the file is opened -- reached by
        no input, since every caller passes its own literal kind and the session's own counters.
        """
        if kind not in KINDS:
            raise ValueError(f"a change row's kind is one of {', '.join(KINDS)}, not {kind!r}")
        if (sequence is None) == (kind in STROBED):
            raise ValueError(
                f"a {kind} row carries a sequence exactly when its kind strobes PARAM_CHANGED "
                f"({', '.join(STROBED)}), and it was given {sequence!r}"
            )
        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
            raise ValueError(f"a change row names what it moved, and {name!r} names nothing")
        if isinstance(change, bool) or not isinstance(change, int) or change < 1:
            raise ValueError(f"a change id is a whole number from 1, not {change!r}")
        row = {
            "change": change, "kind": kind, "name": name, "was": was, "now": now,
            "by": actors.to_map_or_none(by), "at": at, "at_local": _local(at),
            "trial_number": trial_number, "run": run, "meaning": meaning, "offered": [],
            "odds": None, "event_code": event_code, **detail,
        }
        if sequence is not None:
            row["sequence"] = sequence
        with (self.directory / "parameter_changes.jsonl").open("a", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            handle.write(json.dumps(row, sort_keys=True, default=_written) + "\n")
```

add

```python

def _whole(value: object) -> bool:
    """Whether `value` is a whole number as the record writes one: an `int`, never a `bool`."""
    return isinstance(value, int) and not isinstance(value, bool)


def _changes(directory: Path) -> list[dict]:
    """**The change log's rows, each as `SessionRecord.change` writes it, or `Unresumable`**
    (engine build C3's spec §8: resume "fails closed on a row without `sequence`; it learns every
    kind in the commit writing the first such row"). A resume continues the session's `sequence`
    and `change` numbers from these rows and its bounded values from its `set` rows, so **a row
    it cannot read fails closed, naming it**, never a guess, as the rest of the record does. A row
    written before engine build C3 has no `kind` and no `change`, and is a `set`, the only kind
    there was. Refused: a row that is not an object; a `kind` that is not one of `record.KINDS`;
    a row of a kind that strobes `PARAM_CHANGED` (`record.STROBED`), or with no kind, without a
    whole-number `sequence`, which joins it to its code; and a `change` that is not a whole
    number from 1, on a row with a kind or any row holding one."""
    rows = _rows(directory, "parameter_changes.jsonl")
    for number, row in enumerate(rows, start=1):

        def damaged(what: str) -> Unresumable:
            return Unresumable(
                f"its parameter_changes.jsonl row {number} {what}, so the changes it records "
                f"cannot be read back; end it instead"
            )

        if not isinstance(row, dict):
            raise damaged("is not a row")
        if "kind" in row and row["kind"] not in KINDS:
            raise damaged(f"is of the kind {_link._quoted(row['kind'])}, which the rig never "
                          f"writes")
        if row.get("kind", "set") in STROBED and not _whole(row.get("sequence")):
            raise damaged("strobed PARAM_CHANGED and holds no whole-number sequence joining it "
                          "to its code")
        if ("kind" in row or "change" in row) and not (
            _whole(row.get("change")) and row["change"] >= 1
        ):
            raise damaged("holds no change id, a whole number from 1")
    return rows

```

```python
    def _meaning(self, name: str, was: object, now: object) -> dict | None:
        """**What a change of `name` from `was` to `now` means**, as its change row writes it
        (XC-288 §3.4 and §4.1; TRN-03): the setting's resolved meaning (`declarations.resolved`),
        its `kind`, `role`, `raising` and `relative_to` as written (`"background"` for the trial's
        background), with `went`, the way this change went by that meaning, `"easier"` or
        `"harder"` (for an expected setting the expected way, never a fact), and `step`, `now`
        minus `was` in the setting's unit. **`None` for a name that is no setting of the run's
        task**, whose row writes no meaning.

        **`went`** is `variation.easier` read both ways round: easier one way is `"easier"`, the
        other way `"harder"`. **A choice, or a value that is not a number, has no order** (TRN-11:
        a task's own meaning for one "reads on changing it"), so a change goes the way its
        `raising` says, as `easier` reads a choice, where it can read one at all. Null where it
        cannot be read (relative to the background, or to a setting holding no number), for a
        setting that is not a difficulty setting, for a value set to itself, and for two numbers
        as far from what the meaning reads relative to. A meaning relative to another setting
        reads that setting's value in the run's values as this row applies. **`step`** is null
        where either value is not a number."""
        found = None if self._task is None else resolved(self._task).get(name)
        if found is None:
            return None
        meaning = found[0]
        relative = meaning.relative_to
        reference = self.spec.values.get(relative) if isinstance(relative, str) else None
        choices = bool(self._declared[name].choices)
        numbers = all(isinstance(v, (int, float)) and not isinstance(v, bool) for v in (was, now))
        went = None
        if meaning.kind != NOT_DIFFICULTY and was != now:
            if choices or not numbers:
                if easier(meaning, now, was, reference, choices=choices) is not None:
                    went = meaning.raising
            elif easier(meaning, now, was, reference):
                went = EASIER
            elif easier(meaning, was, now, reference):
                went = HARDER
        return {
            "kind": meaning.kind,
            "role": meaning.role,
            "raising": meaning.raising,
            "relative_to": "background" if isinstance(relative, Background) else relative,
            "went": went,
            "step": now - was if numbers else None,
        }

    def _logged(self, kind: str, name: str, was: object, now: object, by: Actor | None,
                at: float, **detail: object) -> None:
        """**A clear or a switch in the change log too** (XC-363; engine build C3's spec §8): its
        control row is in `controls.jsonl` as engine build C2a writes it (`_control`), and this
        row beside it, of `kind`, with a change id of its own, `name` what it moved, the control
        row's instant, the next trial to start as the first it applies to, and no meaning, since
        it names no task setting. **No `sequence`**: it strobes nothing. Both rows until
        wl-preproc reads and times the change log's (XC-B; the C3 ask in
        `docs/pending-wl-preproc-amendments.md`)."""
        self._change += 1
        if self._record is not None:
            self._record.change(
                change=self._change, kind=kind, name=name, was=was, now=now, by=by, at=at,
                trial_number=self._levels.trials + 1, run=self.run_index, meaning=None,
                event_code=None, **detail,
            )

```

### Task 8: The review report: draws, generated conditions, designed orders, the wait's hazard

A task is approved from its review report, never its source (ADR-0006), and **nobody writes a generated condition, so nobody reads one unless it is shown** (the C3 spec §4, pitfall P20). This task makes the report show what C3 varies, all of it arithmetic of what the task declares, none of it a measurement:
- **the task's draws, the plain run's** (the PI, 2026-10-30, Q1a, "Task default, block may replace"), in a new `### Draws` section between the counting tables and the plans (`review._draws`): each draw in the rig's words (`variation.words`), a direction from 0 to 360 as the rig writes it (Call 11), with what a repeat takes, `same` or `fresh` (Q3), or `**not declared**`;
- **the non-aging wait's hazard** (Q2, "Draw again": "the review report shows how much the target's chance rises near the longest"; Call 6), `review._wait`: the chance of the wait ending at each moment against the flat rate at the shortest, the mean and two points nearing the longest, four fifths and nineteen twentieths of the way, each to two decimal places, then the realized average to three significant figures below the declared mean, and the sentence "These describe the declared distribution, not the rig." **The report's own format is pinned** (review M-20): 750 to 1250 ms with a mean of 1000 reads 1.16, 1.58, 3.03 and **10.51** times at 750, 1000, 1150 and 1225 ms, which the spec's §3 table rounds to 1.2, 1.6, 3 and 10 (its "10" rounds 10.51 down), and averages 922 ms. No timing claim (CLAUDE.md): the numbers describe the declared distribution;
- **per block, in the plan tables** (`_plans`): the draws in force, its own or the task's, and a setting it leaves `BY_CONDITIONS` (`_block_draws`); a condition's own range among its values (`_set_label`, Q1b); **its generated conditions**, each with its values and target after the hand-listed ones (`variation.generated`), then its factors, the target and each hand-written number, the exclusions applied, and **each level's share of the trials they owe** (`_factorial`; Q4, "Yes, each cell equal"); each wait the block or its conditions draw of their own, with its hazard (`_block_waits`); and **a designed order in words** (`_block_order` learns `SequenceBalanced` and `Priming`, which read "shuffled passes" until now) with what ends its block (`_ends`; Calls 15 and 16).

`wlx review` checks nothing first, so what the load refuses is said, never raised: a wait whose numbers give no hazard, a draw with no `repeat`, a draw of an undeclared setting, a block draw that is no draw, a priming block with both a chance and runs.

**A defect found drafting this task is fixed in Task 4, which owns `variation.py`** (the controller, 2026-10-30): `variation.realized_mean` raised `OverflowError` for a wait the load accepts whose longest is far past its mean (`(maximum - minimum) / (mean - minimum)` above about 709: `NonAging(0, 0.001, 1.0)`), so `wlx review` of such a task would print nothing. Task 4 computes it in a form that cannot overflow, with its own test (`test_a_wait_whose_longest_is_far_past_its_mean_is_computed_never_raising`); this task's last test reaches the same wait through the report, which is the function's consumer.

```python
"""What varies, in the review report (engine build C3; its spec §3-§5): the task's draws and each
block's, a condition's own range, the conditions a block makes from factors with the exclusions
applied and each level's share, a designed order in words, and each non-aging wait's hazard against
the flat rate with its declared and realized averages. A task is approved from this report, not
from its source (ADR-0006), and nobody writes a generated condition, so nobody reads one unless it
is shown (pitfall P20)."""

from __future__ import annotations

import math

import pytest

from wl_xcon import review, variation
from wl_xcon.review import render_task
from wl_xcon.task import (
    BY_CONDITIONS,
    FRESH,
    SAME,
    After,
    Block,
    Condition,
    Factorial,
    NonAging,
    On,
    Outcome,
    P,
    Param,
    Plan,
    Polar,
    Priming,
    SaccadeTo,
    SequenceBalanced,
    State,
    Task,
    Trial,
    Uniform,
    Weighted,
    Window,
)

LOOK = Trial(
    start="wait",
    params=[
        Param("wait", unit="s", low=0.5, high=3.0, start=1.0),
        Param("contrast", unit="fraction", low=0.0, high=1.0, start=0.5),
        Param("side", unit="side", choices=("left", "right")),
        Param("ecc", unit="deg", low=0.0, high=20.0, start=8.0),
        Param("dir", unit="deg", low=0.0, high=360.0, start=45.0),
    ],
    windows=[Window("target", at=Polar(P("ecc"), P("dir")), radius=2.0)],
    states=[
        State("wait", go=[On(After(P("wait")), "look")]),
        State("look", go=[On(SaccadeTo("target"), Outcome.CORRECT),
                          On(After(0.5), Outcome.NO_RESPONSE)]),
    ],
)

#: What `_wait` says of a wait its numbers give no hazard for.
CANNOT = ("**Its hazard cannot be computed**: a non-aging wait's mean must be past its shortest "
          "and at most its longest, each a finite number, which the load-time check refuses "
          "otherwise.")


def _task(**fields) -> Task:
    """One structure, `look`: a wait, a contrast, a side, and a target placed by eccentricity and
    direction, so `dir` is a direction setting (`variation.directions`)."""
    return Task({"look": LOOK}, default="look", **fields)


def test_the_review_lists_the_tasks_draws_and_each_blocks():
    """The PI, 2026-10-30, Q1a ("Task default, block may replace") and Q1b ("a condition may draw
    its own setting from its own range"): the report lists the task's draws, the plain run's, in
    the rig's words with what a repeat takes (Q3), a direction from 0 to 360 as the rig writes it
    (engine build C3's call 11); then each block's -- its own, the task's it does not replace, a
    setting it leaves to its conditions -- and a condition's own range among its values. A value a
    condition gives is shown as given. A task drawing nothing says so, and a plan whose blocks draw
    nothing has no table of draws."""
    task = _task(
        draws={"wait": NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25, repeat=FRESH),
               "dir": Uniform(-45, 45, repeat=SAME)},
        plans={"p": Plan([
            Block("plain", [Condition("near", {"contrast": 0.9}, target=4)]),
            Block("long", [Condition("far", {"side": "right"}, target=4)],
                  draws={"wait": NonAging(1.0, 1.5, 3.0, repeat=SAME),
                         "contrast": Weighted((0.1, 0.5), (3, 1), repeat=FRESH)}),
            Block("given", [Condition("left", {"dir": 180.0}, target=4),
                            Condition("spread", {"dir": Uniform(-10, 10, repeat=FRESH)},
                                      target=4)],
                  draws={"dir": BY_CONDITIONS}),
        ])},
    )
    out = render_task(task)

    assert "| Setting | Drawn from | On a repeat |" in out
    assert (out.index("### What each trial does to its condition's count") < out.index("### Draws")
            < out.index("### Plans"))
    assert "| wait | non-aging from 0.75 s to 1.25 s, mean 1.0 s | fresh |" in out
    assert "| dir | uniform from 315 deg to 45 deg | same |" in out
    assert "| Block | Setting | Drawn from | Whose | On a repeat |" in out
    assert ("| plain | wait | non-aging from 0.75 s to 1.25 s, mean 1.0 s | the task's | fresh |"
            in out)
    assert "| plain | dir | uniform from 315 deg to 45 deg | the task's | same |" in out
    assert ("| long | wait | non-aging from 1.0 s to 3.0 s, mean 1.5 s | the block's own | same |"
            in out)
    assert ("| long | contrast | one of 0.1 fraction, 0.5 fraction, weighted 3:1 | the block's own "
            "| fresh |") in out
    assert "| long | dir | uniform from 315 deg to 45 deg | the task's | same |" in out
    assert ("| given | wait | non-aging from 0.75 s to 1.25 s, mean 1.0 s | the task's | fresh |"
            in out)
    assert ("| given | dir | each condition's value or own range (above) | by its conditions | |"
            in out)
    assert out.count("| given | dir |") == 1
    assert "| given | left | look | 4 | dir = 180.0 |" in out
    assert ("| given | spread | look | 4 | dir = uniform from 350 deg to 10 deg (fresh on a "
            "repeat) |") in out
    assert "`wait`, the task's draw: non-aging from 0.75 s to 1.25 s, mean 1.0 s." in out
    assert "`wait` in block `long`, its own draw: non-aging from 1.0 s to 3.0 s, mean 1.5 s." in out
    assert "| 2.9 s | 5.52 times |" in out
    assert "Its waits average 1.46 s, below the declared mean of 1.5 s" in out

    plain = render_task(_task(plans={"q": Plan([Block("b", [Condition("c", {}, target=1)])])}))
    assert ("### Draws\n\nNone of the task's own: the plain run draws nothing. A block type's own "
            "draws are in its plan's tables.") in plain
    assert "| Block | Setting |" not in plain


def test_a_factorials_generated_conditions_exclusions_and_level_shares_are_listed():
    """The C3 spec §4 ("Listed for review": "nobody writes generated conditions, so nobody reads
    them unless shown"), TSK-22 and the PI's Q4 ("Yes, each cell equal": "the review report shows
    each level's overall share"): each generated condition in the plan's table after the block's
    hand-listed ones, with its values and target; the factors and levels, the target and each
    hand-written number, the exclusions applied; and each level's share of the trials the
    generated conditions owe, which exclusions and hand-written numbers make unequal. A level may
    be a range of its own (Q1b), its hazard shown once for every condition sharing it; conditions
    that owe nothing, as a priming block's, say so."""
    mixed = Factorial({"contrast": (0.1, 0.5), "side": ("left", "right")},
                      exclude=({"contrast": 0.1, "side": "left"},), target=4,
                      targets={"contrast=0.5, side=right": 8})
    ranges = Factorial({"wait": (NonAging(0.5, 0.75, 1.0, repeat=FRESH),),
                        "side": ("left", "right")}, target=0)
    plans = {"p": Plan([
        Block("mixed", [Condition("catch", {"contrast": 0.0}, target=2)], factorial=mixed),
        Block("ranges", [], factorial=ranges, order=Priming("side", chance=0.5), trials=40),
    ])}
    out = render_task(_task(plans=plans))

    assert ("| mixed | catch | look | 2 | contrast = 0.0 |\n"
            "| mixed | contrast=0.1, side=right | look | 4 | contrast = 0.1, side = right |\n"
            "| mixed | contrast=0.5, side=left | look | 4 | contrast = 0.5, side = left |\n"
            "| mixed | contrast=0.5, side=right | look | 8 | contrast = 0.5, side = right |"
            ) in out
    assert ("Block `mixed` makes 3 conditions from its factors, its last 3 rows in the table of "
            "conditions above: contrast (0.1, 0.5); side (left, right). Each is owed 4 trials, but "
            "`contrast=0.5, side=right` 8. Excluded: `contrast=0.1, side=left`.") in out
    assert ("| Factor | Level | Conditions | Trials owed | Share of trials owed |\n"
            "|---|---|---|---|---|\n"
            "| contrast | 0.1 | 1 | 4 | 25.0% |\n"
            "| contrast | 0.5 | 2 | 12 | 75.0% |\n"
            "| side | left | 1 | 4 | 25.0% |\n"
            "| side | right | 2 | 12 | 75.0% |") in out

    level = "wait=non-aging from 0.5 to 1.0, mean 0.75"
    assert (f"| ranges | {level}, side=left | look | 0 | wait = non-aging from 0.5 s to 1.0 s, "
            f"mean 0.75 s (fresh on a repeat), side = left |") in out
    assert ("Block `ranges` makes 2 conditions from its factors, its last 2 rows in the table of "
            f"conditions above: wait ({level[5:]}); side (left, right). Each is owed 0 trials. "
            "Excluded: none.") in out
    assert f"| wait | {level[5:]} | 2 | 0 | none owed |" in out
    assert (f"`wait` in block `ranges`, the own range of `{level}, side=left`, "
            f"`{level}, side=right`: non-aging from 0.5 s to 1.0 s, mean 0.75 s.") in out
    assert out.count("| 0.5 s, the shortest |") == 1


def test_a_runs_priming_block_shows_its_switch_chance_after_each_trial_of_a_run():
    """The C3 plan's science review, I-8: runs of lengths drawn evenly from 3 to 7 make a switch
    ever more expected along a run -- 0, 0, then 0.2, 0.25, 0.33, 0.5 and certain at 7 -- which a
    non-aging draw of lengths avoids, near 0.4 until its cut; the report shows each, and says a
    distribution of lengths in the rig's words. A block primed by a chance shows none."""
    two = [Condition("l", {"side": "left"}, target=0), Condition("r", {"side": "right"}, target=0)]
    waited = NonAging(3.0, 5.0, 12.0, repeat=FRESH)
    plans = {"p": Plan([
        Block("even", two, order=Priming("side", runs=(3, 7)), trials=200),
        Block("waited", two, order=Priming("side", runs=waited), trials=200),
        Block("chance", two, order=Priming("side", chance=0.7), trials=200),
    ])}
    out = render_task(_task(plans=plans))
    even = out[out.index("Block `even`: the chance its run switches"):]
    assert ("| Shown trials in the run | Chance it switches next |\n|---|---|\n| 1 | 0.00 |\n"
            "| 2 | 0.00 |\n| 3 | 0.20 |\n| 4 | 0.25 |\n| 5 | 0.33 |\n| 6 | 0.50 |\n"
            "| 7 | 1.00 |\n") in even
    flat = out[out.index("Block `waited`: the chance its run switches"):]
    assert "| 3 | 0.40 |\n| 4 | 0.40 |\n| 5 | 0.41 |\n" in flat and "| 11 | 1.00 |" in flat
    assert ("priming on `side`: runs of one value, each its length drawn "
            f"{variation.words(waited, 'shown trials')}, rounded down, then another value at "
            "random") in out
    assert "Block `chance`: the chance its run switches" not in out


def test_a_designed_order_is_said_in_words():
    """The C3 spec §5 and the PI's Q5a ("Block picks; pairs default"), Q5b ("'Again at once' as an
    option") and Q6 ("Both of the last two"): a sequence-balanced block's reach, cycles and break
    rule, and that it ends once its sequence is played out, `(n**depth + depth - 1) * cycles`
    trials, each cycle the linear sequence opening on a lead-in (the PI, 2026-10-31), or its own
    number of trials first (engine build C3's call 15); a priming block's feature, its chance or
    its runs and its break rule, ending on its trials or its time (call 16). Each said apart from
    "shuffled passes", which is what it read before."""
    four = [Condition(name, {"contrast": c}, target=1)
            for name, c in (("a", 0.2), ("b", 0.4), ("c", 0.6), ("d", 0.8))]
    two = [Condition("l", {"side": "left"}, target=0), Condition("r", {"side": "right"}, target=0)]
    plans = {"p": Plan([
        Block("pairs", four, order=SequenceBalanced()),
        Block("triples", [Condition("x", {"contrast": 0.2}, target=8),
                          Condition("y", {"contrast": 0.8}, target=8)],
              order=SequenceBalanced(depth=3, cycles=2, again_at_once=True), trials=12),
        Block("chance", two, order=Priming("side", chance=0.7), trials=200),
        Block("runs", two, order=Priming("side", runs=(3, 7), again_at_once=True),
              time_limit_s=300.0),
    ])}
    out = render_task(_task(plans=plans))
    tail = "| each condition's structure's table | no |"

    assert ("| pairs | its sequence is played out, 17 trials | sequence-balanced from the run's "
            "seed: each cycle a linear de Bruijn sequence, each ordered pair of conditions, a "
            "condition after itself included, once a cycle, its first trial a lead-in that only "
            "precedes what follows; 1 cycle; a broken trial is not repeated, its place a designed "
            "shortfall " + tail) in out
    assert ("| triples | its sequence is played out, 20 trials; or 12 trials run | "
            "sequence-balanced from the run's seed: each cycle a linear de Bruijn sequence, each "
            "ordered triple of conditions, a condition after itself included, once a cycle, its "
            "first 2 trials a lead-in that only precedes what follows; 2 cycles; a broken trial "
            "comes back at once, under the repeat limit " + tail) in out
    assert ("| chance | 200 trials run | priming on `side`: the next trial repeats the last shown "
            "trial's value with a chance of 0.7, else another value at random; within a value, "
            "its conditions in shuffled passes; a broken trial is not repeated " + tail) in out
    assert ("| runs | its time runs out at 5 minutes | priming on `side`: runs of one value, each "
            "3 to 7 shown trials long, drawn, then another value at random; within a value, its "
            "conditions in shuffled passes; a broken trial comes back at once, under the repeat "
            "limit " + tail) in out
    assert "each ordered run of 4 conditions" in review._block_order(SequenceBalanced(depth=4))
    assert "shuffled passes |" not in out


def test_a_non_aging_wait_shows_its_hazard_rise_and_both_averages():
    """The PI, 2026-10-30, Q2 ("Draw again": "the review report shows how much the target's chance
    rises near the longest") and engine build C3's call 6: the chance of the wait ending at each
    moment, against the flat rate, at the shortest, the mean and two points nearing the longest,
    and both averages, the declared mean being the wait's own before its tail is drawn again. The
    spec's example, 750 to 1250 ms with a mean of 1000, **pinned in the report's own format**: two
    decimal places, so 1.16, 1.58, 3.03 and 10.51 times, which the spec's §3 rounds to 1.2, 1.6,
    3 and 10 (review M-20: its "10" rounds 10.51 down); the realized average to three significant
    figures, 922 ms. Arithmetic of the declared distribution, said so: no timing claim."""
    assert review._wait(NonAging(750, 1000, 1250, repeat=FRESH), "ms") == [
        "| At | Chance per moment, against the flat rate |",
        "|---|---|",
        "| 750 ms, the shortest | 1.16 times |",
        "| 1000 ms, the mean | 1.58 times |",
        "| 1150 ms | 3.03 times |",
        "| 1225 ms | 10.51 times |",
        "",
        "A wait drawn past the longest, 1250 ms, is drawn again, so the chance rises toward it. "
        "Its waits average 922 ms, below the declared mean of 1000 ms, which is the wait's own "
        "before its tail is drawn again. These describe the declared distribution, not the rig.",
        "",
    ]
    out = render_task(_task(draws={"wait": NonAging(0.75, 1.0, 1.25, repeat=FRESH)}))
    assert ("| 0.75 s, the shortest | 1.16 times |\n| 1 s, the mean | 1.58 times |\n"
            "| 1.15 s | 3.03 times |\n| 1.225 s | 10.51 times |") in out
    assert "Its waits average 0.922 s, below the declared mean of 1 s" in out
    assert review._wait(NonAging(750, 1000, 1250, repeat=FRESH), "")[2] == (
        "| 750, the shortest | 1.16 times |")

    # A mean past four fifths of the way is listed in its place; a mean at the longest, where
    # every wait not ended before ends, says so.
    assert review._wait(NonAging(0.0, 0.9, 1.0, repeat=SAME), "s")[2:6] == [
        "| 0 s, the shortest | 1.49 times |", "| 0.8 s | 5.02 times |",
        "| 0.9 s, the mean | 9.51 times |", "| 0.95 s | 18.50 times |"]
    assert "| 1 s, the mean | every wait not ended before ends here |" in review._wait(
        NonAging(0.5, 1.0, 1.0, repeat=SAME), "s")


def test_the_report_computes_a_far_tail_and_says_what_the_load_refuses_never_raising():
    """`wlx review` checks nothing first, and a report that raises shows nothing at all. A wait
    whose longest is far past its mean -- e to the power (longest - shortest) / (mean - shortest)
    past a float's range -- is a wait the load accepts, and its realized mean is computed (Task
    3's `variation.realized_mean`, written so it cannot overflow). What the load refuses is said: a
    wait whose numbers give no hazard; a draw not saying what a repeat takes; a draw of, or a
    condition's value for, a setting nothing declares; a block's draw that is no draw, or draws
    that are not a dict; a priming block with both a chance and runs and no end; a factorial
    whose factors, levels, exclusions or own numbers are not of their shape, or whose target is
    not a whole number."""
    assert variation.realized_mean(NonAging(0.0, 0.001, 1.0)) == pytest.approx(0.001)
    far = review._wait(NonAging(0.0, 0.001, 1.0, repeat=FRESH), "s")
    assert "Its waits average 0.001 s, below the declared mean of 0.001 s" in far[-2]
    for wait in (NonAging(1.0, 1.0, 2.0), NonAging(1.0, 3.0, 2.0), NonAging(1.0, math.inf, 2.0),
                 NonAging(1.0, "1.5", 2.0), NonAging(True, 1.5, 2.0)):
        assert review._wait(wait, "s") == [CANNOT, ""]

    task = _task(
        draws={"wait": NonAging(1.0, 1.0, 2.0), "speed": Uniform(1, 2, repeat=SAME)},
        plans={"p": Plan([
            Block("odd", [Condition("l", {"side": "left", "speed": 2}, target=0)],
                  order=Priming("side", chance=0.5, runs=(2, 4)),
                  draws={"contrast": "by condition"}),
            Block("bare", [], draws=("wait",), factorial=Factorial(
                [("contrast", (0.1,))], exclude=("contrast",), targets=[("contrast=0.1", 2)])),
            Block("flat", [], factorial=Factorial({"contrast": (0.1, 0.5), "side": "left"})),
            Block("whole", [], factorial=Factorial({"contrast": (0.1,)}, target=True)),
        ])},
    )
    out = render_task(task)

    assert "| wait | non-aging from 1.0 s to 2.0 s, mean 1.0 s | **not declared** |" in out
    assert "| speed **UNDECLARED** | uniform from 1 to 2 | same |" in out
    assert CANNOT in out
    assert ("| odd | **nothing declared**, which the load-time check refuses | priming on `side`: "
            "**a chance or runs, exactly one**, which the load-time check refuses otherwise;"
            ) in out
    assert "| odd | l | look | 0 | side = left, speed = 2 |" in out
    assert "| odd | contrast | **not a draw**: 'by condition' | | |" in out
    assert "| bare | wait | non-aging from 1.0 s to 2.0 s, mean 1.0 s | the task's |" in out
    assert ("Block `bare` makes 0 conditions from its factors, its last 0 rows in the table of "
            "conditions above: **no factors**. Each is owed 1 trials. Excluded: none.") in out
    assert ("Block `flat` makes 0 conditions from its factors, its last 0 rows in the table of "
            "conditions above: contrast (0.1, 0.5); side (). Each is owed 1 trials.") in out
    assert "| contrast | 0.5 | 0 | 0 | none owed |" in out
    assert "| whole | contrast=0.1 | look | True | contrast = 0.1 |" in out
    assert "| contrast | 0.1 | 1 | 0 | none owed |" in out
```

```python
def _block_order(order) -> str:
    """How a block orders its conditions, in words."""
    if isinstance(order, Constrained):
        weights = f", weighted {order.weights}" if order.weights else ""
        return f"drawn with replacement, runs of at most {order.max_run}{weights}"
    if isinstance(order, WithReplacement):
        return "drawn with replacement" + (f", weighted {order.weights}" if order.weights else "")
    return "shuffled passes"
```

with

```python
def _block_order(order) -> str:
    """How a block orders its conditions, in words: shuffled passes or drawn with replacement, or
    since engine build C3 a designed order (`_balanced_words`, `_priming_words`), which read
    "shuffled passes" before it."""
    if isinstance(order, Constrained):
        weights = f", weighted {order.weights}" if order.weights else ""
        return f"drawn with replacement, runs of at most {order.max_run}{weights}"
    if isinstance(order, WithReplacement):
        return "drawn with replacement" + (f", weighted {order.weights}" if order.weights else "")
    if isinstance(order, SequenceBalanced):
        return _balanced_words(order)
    if isinstance(order, Priming):
        return _priming_words(order)
    return "shuffled passes"


def _balanced_words(order: SequenceBalanced) -> str:
    """**A sequence-balanced order in words** (TSK-23; the PI, 2026-10-30, Q5a, "Block picks; pairs
    default", and Q5b, "'Again at once' as an option"): each cycle a linear de Bruijn sequence from
    the run's seed, how far back its balance reaches, every pair or triple once a cycle, its first
    `depth - 1` trials a lead-in that only precedes what follows (the PI, 2026-10-31, on the engine
    C3 plan's Appendix B, item 1; engine build C3's call 15), its cycles, and what a broken trial
    does."""
    reach = ("pair of" if order.depth == 2 else "triple of" if order.depth == 3
             else f"run of {order.depth}")
    cycles = f"{order.cycles} cycle{'' if order.cycles == 1 else 's'}"
    broken = ("a broken trial comes back at once, under the repeat limit" if order.again_at_once
              else "a broken trial is not repeated, its place a designed shortfall")
    lead = ("its first trial" if order.depth == 2
            else f"its first {order.depth - 1} trials")
    return (f"sequence-balanced from the run's seed: each cycle a linear de Bruijn sequence, each "
            f"ordered {reach} conditions, a condition after itself included, once a cycle, {lead} "
            f"a lead-in that only precedes what follows; {cycles}; {broken}")


def _priming_words(order: Priming) -> str:
    """**A priming order in words** (the PI, 2026-10-30, Q6, "Both of the last two"): its feature;
    its chance that the next trial repeats the last shown trial's value, or its runs of one value
    with drawn lengths, exactly one of them, said where it declares both or neither (refused at
    load); within a value, shuffled passes; and what a broken trial does (engine build C3's calls
    16 and 17). Runs whose lengths a distribution draws are said in the rig's words (the C3 plan's
    science review, I-8)."""
    if order.runs is None and order.chance is not None:
        how = (f"the next trial repeats the last shown trial's value with a chance of "
               f"{_value_label(order.chance)}, else another value at random")
    elif order.chance is None and isinstance(order.runs, tuple) and len(order.runs) == 2:
        how = (f"runs of one value, each {order.runs[0]} to {order.runs[1]} shown trials long, "
               f"drawn, then another value at random")
    elif order.chance is None and isinstance(order.runs, Distribution):
        how = (f"runs of one value, each its length drawn "
               f"{variation.words(order.runs, 'shown trials')}, rounded down, then another value "
               f"at random")
    else:
        how = "**a chance or runs, exactly one**, which the load-time check refuses otherwise"
    broken = ("a broken trial comes back at once, under the repeat limit" if order.again_at_once
              else "a broken trial is not repeated")
    return (f"priming on `{order.feature}`: {how}; within a value, its conditions in shuffled "
            f"passes; {broken}")
```

In `wl_xcon/review.py` (`_set_label`), replace

```python
def _set_label(value: object, choices=()) -> str:
    """A value a condition sets, as the plan's table shows it: **a position eccentricity and
    direction first, its (x, y) beside them** (`position_words`), whether the setting takes a
    `Polar` or a pair, its `choices` declaring which; anything else as written."""
    words = position_words(value, choices)
```
