```python
    def _apply_pending(self, act: Pending, code: int, trial_number: int, index: int) -> None:
        """**One hand-back or live range applied** (`_apply_staged`, whose change id, `sequence`,
        code and first trial it is given; engine build C3's spec §6 and §8). A hand-back ends the
        person's hold (`_edited`), so the open block's conditions or its draw give the setting
        again and its trials are no longer marked, and puts it back to the run's own value
        (`_run_values`; absent where the run has none). A range puts its draw in force for the
        rest of the run wherever that draw applies, with this change id, which the trials drawn
        from it name (`_ranges`, `_draw`); with no draw, the one declared is in force again. Then,
        as a value's row is: one `PARAM_CHANGED` strobe, its row (`record.SessionRecord.change`)
        with the kind's own fields -- a hand-back's `to`, a range's `from` and `block` -- and its
        line on the changes feed. **A range's meaning says which way it went, judged as a whole**
        against the range the task writes (`_range_went`; the PI, 2026-10-31, on the engine C3
        plan's Appendix B, item 18), its `step` null: a range is no single value. **A hand-back's
        `to` and `now` are read as it applies** (`_to`), in the block its next trial plays, not as
        offered."""
        name = act.name
        if act.kind == "hand_back":
            # What takes it back, and the run's value, read now, in the block the next trial
            # plays: one offered as a block ends applies in the next (the C3 plan's engineering
            # review, M-1; a record claims no value no trial held).
            to = self._to(name)
            act = dataclasses.replace(act, to=to,
                                      now=self._run_values.get(name) if to == "run" else None)
            self._edited -= {name}
            if name in self._run_values:
                self.spec.values[name] = self._run_values[name]
            else:
                self.spec.values.pop(name, None)
            detail = {"to": act.to}
        else:
            if act.draw is None:
                self._ranges.pop(act.key, None)
            else:
                self._ranges[act.key] = (act.draw, self._change)
            detail = {"from": act.key[0], "block": act.key[1] if act.key[0] == "block" else None}
        meaning = self._meaning(name, act.was, act.now)
        if act.kind == "range" and meaning is not None:
            # Which way the new range went, judged as a whole against the range the task writes
            # (the PI, 2026-10-31, on the engine C3 plan's Appendix B, item 18).
            meaning = {**meaning, "went": self._range_went(act)}
        # Strobed before its row is written, as every other writer does: a card that faults here
        # leaves no row naming a code that never went out (XC-321 ask 1).
        self.card.emit(code)
        at = self.wall_now()
        if self._record is not None:
            self._record.change(
                change=self._change, kind=act.kind, name=name, was=act.was, now=act.now,
                by=act.by, at=at, trial_number=trial_number, run=self.run_index, meaning=meaning,
                event_code=code, sequence=self._sequence, **detail,
            )
        self._feed(act.kind, act.by, at, f"{self._pending_said(act)}, from trial {index}")

    def _pending_said(self, act: Pending) -> str:
        """A hand-back or a live range as the changes feed says it, applied (`_apply_pending`) or
        dropped (`_after_service_run`): the setting and the person's value, handed back to what
        takes it back in the open block; or which draw takes which numbers, in the rig's words
        (`variation.words`), or "as declared" where it goes back to the declared one."""
        declared = self._declared.get(act.name)
        if act.kind == "hand_back":
            choices = () if declared is None else declared.choices
            if act.to != "run":
                to = f"its {act.to}"
            elif act.now is None:
                to = "the run, which gives it no value"
            else:
                to = f"the run's {_shown(act.now, choices)}"
            return f"{act.name} {_shown(act.was, choices)} handed back to {to}"
        unit = "" if declared is None else declared.unit
        drawn = "as declared" if act.draw is None else variation.words(act.draw, unit)
        return f"{_draw_said(act.key)} → {drawn}"
```

```markdown
### TSK-67 — A person may hand a setting back: from the next trial the conditions' values (or the draw) apply again, trials are no longer marked overridden, and the hand-back is recorded as a change
- **Decided:** 2026-10-30, the PI, in engine build C3's brainstorm: Q7a, "Yes, a 'hand back' button (Recommended)". It revises the C2b reading that setting the value back does not hand control back (the C2b plan's Appendix B item 1, "Confirm all as built", 2026-10-19; TSK-19) by adding an explicit hand-back; typing the old value back still does not hand control back. That the hand-back always puts the setting back to the run's own value (the task's start under the run's given one, none where neither gives one), over which the open block's conditions or its draw give it again, that its change row names what takes it back there (`to`: `conditions`, `draw` or `run`), that it does not undo a range changed live, and that a hand-back that would leave trials no animal can get right is refused (TSK-69) are engineering (the C3 spec §6; the engine C3 plan's calls 20 and 23).
- **Where:** [the C3 spec §6](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#6-live-edits); [`wl_xcon/link.py`](../../wl_xcon/link.py) (`HandBack`); [`wl_xcon/taskd.py`](../../wl_xcon/taskd.py) (`Session._command`, welfare-listed: a branch beside the pause, handing to `Session._hand_back`, off the list; applied by `Session._apply_staged`; `Session.set` unchanged); TSK-19, TSK-69.
- **Basis:** PI decision; an operational and data-integrity choice with no published basis. A welfare item (the C3 spec §14 item 1), approved for the design, "Approve all four", 2026-10-30. A hand-back does not pass through `Session.set`: it carries no new value, only the run's own, and never a reward size, which is no task setting a person holds; put to the PI with the plan as an amendment to the C3 spec's welfare item 3 (the engine C3 plan's Appendix A, item 5).

### TSK-68 — A person may change the numbers of a task's or a block's drawn range live; trials stay drawn, not overridden, and record the range they were drawn from; a condition's own range is not editable live
- **Decided:** 2026-10-30, the PI, in engine build C3's brainstorm: Q7b, "Yes, range changes live (Recommended)" -- from the next trial, recorded as a change, each trial recording the range it was drawn from. On a condition's own range changed live: "Not in C3 (Recommended)" -- a person may set one value over it (trials marked `overridden`) or hand it back; editing the range is a condition edit, which belongs to the rig-edit build. Engineering (the C3 spec §6; the engine C3 plan's call 22): the change is to the draw the open block uses, its own or the task's, for the rest of the run wherever that draw applies; the kind of distribution cannot change live (that is a task edit); numbers outside the declared range are re-checked widened, as a value is (TSK-51); numbers that cannot be drawn, or that would leave trials no animal can get right (TSK-69), are refused; a range travels by its own command, never as a `SetParameter`, its numbers decoded by `link._setting` unchanged. And 2026-10-31, the PI, on the engine C3 plan's Appendix B, item 18, "Judge the range as a whole (Recommended)": the new range is judged as a whole against the range the task writes -- if it reaches any value easier than the written range allows (for a uniform, either end moved the easier way; anything that cannot be read, or mixed, counts as easier, as doubt does), none of its trials count toward moving up until it is put back, by the written numbers sent again or by a revert (TRN-14) -- and its change row says which way it went (`meaning`'s `went`). That a normal's mean and cut and a wait's shortest, average and longest are read as a uniform's ends are, and a normal's spread changed as mixed, is engineering (the engine C3 plan's call 45).
- **Where:** [the C3 spec §6](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#6-live-edits); [`wl_xcon/link.py`](../../wl_xcon/link.py) (`SetRange`); [`wl_xcon/taskd.py`](../../wl_xcon/taskd.py) (`Session._command`, a branch beside the pause, handing to `Session._range`, off the list; applied by `Session._apply_staged`, and drawn from by `Session._draw`); [`wl_xcon/variation.py`](../../wl_xcon/variation.py) (`LIVE_NUMBERS`, `with_numbers`, `easier_range`); [`wl_xcon/check.py`](../../wl_xcon/check.py) (`undrawable`); TSK-51, TSK-64, TSK-67, TSK-69, TRN-14.
- **Basis:** PI decision; operational, with no published basis. ### Task 14: Revert
```

The C3 spec §8 (revert) and §14 items 1 and 3; the PI, 2026-10-07, TSK-43, "Yes, with revert" ("any earlier state restored in one action, itself recorded"), and 2026-10-30, "Approve all four" on the welfare items for the design (item 3: "Revert goes on the welfare summary: it restores task settings and drawn ranges only, never a bounded setting such as a reward size; each value goes through `Session.set` unchanged, and the revert is refused whole if any value is"); Calls 19 (its third step), 20 and 24; the outline review's I-1, M-5, M-15, M-16 and M-23. Task 2 put `link.Revert` on the wire, and a session refused it as a kind it does not act on. This task makes a session act on it, all of it off the welfare list but one branch:
- **A third branch in `_command`** (Global Constraints; Appendix A item 1). Right after Task 13's `SetRange` branch, before `if not isinstance(command, _link.SetParameter):`, a `Revert` goes to `Session._revert`, which returns after. It sits outside the listed `try`, so `_revert` never raises (Call 20; review I-1): it refuses what it cannot accept with `_refuse` and a sentence, a check that raises among them ("could not be checked ..., so it is refused, none of it applies, and the session runs on"). The listed `held` pass-through and `except` line are unchanged; `Session.set` and `link._setting` are byte-identical.
- **Moments** (Call 24; review M-23 moved them here from Task 7). `Session._moments` holds the run's start, `Moment(0, <its instant>, "the run's start", {}, {})`, and one `Moment` kept after each act `_apply_staged` applies that moves a task setting or a range: its change id, instant, the act in the feed's words, each setting a person holds with its value (`_edited`) and each draw changed live (`_ranges`, its change id left out), both in sorted order. A reward size's act keeps none; a clear and a switch take a change id (`_logged`, Task 7) and keep none. As each run starts, its start alone (`run`), with `Session._change_at_start`, the change ids above which are the run's own.
- **The revert** (Call 24). `command.change` is 0, the run's start, or a change id of the run in progress, which goes back to the latest moment at or before it, so a clear's or a switch's goes back to what was in force then (review M-15); one of an earlier run, one not made yet, and one that is no whole number from 0 (the wire's rule again, as `_clear` meets its own) are refused with a sentence. From what the run will hold once all offered ahead of it applies (`_ahead`): each setting held then at another value, or not held now, is set to its value then **through `Session.set`, unchanged**, and held again; each setting held now and not then is handed back to what gives it in the open block (`_to`, Task 13's rule, factored out: review M-16, "`to` reads the open block"); each draw changed live then or since goes back to its range then, or to the declared one (a `Pending` range whose `draw` is `None`). Nothing to revert is refused. `_possible` judges all of it at once, before any value is set.
- **Refused whole** (welfare item 3; review M-16). On any refusal, by `set` or by `_possible`, or a check that raises, `_staged` and `_pending` are cut back to their lengths before the revert, and `_acts` is written only once all of it is accepted: no change row is written and nothing applies. **It does not "write nothing"**: a warning `set` accepted (`_beyond_range`) for one of its values ahead of the refused one stays accepted, by that function's documented rule, and a test pins it.
- **One act** (Call 19, its third step). `_apply_staged` gives every change of one revert one change id (`Session._acts`, a value's place in `_staged` to its act; `Pending.act` for its hand-backs and ranges; `Session._act_moments`, an act to the change id it goes back to), each its own `PARAM_CHANGED` strobe, `sequence`, row and feed line, kind `revert`, with `moment` (the ask's table: a setting handed back reads `now` null and carries no `to`; a range keeps `from` and `block`). A change offered on its own is its own act.
- **Dropped between runs** (review M-5). `_after_service_run` says a revert it drops once, as the act it is, and clears `_acts` and `_act_moments` with `_staged`.

**Engineering calls made here** (each in the report):
- **A revert's hand-backs and ranges are offered ahead of its values, and its values in the order of their names.** `set` judges a value outside its range over what is offered ahead of it (`_ahead`), so a value judged before the revert's own hand-backs would be judged over what the revert is about to undo, and could be refused though the moment it goes back to was accepted. `test_a_revert_judges_each_value_over_what_it_hands_back_and_restores` pins the order. What remains: two values of one revert both outside their ranges are judged in name order, the first over the second's value before the revert.
- **A revert's row writes `was` as what the setting held just before it**, not `set`'s value before the inter-trial interval: another person's value applied ahead of the revert in the same drain is its `was`. A hand-back's and a range's `was` are read from `_ahead` as they are offered, which is the same value.
- **A revert to a change id goes back to what the run held then, and its rows' `moment` is the id asked for**, even where that id is a clear's, a switch's or a reward size's, which keep no moment of their own.
- **A reward size's act keeps no moment**, so the console's revert list (Task 17) never offers a moment a revert would not restore.
- **A revert that changes nothing is refused**, as a training switch to the value it holds is ("already on, so nothing changed").
- **A revert re-checks no restored range's extremes widened**: each was accepted by `_range` when offered, its extremes checked widened then, and `check.beyond_range` reasons over every declared range, so no value inside its own range can make them fail later (probed: a ring drawn down to 4° with 12 objects set before or after it is accepted either way, warned). The revert's `_possible` judges the range again with all the revert restores, and its values outside their ranges meet `set`'s widened checks with the ranges restored ahead of them. Such a re-check would be a line no test could fail.
- **By construction no check of the task refuses a revert**: it goes back exactly to a moment the run held, each act of which was checked as offered. So the refused-whole tests use this task's stand-in for a widened check that breaks the run (`_breaks`), and the check-that-raises test its stand-ins for checks that raise; the refusal path is welfare item 3's safety net.
- **`Session._act` counts for the session and is never reset**: an act is only ever told apart from another offered with it. `_acts` and `_act_moments` are cleared where `_staged` is.
- **Refusals are filed under `"revert"`**, the command's kind, as `_clear`'s are under `"clear"`: a revert names no one setting.

```python
"""Revert (engine build C3's spec §8 and §14 items 1 and 3).

The PI, 2026-10-07, TSK-43, "Yes, with revert": "any earlier state restored in one action, itself
recorded"; and 2026-10-30, "Approve all four", the C3 spec's welfare items for the design. Item
1: a third branch beside the pause in the welfare-listed `Session._command` hands `link.Revert` to
`Session._revert`, off the list, which never raises. Item 3: revert is on the welfare summary --
it restores task settings and drawn ranges only, never a bounded setting such as a reward size;
each value goes through `Session.set` unchanged, and the revert is refused whole if any value is.
A revert goes back to a moment of the run in progress (`Session._moments`: the run's start, then
one kept after each act) and applies at the next boundary as one act: one change id for all its
rows, kind `revert`, each naming the moment it goes back to.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

import _sessions
from _rig import DIRECT
from wl_xcon import taskd, variation
from wl_xcon.actor import Box
from wl_xcon.cli import _load_task
from wl_xcon.dio import Simulated as Card
from wl_xcon.findings import SESSION_KINDS, Finding
from wl_xcon.link import (
    CONTROL_HISTORY, ClearOwed, Drum, HandBack, Pause, Resume, Revert, SetParameter, SetRange,
    Simulated, Stop, Training,
)
from wl_xcon.photometry import SRGB
from wl_xcon.run import Scripted
from wl_xcon.task import FRESH, Block, Condition, SaccadeTo, Uniform
from wl_xcon.taskd import RunSpec, Session, SessionSpec
from wl_xcon.welfare import Deployment, Simulated as Pump

#: The wall every session here reads from, plus its frames' seconds (`_session`).
WALL_NOW = 1_700_000_000.0
SEED = 7
JAKE = Box("jake")
ANA = Box("ana")
#: Jake and Ana as a change row writes them.
BY = {"kind": "box", "name": "jake"}
ANA_BY = {"kind": "box", "name": "ana"}
#: `PARAM_CHANGED`'s code in the reference allocation: what each change row here strobes.
PARAM_CHANGED = 4130
#: The reference task's fixation hold's meaning, and its fixation point's luminance's, as a
#: change row writes them.
FIX_HOLD = {"kind": "clear-cut", "role": "criterion", "raising": "harder", "relative_to": None}
FIX_LUMINANCE = {"kind": "expected", "role": "stimulus", "raising": "easier",
                 "relative_to": "background"}
#: The task's draw of the fixation hold, every trial afresh.
DRAWN = '{"fix_hold": Uniform(0.2, 0.4, repeat=FRESH)}'
#: `visual_search`'s values: its target red among green, a ring of six objects 8° out.
SEARCH = _load_task(Path("tasks/visual_search.py"))
((RED, GREEN, _),) = [p.choices for p in SEARCH.params if p.name == "target_appearance"]
SEARCHED = {"fix_acquisition": 4.0, "fix_hold": 0.3, "response_deadline": 0.6,
            "target_hold": 0.2, "fix_window": 2.0, "object_window": 0.5,
            "array_eccentricity": 8.0, "set_size": 6, "target_index": 0,
            "array_rotation": 0.0, "fix_luminance": 40.0,
            "target_appearance": RED, "distractor_appearance": GREEN}


def _near(target: int) -> Block:
    """One block of one condition placing the target 5° out, owing `target` trials."""
    return Block("b", [Condition("near", {"target_x": 5.0}, target=target)])


def _right(values: dict) -> Scripted:
    """A trial the animal gets right, whatever its holds: it holds the fixation point 20 frames
    past its hold, then looks at the target and stays on it 400 frames, past any target hold."""
    held = round(values["fix_hold"] * 240) + 20
    return Scripted({SaccadeTo("target"): held + 10},
                    inside={frame: "fix" if frame <= held else "target"
                            for frame in range(1, held + 400)})


def _always_right(trial, values, index) -> Scripted:
    return _right(values)


def _spec(tmp_path, task, **over) -> SessionSpec:
    spec = SessionSpec(
        task=str(task), allocation="tasks/allocation.py", root=tmp_path,
        session_id="2027-01-14_01", subject="A", trials=400, frame_period=1 / 240, seed=SEED,
        values={"target_appearance": None}, bounds=_sessions.bounds(),
        already_delivered_today=0.0, deployment=Deployment.RIG_FIXED, geometry=DIRECT,
        session_kind="training", calibration=SRGB,
    )
    for name, value in over.items():
        setattr(spec, name, value)
    return spec


def _session(spec, link=None, world=_always_right, *, service=False) -> Session:
    """On the simulators, its wall following its frames from `WALL_NOW`, the animal out of its
    cage and its head fixed then; the animal right on every trial unless `world` says otherwise,
    the simulated animal where it is `None`; a `wlx taskd` session, opened, where `service`."""
    session = Session(spec, card=Card(), pump=Pump(),
                      link=link if link is not None else Simulated(), service=service)
    session.wall_clock = lambda: WALL_NOW + session.now()
    session.left_cage(at=WALL_NOW)
    session.head_fixed(at=session.wall_now())
    session.world = world
    if service:
        session.open(how="wlx taskd")
    return session


class _Drained(Simulated):
    """A link that queues `script[n]` as the `n`th drain begins. The loop drains once before each
    trial, once each time the plan moves to another block, and once each pass while paused; a
    command drained before trial `n` applies from trial `n + 1`."""

    def __init__(self, script):
        super().__init__()
        self.script, self.drains = dict(script), 0

    def drain(self) -> list:
        self.drains += 1
        for command in self.script.get(self.drains, ()):
            self.queue(command)
        return super().drain()


def _rows(session: Session, name: str) -> list[dict]:
    """The rows of one of the session's files, none where it was never written."""
    path = session.directory / name
    return [json.loads(line) for line in path.read_text().splitlines()] if path.exists() else []


def _lines(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    return _rows(session, "trials.jsonl")


def _changes(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    return _rows(session, "parameter_changes.jsonl")


def _reverted(session: Session) -> list[dict]:
    return [row for row in _changes(session) if row["kind"] == "revert"]


def _without_instants(row: dict) -> dict:
    return {key: value for key, value in row.items() if key not in ("at", "at_local")}


def _fed(session: Session, *kinds: str) -> list[tuple]:
    """The changes feed's lines of `kinds`, as `(kind, by, said)`."""
    return [(kind, by, said) for kind, by, _, said in session.controls if kind in kinds]


def _edited(path: Path, *edits: tuple[str, str], tail: str = "") -> Path:
    """`path` with each `(old, new)` made, each `old` found once, and `tail` appended."""
    text = path.read_text()
    for old, new in edits:
        assert text.count(old) == 1, old
        text = text.replace(old, new)
    path.write_text(text + tail)
    return path


def _ceiling(folder: Path) -> Path:
    """`varied_task` declaring a setting named as the reward ceiling is, `reward_correct`, which
    nothing reads, with a meaning, as a task may (as `tests/test_hand_back_and_ranges.py`'s does).
    Engine test material."""
    return _edited(
        _sessions.varied_task(folder, name="ceiling"),
        ('        Param("target_hold", unit="s", low=0.05, high=1.0, start=0.2),',
         '        Param("reward_correct", unit="mL", low=0.0, high=1.0),\n'
         '        Param("target_hold", unit="s", low=0.05, high=1.0, start=0.2),'),
        tail=("from wl_xcon.task import NEITHER, NOT_DIFFICULTY, Meaning\n"
              "TASK = _dataclasses.replace(TASK, meanings={'reward_correct': Meaning(\n"
              "    NOT_DIFFICULTY, NEITHER, note='named as a ceiling is, read by nothing')})\n"))


def _breaks(monkeypatch, refused: tuple[str, float], warned: tuple[str, float] | None = None):
    """**This file's stand-in for a value whose widened checks break the run**, installed from
    the moment it is called: `check.beyond_range`, as `Session._beyond_range` meets it, refuses
    values holding `refused`'s setting at its value with a finding that blocks, and gives values
    holding `warned`'s, where given, a warning of its own, a sentence never accepted before. A
    revert restores what the run held at an earlier moment, which every check passed when it was
    set, so no check of the task itself refuses one: only a check that answers otherwise now."""
    real = taskd.beyond_range

    def standing_in(task, values, *args, **kwargs):
        found = real(task, values, *args, **kwargs)
        name, value = refused
        if values.get(name) == value:
            return [*found, Finding("stand-in", f"{name!r} at {value:g} breaks the run here")]
        if warned is not None and values.get(warned[0]) == warned[1]:
            return [*found, Finding("stand-in-warning", f"{warned[0]!r} at {warned[1]:g} is warned",
                                    blocking=False, accepted_in=SESSION_KINDS)]
        return found

    monkeypatch.setattr(taskd, "beyond_range", standing_in)


def test_a_revert_restores_each_value_held_or_handed_back_and_each_range_as_then(tmp_path):
    """The C3 spec §8 ("each task setting to its value then, held or handed back as it was then,
    and each drawn range as it was"). A person holds the target's place over its condition's and
    its height, and narrows the task's draw of the fixation hold (changes 1 to 3); then hands the
    place back, moves the height, narrows the draw again and holds the fixation point's luminance
    (4 to 7). The revert to change 3 puts back each value held then through `set` -- the place,
    held over its condition's again, and the height -- hands back the luminance, held since, and
    puts the draw back as it was then: from the next trial on, as after change 3, the hold drawn
    from that range and naming the revert's change."""
    path = _sessions.varied_task(tmp_path, draws=DRAWN)
    key = ("task", "fix_hold")
    then, since = Uniform(0.2, 0.3, repeat=FRESH), Uniform(0.25, 0.3, repeat=FRESH)
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=2.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetRange(name="fix_hold", numbers={"high": 0.3}, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [HandBack(name="target_x", by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=3.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetRange(name="fix_hold", numbers={"low": 0.25}, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="fix_luminance", value=50.0, by=JAKE)],
                     6: [Revert(change=3, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, path, blocks=[_near(8)]), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    lines = _lines(session)
    assert [(line["params"]["target_x"], line["params"]["target_y"],
             line["params"]["fix_luminance"], line["live"], line["overridden"], line["drawn"])
            for line in lines] == (
        [(5.0, 0.0, 40.0, [], [], {"fix_hold": "task"})] * 2
        + [(12.0, 2.0, 40.0, ["target_x", "target_y"], ["target_x"], {"fix_hold": 3})] * 2
        + [(5.0, 3.0, 50.0, ["fix_luminance", "target_y"], [], {"fix_hold": 6})] * 2
        + [(12.0, 2.0, 40.0, ["target_x", "target_y"], ["target_x"], {"fix_hold": 8})] * 2)
    assert [line["params"]["fix_hold"] for line in lines[6:]] == [
        variation.draw(then, SEED, 6, key), variation.draw(then, SEED, 7, key)]
    assert [(row["change"], row["sequence"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"], row["moment"])
            for row in _reverted(session)] == [
        (8, 8, "fix_luminance", 50.0, None, 3),
        (8, 9, "fix_hold", variation.recorded(since), variation.recorded(then), 3),
        (8, 10, "target_x", 10.0, 12.0, 3),
        (8, 11, "target_y", 3.0, 2.0, 3)]
    assert (session._ranges, session._edited) == (
        {key: (then, 8)}, frozenset({"target_x", "target_y"}))
    assert (session.spec.values["target_x"], session.spec.values["fix_luminance"]) == (12.0, 40.0)


def test_a_revert_to_the_runs_start_hands_everything_back_and_restores_the_declared_ranges(
        tmp_path):
    """The C3 spec §8, a revert to change 0, the run's start: every setting a person holds is
    handed back to what gives it in the open block -- the target's place to its condition, its
    height to the run -- and every draw changed live, the block's own and the task's, is put back
    as declared. Its rows say so: a setting handed back now null, its `to` left out; a draw as
    declared, with every field and whose draw it was (`from`, `block`); each naming the moment, 0.
    The trials after it draw from the declared draws again, naming them as declared. A revert
    then to change 4 brings all of it back, each range from the one declared, naming its change."""
    path = _sessions.varied_task(tmp_path, draws=(
        '{"fix_hold": Uniform(0.2, 0.4, repeat=FRESH), '
        '"fix_luminance": Uniform(30.0, 50.0, repeat=FRESH)}'))
    declared = _load_task(path).draws["fix_luminance"]
    own = Uniform(0.5, 0.6, repeat=FRESH)
    own_key, task_key = ("block", "own", "fix_hold"), ("task", "fix_luminance")
    blocks = [Block("own", [Condition("near", {"target_x": 5.0}, target=8)],
                    draws={"fix_hold": own})]
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=2.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetRange(name="fix_hold", numbers={"high": 0.7}, by=JAKE),
                         SetRange(name="fix_luminance", numbers={"low": 35.0}, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [Revert(change=0, by=JAKE)],
                     6: [Revert(change=4, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, path, blocks=blocks), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    lines = _lines(session)
    assert [(line["params"]["target_x"], line["params"]["target_y"], line["live"],
             line["drawn"]) for line in lines] == (
        [(5.0, 0.0, [], {"fix_hold": "block", "fix_luminance": "task"})] * 2
        + [(12.0, 2.0, ["target_x", "target_y"], {"fix_hold": 3, "fix_luminance": 4})] * 2
        + [(5.0, 0.0, [], {"fix_hold": "block", "fix_luminance": "task"})] * 2
        + [(12.0, 2.0, ["target_x", "target_y"], {"fix_hold": 6, "fix_luminance": 6})] * 2)
    assert [(line["params"]["fix_hold"], line["params"]["fix_luminance"])
            for line in lines[4:6]] == [
        (variation.draw(own, SEED, index, own_key), variation.draw(declared, SEED, index, task_key))
        for index in (4, 5)]
    widened, raised = Uniform(0.5, 0.7, repeat=FRESH), Uniform(35.0, 50.0, repeat=FRESH)
    reverted = _reverted(session)
    assert [(row["change"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"], row.get("from"),
             row.get("block"), row["moment"]) for row in reverted] == [
        (5, "target_x", 12.0, None, None, None, 0),
        (5, "target_y", 2.0, None, None, None, 0),
        (5, "fix_hold", variation.recorded(widened), variation.recorded(own), "block", "own", 0),
        (5, "fix_luminance", variation.recorded(raised), variation.recorded(declared), "task",
         None, 0),
        (6, "fix_hold", variation.recorded(own), variation.recorded(widened), "block", "own", 4),
        (6, "fix_luminance", variation.recorded(declared), variation.recorded(raised), "task",
         None, 4),
        (6, "target_x", 10.0, 12.0, None, None, 4),
        (6, "target_y", 0.0, 2.0, None, None, 4)]
    assert _without_instants(reverted[3]) == {
        "change": 5, "kind": "revert", "name": "fix_luminance",
        "was": variation.recorded(raised), "now": variation.recorded(declared),
        "from": "task", "block": None, "moment": 0,
        "by": BY, "trial_number": 5, "run": 0,
        "meaning": {**FIX_LUMINANCE, "went": None, "step": None},
        "offered": [], "odds": None, "event_code": PARAM_CHANGED, "sequence": 8,
    }
    assert "to" not in reverted[0] and "to" not in reverted[1]
    assert (session._ranges, session._edited) == (
        {own_key: (widened, 6), task_key: (raised, 6)}, frozenset({"target_x", "target_y"}))
    assert _fed(session, "revert")[:4] == [
        ("revert", JAKE, "target_x 12.00 handed back to its conditions, reverting to the run's "
                         "start, from trial 4"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "target_y 2.00 handed back to the run's 0.00, reverting to the run's "
                         "start, from trial 4"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "block 'own''s draw of 'fix_hold' → as declared, reverting to the run's "
                         "start, from trial 4"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "the task's draw of 'fix_luminance' → as declared, reverting to the "
                         "run's start, from trial 4")]


def test_a_revert_is_one_change_its_rows_naming_the_moment(tmp_path):
    """XC-288 §3.4 and the C3 spec §8 ("one `change` id for the whole revert"): every row of one
    revert shares one change id, kind `revert`, each with the moment it goes back to, each its own
    `PARAM_CHANGED` strobe and `sequence`. Each row's `was` is what the setting held just before
    it: here the fixation hold another person set in the same drain, applied ahead of the revert
    with its own change id, not the value before that drain (`set`'s `was`). A setting handed back
    reads `now` null. A value set after the revert applied is an act, and a change, of its own."""
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.7, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=2.0, by=JAKE)],
                     6: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.9, by=ANA),
                         Revert(change=1, by=JAKE)],
                     8: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(10)]), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    rows = _changes(session)
    assert [(row["change"], row["sequence"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"],
             row["by"], row.get("moment")) for row in rows] == [
        (1, 1, "set", "fix_hold", 0.3, 0.5, BY, None),
        (2, 2, "set", "fix_hold", 0.5, 0.7, BY, None),
        (3, 3, "set", "target_y", 0.0, 2.0, BY, None),
        (4, 4, "set", "fix_hold", 0.7, 0.9, ANA_BY, None),
        (5, 5, "revert", "target_y", 2.0, None, BY, 1),
        (5, 6, "revert", "fix_hold", 0.9, 0.5, BY, 1),
        (6, 7, "set", "target_x", 10.0, 12.0, BY, None)]
    assert rows[5]["meaning"] == {**FIX_HOLD, "went": "easier", "step": -0.4}
    assert session.card.codes.count(PARAM_CHANGED) == 7
    assert [(line["params"]["fix_hold"], line["params"]["target_y"], line["live"])
            for line in _lines(session)[5:]] == [
        (0.7, 2.0, ["fix_hold", "target_y"])] + [(0.5, 0.0, ["fix_hold"])] * 2 + [
        (0.5, 0.0, ["fix_hold", "target_x"])] * 2
    assert _fed(session, "revert") == [
        ("revert", JAKE, "target_y 2.00 handed back to the run's 0.00, reverting to change 1, "
                         "from trial 6"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "fix_hold 0.90 → 0.50, reverting to change 1, from trial 6")]
    assert (session._acts, session._act_moments) == ({}, {})


def test_a_moment_is_kept_after_each_act_the_first_the_runs_start(tmp_path):
    """The engine C3 plan's call 24 ("rebuilt from `Session._moments`, a snapshot after each act"):
    the run's start first, change 0, holding nothing; then, after each act as it applies, its
    change id and instant, the act in the feed's words, and what the live layer holds -- each
    setting a person holds with its value, and each draw changed live -- a revert's among them.
    The revert to change 2 puts back the target's place; the range it finds as it was then."""
    path = _sessions.varied_task(tmp_path, draws=DRAWN)
    key, narrowed = ("task", "fix_hold"), Uniform(0.2, 0.3, repeat=FRESH)
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE),
                         SetRange(name="fix_hold", numbers={"high": 0.3}, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [HandBack(name="target_x", by=JAKE)],
                     6: [Revert(change=2, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, path, blocks=[_near(8)]), link)

    session.run()

    at, moment = {row["change"]: row["at"] for row in _changes(session)}, taskd.Moment
    assert session._moments == [
        moment(0, WALL_NOW, "the run's start", {}, {}),
        moment(1, at[1], "target_x 10.00 → 12.00", {"target_x": 12.0}, {}),
        moment(2, at[2], "the task's draw of 'fix_hold' → uniform from 0.2 s to 0.3 s",
               {"target_x": 12.0}, {key: narrowed}),
        moment(3, at[3], "target_x 12.00 handed back to its conditions", {}, {key: narrowed}),
        moment(4, at[4], "reverted to change 2", {"target_x": 12.0}, {key: narrowed}),
    ]
    assert [(row["kind"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"]) for row in _reverted(session)] == [
        ("revert", "target_x", 10.0, 12.0)]


def test_every_moment_of_the_run_is_kept_past_the_consoles_cap_its_start_first(tmp_path):
    """The outline review's M-15: the console's list of moments is capped, keeping the run's start
    (`link.CONTROL_HISTORY`; telemetry schema 19, the engine C3 plan's Task 17). The session keeps
    every moment of the run, its start first, so a revert reaches any change of it, the first
    among them, however many came after: 55 values set in one drain, then a revert to change 1."""
    held = [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=round(0.3 + step / 100, 2), by=JAKE)
            for step in range(1, 56)]
    link = _Drained({2: held, 4: [Revert(change=1, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(6)]), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    assert len(session._moments) == 57 > CONTROL_HISTORY
    assert (session._moments[0].change, session._moments[0].said) == (0, "the run's start")
    (row,) = _reverted(session)
    assert (row["change"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"], row["moment"]) == (
        56, "fix_hold", 0.85, 0.31, 1)
    assert [line["params"]["fix_hold"] for line in _lines(session)[2:]] == [0.85] * 2 + [0.31] * 2


def test_a_revert_to_a_clears_change_restores_the_moment_in_force_then(tmp_path):
    """The engine C3 plan's call 24 (its review, M-15): a clear, a drumming switch and a training
    switch each take a change id and keep no moment, since they move no setting and no range; a
    revert to one goes back to what was in force then, the latest moment at or before it, and its
    rows name the id it was given. Counts and training aids are not reverted (the C3 spec §8): the
    trial cleared stays cleared, drumming and *clear* stay on, and their control rows stand."""
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)],
                     3: [Training(setting="clear", on=True, by=JAKE),
                         ClearOwed(condition="near", by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=2.0, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [Drum(scope="block", by=JAKE)],
                     5: [SetParameter(name="fix_luminance", value=50.0, by=JAKE)],
                     7: [Revert(change=3, by=JAKE)],
                     9: [Revert(change=5, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(12)]), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"]) for row in _changes(session)][:6] == [
        (1, "set", "target_x"), (2, "training", "clear"), (3, "clear", "owed"),
        (4, "set", "target_y"), (5, "drum", "drumming"), (6, "set", "fix_luminance")]
    assert [(row["change"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"], row["moment"])
            for row in _reverted(session)] == [
        (7, "fix_luminance", 50.0, None, 3), (7, "target_y", 2.0, None, 3),
        (8, "target_y", 0.0, 2.0, 5)]
    assert [m.change for m in session._moments] == [0, 1, 4, 6, 7, 8]
    assert [(line["params"]["target_y"], line["params"]["fix_luminance"])
            for line in _lines(session)] == (
        [(0.0, 40.0)] * 3 + [(2.0, 40.0)] * 2 + [(2.0, 50.0)] * 2 + [(0.0, 40.0)] * 2
        + [(2.0, 40.0)] * 2)
    scheduler = session._scheduler
    assert (scheduler.drumming, scheduler.clearing) == ("block", True)
    assert [(s.condition, s.trials, s.because) for s in scheduler.shortfalls] == [
        ("near", 1, "cleared")]
    assert [row["kind"] for row in _rows(session, "controls.jsonl")
            if row["kind"] in ("clear", "drum", "training")] == ["training", "clear", "drum"]


def test_a_revert_is_refused_whole_when_one_value_is_and_writes_no_change_row(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """The C3 spec's welfare item 3 ("each value goes through `Session.set` unchanged, and the
    revert is refused whole if any value is"), with this file's stand-in for a value whose widened
    checks break the run. The revert to change 2 puts back two values outside their declared
    ranges, each through `set`: the fixation hold first, accepted with a warning the stand-in
    gives it, then the response deadline, refused. The whole revert is refused with `set`'s
    sentence: no change row is written and nothing applies -- what it staged and offered is cut
    back, and the trials after run as before. The warning `set` accepted for the earlier value
    stays accepted, by `_beyond_range`'s rule (the outline review's M-16)."""
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=2.5, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="response_deadline", value=3.5, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [HandBack(name="fix_hold", by=JAKE),
                         HandBack(name="response_deadline", by=JAKE)],
                     6: [Revert(change=2, by=JAKE)]})

    def world(trial, values, index):
        if index == 4:
            # After the two hand-backs were offered (the 4th drain), before the revert is.
            _breaks(monkeypatch, ("response_deadline", 3.5), warned=("fix_hold", 2.5))
        return _right(values)

    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(8)]), link,
                       world=world)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == [("revert", JAKE, (
        "the revert to change 2 is refused, and none of it applies: 'response_deadline' at 3.5 "
        "is outside its declared range, and with the range widened to it the load-time checks "
        "refuse it: stand-in: 'response_deadline' at 3.5 breaks the run here; the previous value "
        "stands"))]
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"]) for row in _changes(session)] == [
        (1, "set", "fix_hold"), (2, "set", "response_deadline"),
        (3, "hand_back", "fix_hold"), (4, "hand_back", "response_deadline")]
    (*_, kept) = _rows(session, "warnings.jsonl")
    assert (kept["code"], kept["detail"], kept["by"]) == (
        "stand-in-warning", "'fix_hold' at 2.5 is warned", BY)
    assert (session._staged, session._pending, session._acts, session._act_moments) == (
        [], [], {}, {})
    assert [(line["params"]["fix_hold"], line["params"]["response_deadline"], line["live"])
            for line in _lines(session)[4:]] == [(0.3, 0.6, [])] * 4


def test_a_revert_refused_whole_leaves_another_persons_staged_change_alone(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch):
    """Review Focus 3 (the C3 spec §8; `_hold` drains through `_command`): while the session is
    paused, Ana sets the fixation point's luminance, then Jake sends two reverts in the same
    drain. The first, to change 1, would put back a response deadline whose widened checks this
    file's stand-in breaks: it is refused whole, and Ana's value stays staged. The second, to
    change 3, is accepted: it hands back what is held since, Ana's luminance among the rest, since
    a revert goes back to its moment whatever changed since. At the resume Ana's change applies
    first with its own change id, and the revert after it as one act."""
    waiting = []

    class Watched(_Drained):
        def drain(self) -> list:
            if self.drains == 7:
                # As the 8th drain, the resume's, begins: what the paused drain left offered.
                waiting.append((list(session._staged),
                                [(act.kind, act.name, act.act) for act in session._pending],
                                dict(session._act_moments)))
            return super().drain()

    link = Watched({2: [SetParameter(name="response_deadline", value=3.5, by=JAKE)],
                    3: [HandBack(name="response_deadline", by=JAKE),
                        SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=JAKE)],
                    5: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)],
                    6: [Pause(by=JAKE)],
                    7: [SetParameter(name="fix_luminance", value=50.0, by=ANA),
                        Revert(change=1, by=JAKE), Revert(change=3, by=JAKE)],
                    8: [Resume(by=JAKE)]})

    def world(trial, values, index):
        if index == 3:
            # After the response deadline was handed back, before anything is reverted.
            _breaks(monkeypatch, ("response_deadline", 3.5))
        return _right(values)

    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(8)]), link,
                       world=world)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == [("revert", JAKE, (
        "the revert to change 1 is refused, and none of it applies: 'response_deadline' at 3.5 "
        "is outside its declared range, and with the range widened to it the load-time checks "
        "refuse it: stand-in: 'response_deadline' at 3.5 breaks the run here; the previous value "
        "stands"))]
    ((staged, pending, moments),) = waiting
    (act,) = moments
    assert (staged, pending, moments) == (
        [("fix_luminance", 40.0, 50.0, ANA, False)],
        [("hand_back", "fix_luminance", act), ("hand_back", "target_x", act)], {act: 3})
    rows = _changes(session)
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"], row["by"])
            for row in rows[4:]] == [
        (5, "set", "fix_luminance", 40.0, 50.0, ANA_BY),
        (6, "revert", "fix_luminance", 50.0, None, BY),
        (6, "revert", "target_x", 12.0, None, BY)]
    kinds = [kind for kind, _, _, _ in session.controls]
    assert kinds.index("pause") < kinds.index("resume") < kinds.index("set", kinds.index(
        "resume")) < kinds.index("revert")
    assert [(line["params"]["fix_luminance"], line["params"]["target_x"], line["live"])
            for line in _lines(session)[5:]] == [(40.0, 5.0, ["fix_hold"])] * 3


@pytest.mark.parametrize("broken", ["impossible", "possible", "beyond_range", "set"])
def test_a_check_that_raises_inside_a_revert_refuses_it_and_the_session_runs_on(
        tmp_path, monkeypatch, broken):
    """Review Focus 5, the revert's part (the outline review's I-1; the C3 plan's call 20): a
    revert runs beside the pause, outside `_command`'s listed `try`, so it refuses its own faults.
    A check that raises -- `check.impossible`, as `_possible` meets it and says it could not run;
    `_possible` itself; `check.beyond_range`, as `set`'s `_beyond_range` meets it and refuses the
    value; `set` itself, on the second of the two values the revert puts back -- refuses the
    revert whole, saying so, and the session runs to its end with nothing of the revert applied:
    the hand-back it offered and the value it staged ahead of the fault are cut back too. The
    stand-ins are this file's own: each raises from the trial after the values the revert puts
    back were set and handed back, so that they were checked first."""
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=2.5, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)],
                     3: [HandBack(name="fix_hold", by=JAKE), HandBack(name="target_x", by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_y", value=2.0, by=JAKE)],
                     5: [Revert(change=2, by=JAKE)]})

    def raising(*args, **kwargs):
        raise ZeroDivisionError("division by zero")

    def world(trial, values, index):
        if index == 3:
            # After the hand-backs were applied (the 4th trial), before the revert is offered.
            if broken == "possible":
                monkeypatch.setattr(session, "_possible", raising)
            elif broken == "set":
                real = session.set
                monkeypatch.setattr(session, "set", lambda name, value, by: (
                    raising() if name == "target_x" else real(name, value, by=by)))
            else:
                monkeypatch.setattr(taskd, broken, raising)
        return _right(values)

    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/fixation_detection.py", blocks=[_near(7)]), link,
                       world=world)

    session.run()

    assert session.stop_kind == "completed"
    assert session.refusals == [("revert", JAKE, {
        "impossible": "the revert to change 2 is refused, and none of it applies: the check for "
                      "trials no animal can get right could not be run (ZeroDivisionError: "
                      "division by zero)",
        "beyond_range": "the revert to change 2 is refused, and none of it applies: 'fix_hold' "
                        "at 2.5 is outside its declared range, and the load-time checks could "
                        "not be run again with the range widened (ZeroDivisionError: division by "
                        "zero), so it is refused and the previous value stands",
    }.get(broken, "the revert to change 2 could not be checked (ZeroDivisionError: division by "
                  "zero), so it is refused, none of it applies, and the session runs on"))]
    assert [row["kind"] for row in _changes(session)] == [
        "set", "set", "hand_back", "hand_back", "set"]
    assert (session._staged, session._pending, session._edited) == (
        [], [], frozenset({"target_y"}))
    assert {(line["params"]["fix_hold"], line["params"]["target_x"])
            for line in _lines(session)[4:]} == {(0.3, 5.0)}


def test_a_revert_never_moves_a_reward_size(tmp_path):
    """The C3 spec's welfare item 3 ("never a bounded setting such as a reward size"; engine spec
    §17.6): a reward size a person sets is a ceiling's, staged and applied by `set`'s and
    `bounds`' own branch, never held as a task setting, even where the task declares a setting of
    its name. So its act keeps no moment, no moment holds it, and a revert -- even to its own
    change id, which goes back to the moment in force then -- hands back the task's own setting
    and leaves the reward size where the person last set it."""
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="reward_correct", value=0.2, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=JAKE)],
                     4: [SetParameter(name="reward_correct", value=0.25, by=JAKE)],
                     6: [Revert(change=1, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, _ceiling(tmp_path), trials=8), link)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    assert session.spec.bounds.value("reward_correct") == 0.25
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["now"]) for row in
            _changes(session)] == [
        (1, "set", "reward_correct", 0.2), (2, "set", "fix_hold", 0.5),
        (3, "set", "reward_correct", 0.25), (4, "revert", "fix_hold", None)]
    assert [moment.change for moment in session._moments] == [0, 2, 4]
    assert all("reward_correct" not in moment.held for moment in session._moments)


def test_a_revert_to_an_earlier_runs_change_or_an_unknown_one_is_refused(tmp_path):
    """The engine C3 plan's call 24 and its Appendix B item 5 ("Revert reaches back within the
    current run"): in a `wlx taskd` session's second run, a revert to a change of the first run,
    to one not made yet, or to the run's start while nothing has changed since, is refused with
    its sentence; one whose change is no whole number from 0 is refused by the wire's own rule,
    since a command can reach the session another way. The second run's moments begin with its
    own start; a revert to its own change goes back to it."""
    path = _sessions.varied_task(tmp_path)
    link = _Drained({1: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=JAKE)],
                     3: [Stop(by=JAKE)],
                     4: [Revert(change=0, by=JAKE), Revert(change=1, by=JAKE),
                         Revert(change=9, by=JAKE), Revert(change=-1, by=JAKE),
                         Revert(change=True, by=JAKE), Revert(change="2", by=JAKE)],
                     5: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)],
                     6: [HandBack(name="target_x", by=JAKE)],
                     8: [Revert(change=2, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "", trials=0, values={}), link, service=True)
    run = RunSpec(task=str(path), trials=10, seed=SEED, values={"target_appearance": None})

    session.run(run)
    session.run(run)

    wire = ("a 'revert' command's change is a whole number from 0, and {} is not one, so it is "
            "refused")
    assert session.refusals == [
        ("revert", JAKE, "the revert to the run's start is refused, and none of it applies: the "
                         "run holds now what it held then, so there is nothing to revert"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "the revert to change 1 is refused, and none of it applies: change 1 was "
                         "made before run 2 started, and a revert goes back within the run in "
                         "progress, to one of its changes or to its start (0)"),
        ("revert", JAKE, "the revert to change 9 is refused, and none of it applies: no change 9 "
                         "has been made yet"),
        ("revert", JAKE, wire.format("-1")), ("revert", JAKE, wire.format("True")),
        ("revert", JAKE, wire.format("'2'")),
    ]
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["run"]) for row in
            _changes(session)] == [
        (1, "set", "fix_hold", 0), (2, "set", "target_x", 1), (3, "hand_back", "target_x", 1),
        (4, "revert", "target_x", 1)]
    assert [moment.change for moment in session._moments] == [0, 2, 3, 4]
    assert session._moments[0].said == "the run's start"


def test_a_revert_drained_with_a_stop_is_dropped_and_said(tmp_path):
    """The b3a-1 plan's decision 2, for a revert (the outline review's M-5): between a `wlx taskd`
    session's runs nothing applies what was offered, so a revert drained with the stop that ends a
    run -- here a value put back and a setting handed back -- is dropped, said once on the feed,
    as the one act it is, and not written; and what it staged is forgotten with it, so the next
    run's first value is a change of its own, no revert's."""
    path = _sessions.varied_task(tmp_path)
    link = _Drained({1: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.5, by=JAKE)],
                     2: [SetParameter(name="fix_hold", value=0.7, by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)],
                     3: [Revert(change=1, by=JAKE), Stop(by=JAKE)],
                     4: [SetParameter(name="target_x", value=12.0, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "", trials=0, values={}), link, service=True)
    run = RunSpec(task=str(path), trials=4, seed=SEED, values={"target_appearance": None})

    session.run(run)

    assert _fed(session, "revert") == [
        ("revert", JAKE, "the revert to change 1 was not applied: run 1 ended first")]
    assert (session._staged, session._acts, session._act_moments) == ([], {}, {})

    session.run(run)

    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["run"]) for row in _changes(session)] == [
        (1, "set", "fix_hold", 0), (2, "set", "fix_hold", 0), (3, "set", "target_x", 0),
        (4, "set", "target_x", 1)]


def test_a_revert_judges_each_value_over_what_it_hands_back_and_restores(tmp_path):
    """An engineering call of the engine C3 plan's Task 14: a revert offers its hand-backs and
    ranges ahead of its values, so `set` judges each value over the moment the revert goes back
    to, not over what it is about to undo. 13 objects fit on `visual_search`'s 8° ring (change 1);
    then the set size is handed back and the ring drawn in to 4°, past its declared 5° (warned:
    six fit there). The revert to change 1 hands the ring back to 8° and puts 13 objects back:
    judged on the 8° ring, they are accepted; judged on the 4° one, they would crowd it."""
    blocks = [Block("ring", [Condition("any", {}, target=8)])]
    link = _Drained({2: [SetParameter(name="set_size", value=13, by=JAKE)],
                     3: [HandBack(name="set_size", by=JAKE),
                         SetParameter(name="array_eccentricity", value=4.0, by=JAKE)],
                     5: [Revert(change=1, by=JAKE)]})
    session = _session(_spec(tmp_path, "tasks/visual_search.py", blocks=blocks,
                             values=dict(SEARCHED)), link, world=None)

    session.run()

    assert session.refusals == []
    assert [(row["change"], row["kind"], row["name"], row["was"], row["now"])
            for row in _changes(session)] == [
        (1, "set", "set_size", 6, 13), (2, "hand_back", "set_size", 13, 6),
        (3, "set", "array_eccentricity", 8.0, 4.0),
        (4, "revert", "array_eccentricity", 4.0, None), (4, "revert", "set_size", 6, 13)]
    lines = _lines(session)
    assert len(lines) > 6 and all(
        (line["params"]["set_size"], line["params"]["array_eccentricity"]) == (13, 8.0)
        for line in lines[5:])
```

```python
def _draw_said(key: tuple) -> str:
    """A draw named by its key (`variation.in_force`'s, `own_ranges`'), as a sentence says it."""

    if key[0] == "block":
        return f"block {key[1]!r}'s draw of {key[2]!r}"
    return f"condition {key[1]!r}'s own range for {key[2]!r}"
```

```python
class Moment:
    """**A moment of the run a revert can go back to** (engine build C3's spec §8; the PI,
    2026-10-07, TSK-43, "Yes, with revert": "any earlier state restored in one action"): what the
    run's live layer held just after an act applied (`Session._apply_staged`), or as the run
    started. Kept in `Session._moments`, the run's start first.

    - `change` is the act's change id, or 0 for the run's start. A revert to any change id of the
      run goes back to the latest moment at or before it (`Session._revert`), so a clear's or a
      switch's, which keep none, goes back to what was in force then.
    - `at` is when it was kept, on the session's anchored clock; `said`, the act in the changes
      feed's words, or "the run's start".
    - `held` is each task setting a person held then, by name, with its value; `ranges`, each draw
      changed live then, by its key (`variation.in_force`'s), with the distribution in force.
      **Never a bounded setting**: a reward size is no task setting a person holds
      (`Session._edited`) and no draw, so no moment holds one, and no revert reaches one."""

    change: int
    at: float
    said: str
    held: dict
    ranges: dict
```

```python
    def _offered_acts(self) -> list[tuple[object, int | None]]:
        """**`_offered`'s changes, each with the act it belongs to** (engine build C3's spec §8):
        a revert's (`_revert`) -- for a value it staged, from `_acts` by the value's place in
        `_staged`; for a hand-back or a range it offered, its `Pending.act` -- or `None` for a
        change offered on its own, an act of its own. A revert offers all its changes at once,
        its hand-backs and ranges ahead of its values, so they stand together here. What
        `_apply_staged` gives change ids by, and `_after_service_run` says a dropped revert by."""
        offered: list = []
        waiting = list(self._pending)
        for at, row in enumerate(self._staged):
            offered += [(pending, pending.act) for pending in waiting if pending.after <= at]
            waiting = [pending for pending in waiting if pending.after > at]
            offered.append((row, self._acts.get(at)))
        return offered + [(pending, pending.act) for pending in waiting]
```

```python
    def _revert(self, command, index: int) -> None:
        """**A person takes the run back to an earlier moment** (`link.Revert`; engine build C3's
        spec §8; the PI, 2026-10-07, TSK-43, "Yes, with revert": "any earlier state restored in
        one action, itself recorded"), offered between trials or while paused and applied at the
        next boundary as one act (`_apply_staged`): one change id for all its rows, of kind
        `revert`, each naming the moment. `command.change` names it: 0, the run's start, or a
        change id of the run in progress, which goes back to the latest moment kept at or before
        it (`_moments`), so a clear's or a switch's goes back to what was in force then (the C3
        plan's call 24). It goes back from what the run will hold once all offered ahead of it
        applies (`_ahead`), so that it reaches the moment exactly:
        - each setting a person held then, at another value now or not held now, is set to its
          value then **through `set`, unchanged** (the C3 spec's welfare item 3), and held again;
        - each setting held now and not then is handed back to what gives it in the open block
          (`_to`), as the *hand back* button does;
        - each draw changed live then or since goes back to its range then, or to the one the
          task declares, as a live range is put in force.

        **Never a bounded setting**: a reward size is no task setting a person holds and no draw,
        so no moment holds one, and a revert neither sets nor hands back one (engine spec §17.6).
        Counts and training aids are not reverted. `index`, the trial about to run, is every
        branch's.

        **Refused whole, with the sentence, none of it applying**: a `change` that is no whole
        number from 0 (the wire's rule again, as `_clear` meets its own); one made before the run
        started; one not made yet; a moment the run already holds, leaving nothing to revert; a
        revert that would leave trials no animal can get right (`_possible`, judging all of it at
        once, before any value is set, so a revert refused for it writes no warning); and one any
        of whose values `set` refuses. What it staged and offered is cut back to what was there
        before it (`_staged`, `_pending`; `_acts` is written only once all of it is accepted), and
        no change row is written. A warning `set` accepted (`_beyond_range`) for one of its values
        ahead of the refused one stays accepted, by that function's rule. **Its hand-backs and
        ranges are offered ahead of its values**, which are set in the order of their names, so
        `set` judges each value over the settings handed back and the ranges put back, not over
        what the revert is about to undo.

        **It never raises** (the C3 plan's call 20; its review, I-1): it runs beside the pause,
        outside `_command`'s listed `try`, so a check that raises refuses the revert, saying it
        could not be checked, and the session runs on. Its hand-backs and ranges do not pass
        through `set`, as the buttons' do not (the C3 plan's Appendix A, item 5, put to the PI
        with the plan): a hand-back puts back the run's own value, and a range puts back one in
        force before, accepted when it was offered, or the declared one. Run between trials, never
        in a frame. Not welfare-critical: the branch handing to it is `_command`'s."""
        change = command.change
        if isinstance(change, bool) or not isinstance(change, int) or change < 0:
            self._refuse(command.KIND, command.by, (
                f"a 'revert' command's change is a whole number from 0, and {change!r} is not "
                f"one, so it is refused"))
            return
        where = _back_to(change)
        staged, pending = len(self._staged), len(self._pending)
        try:
            if 0 < change <= self._change_at_start:
                raise Exceeded(
                    f"change {change} was made before run {self.run_index + 1} started, and a "
                    f"revert goes back within the run in progress, to one of its changes or to "
                    f"its start (0)")
            if change > self._change:
                raise Exceeded(f"no change {change} has been made yet")
            then = next(moment for moment in reversed(self._moments) if moment.change <= change)
            values, held, ranges = self._ahead()
            restored = {name: value for name, value in then.held.items()
                        if name not in held or values.get(name) != value}
            handed = sorted(held - then.held.keys())
            drawn = {key: then.ranges.get(key) for key in sorted({*ranges, *then.ranges})
                     if ranges.get(key) != then.ranges.get(key)}
            if not (restored or handed or drawn):
                raise Exceeded(
                    "the run holds now what it held then, so there is nothing to revert")
            why = self._possible(restored, handed=frozenset(handed), ranges=drawn)
            if why is not None:
                raise Exceeded(why)
            self._act += 1
            act = self._act
            for name in handed:
                to = self._to(name)
                self._pending.append(Pending(
                    "hand_back", name, was=values.get(name),
                    now=self._run_values.get(name) if to == "run" else None, by=command.by,
                    after=staged, to=to, act=act,
                ))
            for key, draw in drawn.items():
                declared, before = self._declared.get(key[-1]), ranges.get(key)
                self._pending.append(Pending(
                    "range", key[-1], by=command.by, after=staged, key=key, draw=draw, act=act,
                    was=variation.recorded(
                        self._declared_draw(key) if before is None else before, declared),
                    now=variation.recorded(
                        self._declared_draw(key) if draw is None else draw, declared),
                ))
            for name in sorted(restored):
                self.set(name, restored[name], by=command.by)
            self._acts.update(dict.fromkeys(range(staged, len(self._staged)), act))
            self._act_moments[act] = change
        except Exceeded as refused:
            del self._staged[staged:]
            del self._pending[pending:]
            self._refuse(command.KIND, command.by,
                         f"the revert to {where} is refused, and none of it applies: {refused}")
        except Exception as broken:  # noqa: BLE001 -- see the docstring
            del self._staged[staged:]
            del self._pending[pending:]
            self._refuse(command.KIND, command.by, (
                f"the revert to {where} could not be checked ({type(broken).__name__}: "
                f"{broken}), so it is refused, none of it applies, and the session runs on"))
```

```python
    def _keep_moment(self, said: str) -> None:
        """**A moment a revert can go back to, kept as an act applies** (`Moment`; engine build C3's
        spec §8; `_apply_staged`): the act's change id, now, `said`, and what the live layer holds
        once it applied -- each setting a person holds, with its value (`_edited`), and each draw
        changed live (`_ranges`, its change id left out) -- each in sorted order, so a revert's
        rows come out in one order in every process. Between trials, never in a frame."""
        self._moments.append(Moment(
            self._change, self.wall_now(), said,
            {name: self.spec.values.get(name) for name in sorted(self._edited)},
            {key: self._ranges[key][0] for key in sorted(self._ranges)},
        ))
```

`docs/references/decisions.md`: insert

```markdown
### TSK-70 — Revert restores any earlier moment of the run the change log names in one recorded action, task settings and drawn ranges only, never a bounded setting; each value goes through `Session.set` and the revert is refused whole if any value is
- **Decided:** 2026-10-07, the PI ("Yes, with revert"; TSK-43), built by engine build C3; and 2026-10-30, the PI, "Approve all four" on the welfare items for the design (item 3: revert on the welfare summary, engine spec §20 item 3). Engineering (the C3 spec §8; the engine C3 plan's calls 19 and 24): a revert goes back to a change of the run in progress, or to its start, never to an earlier run's; each task setting is restored to its value then, held or handed back as it was then, and each drawn range as it was, from what the run will hold once every change offered ahead of it applies; a clear's or a switch's change goes back to what was in force then; counts and training aids are not reverted; presets are build C5's; the change gets one `change` id for the whole revert, each of its rows naming the moment it goes back to; its hand-backs and ranges are offered ahead of its values, so each value is judged over what the revert restores; and a revert that would leave trials no animal can get right (TSK-69), or that changes nothing, is refused.
- **Where:** [the C3 spec §8](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#8-the-change-log-and-revert) and [§14](../superpowers/specs/2026-10-30-engine-c3-design.md#14-welfare-items); [`wl_xcon/link.py`](../../wl_xcon/link.py) (`Revert`); [`wl_xcon/taskd.py`](../../wl_xcon/taskd.py) (`Session._command`, welfare-listed: a branch beside the pause, handing to `Session._revert`, off the list; the moments it goes back to, `Session._moments`, kept by `Session._apply_staged`, which applies it as one act; `Session.set` unchanged); TSK-43, TSK-67, TSK-68, TSK-69.
- **Basis:** PI decision; an operational and welfare choice with no published basis. A bounded setting such as a reward size never reverts (engine spec §17.6; the PI's b3a rule that a reward size changed in a run lasts only for that session): a reward size is no task setting a person holds and no draw, so no moment holds one, and a revert cannot reach a reward. A revert's hand-backs and ranges go as the buttons' do, not through `Session.set` (TSK-67, TSK-68); put to the PI with the plan as an amendment to the C3 spec's welfare item 3 (the engine C3 plan's Appendix A, item 5).

```

### Task 15: Eased trials kept out of moving up

The C3 spec §7; the PI: with the C2b merge, Q8, "Merge; fix eased trials in C3" ("eased trials do not count toward moving up, and do count toward moving back"), and in C3's brainstorm, on a change to an expected setting, "No, after any change (Recommended)" ("trials after any change to an expected setting do not count toward moving up (matches Q13, TRN-06)"); Calls 13 and 18; the outline review's I-7 and M-19; the controller's rulings on Task 4 (`variation.easier` takes `choices=bool(param.choices)`) and Task 6 (`Counts.eased_paid`; the sequence-balanced stage, put to the PI with I-7's item). Task 6 taught `Scheduler.record` an `eased` flag: an eased trial is left out of the window a block's criterion and a stage's rule read, is still judged toward the fall-back and counted toward its condition, and in a training progression (`ByCriterion`) is left out of its stage's number of trials and its targets (`Counts.eased`, `eased_paid`; review I-7; Appendix B item 10). Task 10 gave each trial line its `eased`, written `[]`. Nothing passed `eased=True` until this task, which decides which trials are eased and hands the verdict on, all of it off the welfare list:
- **`Session._eased(condition, values, drawn, number)`**, judged between trials, once the trial's values are built and before it runs, never in a frame.
  - **What a live change reaches** (the spec: "a person's value or a live range"): each setting a person holds (`_edited`), and each drawn from a range changed live (`drawn`, `_draw`'s sources, naming a change id).
  - **What the trial would otherwise have had** (Call 18). Where a draw gives the setting in the open block (the block's own, the task's, or the condition's own range): the value the seed draws for the trial from the range as written (`variation.draw` on the declaration, never on `_ranges`), on a `SAME` setting's repeat for the trial whose key drew it (`_kept`'s `original`, Call 13), else for this one. Else the condition's value. Else the run's own (`_run_values`).
  - **How it reads** (the setting's resolved meaning, TRN-03). An expected setting keeps the trial out at any value but that one, either way (the PI, "No, after any change"). A clear-cut one does where `variation.easier` says easier, **or cannot say** (relative to the trial's background, or against no value: never moved up on doubt, Appendix B item 2); a choice is read by its `raising` (`choices=bool(param.choices)`, review M-19). One declared not a difficulty setting never does.
- **The loop** calls `scheduler.record(condition.name, result.outcome, shown=shown, eased=bool(eased))` and passes `eased=eased` to `record.trial`.
- **A training stage ending by its trials or targets** (review I-7; Appendix B item 10, built as recommended, for the PI to confirm): Task 6's `Counts.eased` and `eased_paid` keep eased trials out of both; `test_a_training_stage_is_not_passed_on_eased_trials_by_its_trials_or_targets` proves it through `Session.run`.
- **A trial whose paying try was eased is eased** (the controller's ruling on this task, 2026-10-30: "A trial counts as eased for a stage's trial count if the try that paid it was eased, not only if its first try was. A drummed trial whose paying retry came after a person's easing change was made easier, and it must not move the animal up."). This task owns what "eased" means, so it changes Task 6's counting in `scheduler.py`, keeping `Counts.eased` and `eased_paid`. **Exactly what changed:** `Counts.eased` counted a trial in a training progression when its first try was eased (`counts.eased += kept and first_try`); it now also counts it, once, when its first try was not eased and the try that pays it (an answer counted or a trial spent, a drum's try among them) was. A new field, `Scheduler._eased_chain`, says whether the trial in flight is already counted, set by each first try. `block_trials` (`trials - eased`) therefore leaves such a trial out of the stage's number of trials. `eased_paid` (each eased try that paid, the targets' term), the window a block's criterion reads (each eased try left out) and the fall-back are unchanged. `test_a_drummed_trial_whose_paying_try_was_eased_does_not_count_toward_a_stages_trials` pins it through `Session.run`: a stage of target 0 ending on its two trials, its drummed first trial uneased on its first try and eased on the try that pays it.

**Engineering calls made here** (each in the report):
- **A held drawn setting's counterfactual is drawn by `_eased` itself.** A person's hold skips the draw (`_draw`), so nothing drew the seed's value for that trial. `_eased` draws it on the declaration's key: on a `SAME` repeat for the trial it repeats (that trial's `_kept` entry, found through `Scheduler.drawn.repeat_of`), else for this trial. Where that trial drew the value from the declaration, the value it drew is taken as it is (exact for a prepared list, whose place cannot be drawn again). Otherwise a prepared list is read at the place its next fresh draw takes (`_listed`, not advanced while held), which the trial after a hand-back then draws.
- **A meaning relative to another setting reads that setting as the trial has it**, for the trial's value and the otherwise alike. Each changed setting is judged on its own; a change to the reference is judged as its own setting.
- **A name that is no setting of the run's task keeps nothing out.** `_edited` can hold one: a value staged before the run is validated against the task the session last named and applies at the run's first boundary, whatever task the run plays (C2b). Nothing of the trial reads it, so it is skipped, never looked up (which would raise between trials).
- **`NOT_DIFFICULTY` has no branch of its own.** `variation.easier` returns `False` for it before reading anything, and only an expected setting is read otherwise; a branch would be a line no test could fail.
- **A drum's try and a repeat are judged as any trial is**, each on its own values.
- **Where it is called:** after `values` is built and before a drawn direction is spelled from 0 to 360 for `params`, so it reads values in the task's own terms, as `_draw` and the counterfactual draw them.
- **`Scheduler.drawn.repeat_of` is read inside `_eased`**, so the outline's signature `(condition, values, drawn, number)` stands.
- **A range changed live is judged as a whole, by the range that drew the value** (revision round 2; the PI, 2026-10-31, Appendix B item 18, "Judge the range as a whole (Recommended)"; Call 45). `Session._range_eases` reads Task 13's `variation.easier_range` against the declaration: every trial drawn from a range that counts as easier, or whose way cannot be read, is kept out, an expected setting's whenever its range differs from the one written; the range is the one named by the line's `drawn`, in force now or kept with its change's moment (`_moments`, Task 14), so a `same` repeat of a trial drawn from a range since put back is still judged by it. The trial-by-trial comparison of a range is gone; a person's value is judged as before, against the range as written.
